items.body:
Asda has today published its latest Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Report, revealing it has exceeded its operational carbon reduction target, surpassed £100 million raised through Tickled Pink and continued to improve the nutritional profile of products sold to customers.
The report highlights progress across Asda’s five ESG priorities: Healthy and Sustainable Choices, Net Zero Carbon, Nature, Zero Waste and Responsible Business Fundamentals.
Key achievements in 2025 include:
- Exceeded Asda’s target to reduce operational carbon emissions by 50%, achieving a 55% reduction since 2015
- Surpassed £100 million raised through Tickled Pink during the reporting period, with the total now at £110 million as the campaign celebrates its 30th anniversary this year.
- Increased global fresh produce sourced from farms with Biodiversity Improvement Plans from 25% to 80%
- Improved the nutritional profile of products sold for the second consecutive year, with Asda’s sales-weighted health score improving from 1.77 to 1.50
- Increased the proportion of operational waste reused, recycled or redistributed to 89.2%, while maintaining zero waste to landfill. 
An Asda spokesperson said: “This year’s report highlights strong progress in areas where we can have the greatest impact. We’ve exceeded our operational carbon reduction target and continued to improve the nutritional profile of products sold.
“We’re also proud to have surpassed £100 million raised through Tickled Pink during the reporting period, with the total now reaching £110 million as we celebrate the campaign’s 30th anniversary this year. While there’s more to do, we’re committed to building on this progress and focusing on the issues that matter most to our business and stakeholders.”
Further highlights from the year include:
Net Zero Carbon
- Cut emissions from transport fleet by 18% year-on-year, supported by the continued transition from diesel to LNG and Bio-LNG fuels.
Nature
- Achieved 80% LEAF Marque certification across global fresh produce growers in more than 40 countries, building on the achievement of 100% certification across UK growers in 2024.
- Reduced operational water consumption to 2.2 million m³, down from 2.6 million m³ in 2024.
- Supported biodiversity and habitat restoration projects across more than 8,500 acres of farmland through the Asda Lamb Group Habitat Project.
Healthy and Sustainable Choices
- Reformulated the malted bread used across its Food To Go range, adding an estimated 21 tonnes of fibre to customers’ diets each year.
- Maintained 97.5% recyclability across own-brand packaging. 
Zero Waste
- Increased recycled content across own-brand plastic packaging from 21.6% to 32.7%, exceeding its target of 30%.
- Redistributed 3,852 tonnes of surplus food through community partners, supporting local communities.
Responsible Business Fundamentals
- Invested £80 million in retail pay for more than 115,000 retail and convenience colleagues, while enhancing family-friendly policies and increasing the colleague discount from 10% to 15%.
- Through the Asda Foundation, awarded more than £3.2 million to 2,326 community groups across the UK.
- Raised £3.1 million for BBC Children in Need during the charity partnership’s 25th anniversary year.

items.body:
GXO Logistics, Inc. (NYSE: GXO), the world’s largest pure-play contract logistics provider, today announced a new nine-year contract renewal with ASOS, one of the leading global online fashion destinations, extending a successful partnership that began in 2013.
Over the past 13 years, GXO has worked closely with ASOS to support the retailer’s evolving business needs through a combination of operational expertise, service excellence, continuous improvement and technology-enabled innovation at its highly automated logistics hub in Barnsley. Throughout the partnership, GXO has helped optimise one of the UK’s most advanced e-commerce fulfilment operations, supporting ASOS as customer expectations and market demands have evolved.
The renewed agreement, which covers warehouse fulfilment and transportation services, showcases GXO’s ability to deliver innovation over the long-term and to provide high levels of service to over 16 million ASOS customers every year.
“Our partnership with ASOS is built on a shared commitment to delivering outstanding service and value,” said Russell Atkinson, managing director of fashion, GXO UK&I. “For more than a decade we’ve worked together to support millions of customer orders through a highly efficient, resilient and increasingly technology-enabled operation. Over the course of our partnership, we’ve been on a continuous improvement journey, helping to evolve one of the UK’s most advanced e-commerce fulfilment operations. By combining the expertise of our colleagues with technology and automation, we’ve continued to adapt to changing customer expectations and support ASOS’ growth. This renewal is a testament to the strength of our relationship and the dedication of our teams, and we’re excited to continue building on that success over the next nine years.”
The partnership has evolved alongside the rapidly changing e-commerce market, with GXO supporting ASOS to meet evolving customer expectations through continuous operational and technology improvements, while maintaining a strong and consistent operation. Over the last 5 years, GXO has introduced new ways of working that enabled ASOS to extend customer order cut-off times to 11pm, giving shoppers even more time to place their orders and greater flexibility over when they shop.
The renewed partnership will see GXO continue to support ASOS in delivering the fast, reliable service its customers expect. Together, GXO and ASOS will continue to explore new ways to enhance the shopping experience, helping customers receive the convenience, choice and dependable service they value.
Jonny O’Hara, logistics director ASOS said: “Our ambition at ASOS is to be The Stylist for our customers, bringing the latest trends and exciting brands through curated, personalised experiences that help customers put together outfits with confidence. Delivering that experience relies on strong, flexible and reliable operations, and GXO, as leaders in the industry, have been a trusted partner for more than 13 years. As we extend our partnership for the years ahead, this renewal will support our growth while helping us continue to deliver the excellent service our customers expect.”

items.title: Where online retailers should look before the holiday rush
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. For most online retailers, the final three months of the year decide whether the annual numbers hold up. Black Friday, Cyber Monday and the run-up to Christmas compress weeks of demand into a handful of days, and the weak points in an operation tend to show up at exactly the moment they are hardest to […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
For most online retailers, the final three months of the year decide whether the annual numbers hold up. Black Friday, Cyber Monday and the run-up to Christmas compress weeks of demand into a handful of days, and the weak points in an operation tend to show up at exactly the moment they are hardest to fix. Marketing plans for the season are usually locked in by now. The fulfilment side deserves the same attention, because a campaign that works is only good news if the orders it generates actually leave the building on time.
Start with the bottleneck, not the headline volume
It is tempting to plan peak around a single forecast figure. In practice, the constraint is rarely total volume. It is whichever step in the chain runs out of capacity first: goods-in, putaway, picking, packing, carrier collection or customer service. A warehouse that copes comfortably with double its normal order count can still stall if inbound stock arrives late and sits unprocessed on the dock, or if packing stations run out of the right box sizes.
A useful exercise is to walk an order through every stage and ask, for each one, what happens at two and three times a normal day. Who does the work, how long does it take, and what is the fallback if a person, a machine or a supplier lets you down? The answers often point to modest fixes, such as pre-built packaging, extra scanners or an earlier stock delivery date, rather than expensive overhauls.
Cut-off times are a customer promise
Shoppers in the last fortnight before Christmas pay close attention to delivery promises. The order cut-off time on a product page is effectively a commitment, and missing it costs more than a single sale: it generates contact centre volume, refund requests and, sometimes, a public review that lingers well into the new year.
Retailers who keep fulfilment in-house should check whether their stated cut-off is realistic on the busiest days, not just on an average Tuesday in September. Those who work with a partner for e-commerce fulfilment should confirm the agreed cut-off, carrier collection times and any peak surcharges in writing, well before November. It is also worth agreeing in advance how stock allocation will work if a product sells out faster than expected across several channels at once.
Plan for January returns now
Peak does not end on Christmas Eve. Gifts that do not fit, duplicates and impulse purchases flow back in January, often at the same time as the sales period begins. Returns that sit unprocessed are stock that cannot be resold, which matters most for seasonal or fashion lines that lose value quickly.
Setting clear return windows, preparing a simple grading process (resell, refurbish, write off) and reserving space and staff for returns are small decisions that make the post-Christmas weeks far calmer. Communicating the returns policy clearly at checkout also reduces the number of customers who chase refunds by email.
Keep channels and stock data in sync
Many retailers now sell through their own site, one or more marketplaces and sometimes physical stores. During peak, the risk of overselling grows with every channel, because stock levels change faster than manual updates can keep up. Integrations between the shop platform, marketplaces and the warehouse management system should be tested under realistic load, not just switched on. A short test with a batch of dummy orders can reveal sync delays before real customers find them.
Logistics providers such as Monta connect webshops and marketplaces to warehouse software so that orders and stock levels flow between systems automatically. Whatever set-up a retailer uses, the principle is the same: one reliable source of stock truth, updated as close to real time as possible.
Debrief while it is still fresh
The most valuable peak planning document is the one written in early January, while the problems of the previous weeks are still vivid. Which days went wrong, which products caused the most handling issues, which carriers struggled, and where did customers complain? Writing this down, with dates and specifics, turns one difficult season into a better brief for the next.
Peak trading will always involve some pressure. Retailers who treat fulfilment as part of their commercial plan, rather than something that simply happens after the sale, give themselves the best chance of finishing the year with satisfied customers and a clean stock position.

items.title: Operation Machinize success reported with rogue stores targeted in Hertfordshire and Surrey
items.summary: Hertfordshire’s Constabulary and County Council took part in Operation Machinize, a national initiative targeting organised criminal gangs. Dozens of officers from the constabulary’s Operational Support Group, Neighbourhood Policing Teams, Hertfordshire County Council’s Trading Standards and government immigration officers visited retailers and business premises around the… This story continues at Operation Machinize success reported with rogue stores targeted in Hertfordshire and Surrey Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Dozens of officers from the constabulary’s Operational Support Group, Neighbourhood Policing Teams, Hertfordshire County Council’s Trading Standards and government immigration officers visited retailers and business premises around the county.
The visits were carried out to ensure the businesses were operating in accordance with the law.
Twenty-four premises in Borehamwood, Hemel Hempstead, Hatfield, Hoddesdon, Watford and St Albans were visited during October, with more than 15 kilograms of illicit tobacco products and 524 illegal vapes, worth more than £13,000 in total being seized.
Councillor Ajanta Hilton, executive member for public health and community safety at Hertfordshire County Council said: “Criminals often seek to hide the proceeds of crime through seemingly legitimate businesses, which is why operations like this are so important.
“By working with the National Crime Agency, the police and partner organisations, we are helping to crack down on criminal activity, remove illicit products from sale and protect local communities from harm.
“Our Trading Standards team can offer practical advice and support to any trader who needs help understanding their legal obligations.”
Chief Inspector Stuart Bence, from Hertfordshire Constabulary’s Crime and Intel team, said: “We have worked with our partners in Trading Standards to ensure high street businesses are not involved in criminal activities, such as selling counterfeit products, drug dealing, handling stolen goods and exploiting workers.
“This activity funds organised crime and violence, distributing harmful products and posing a risk to the young and vulnerable.”
The Hertfordshire activity follows Operation Machinize raids in Surrey last month, with Trading Standards officers seizing a range of products.
Locations targeted included Elmbridge, Epsom, Guildford, Reigate, Spelthorne, Surrey Heath and Woking.
The range of products seized included illicit cigarette sticks, HRT, niche tobacco, vapes, liquids and counterfeit goods. The total value of seized goods amounted to £55,500.
Agencies involved alongside Trading Standards included Surrey Fire and Rescue Service, Surrey Police and Home Office Immigration Enforcement.
Kevin Deanus, Surrey County Council cabinet member for fire and rescue, and resilience, said: “We are here to protect our residents from harm, and we take that responsibility incredibly seriously.
“The success of Operation Machinize is testament to the fact that we will not tolerate illegal activities on our streets and will always protect our residents from any potentially unsafe goods.
“Not only that, we also have a duty to protect both legitimate businesses on our high streets and their vital contribution to the local economy.
“As always, I’d like to thank the Trading Standards team involved with this operation for their invaluable work in keeping residents safe.”
Following the raids, the first secretary of state Louise Haigh told the BBC shops involved in offences such as money laundering, illegal working and organised crime a “blight on our high street”.
“Because it’s been ignored, that kind of crime has been allowed to thrive and take root in our communities,” Haigh said, adding that a “serious priority” of prime minister Andy Burnham was to crackdown on these illicit businesses and put pride back in local places.

items.title: Police launch £2.5m pilot targeting prolific shoplifters across 16 forces
items.summary: Police forces across England and Wales are set to take part in a new £2.5m pilot scheme targeting some of the country’s most prolific retail offenders, as part of a wider crackdown on shoplifting and organised retail crime. The initiative, announced by the Home Secretary today, during Safer Business Action Week, will see up to...
items.body:
Police forces across England and Wales are set to take part in a new £2.5m pilot scheme targeting some of the country’s most prolific retail offenders, as part of a wider crackdown on shoplifting and organised retail crime.
The initiative, announced by the Home Secretary today, during Safer Business Action Week, will see up to 16 police forces work with local partners to tackle repeat offending and address the underlying causes of retail crime.
Under the Prolific Retail Offender Pilot, each participating force will identify around 30 of its most prolific offenders and introduce more intensive measures aimed at preventing further offences.
The Home Office has proposed £2.5m in funding for the programme, with activity expected to begin in phases in early 2027 ahead of a full 12-month rollout from spring.
The scheme follows figures showing that just nine per cent of offenders are responsible for more than half of all retail crime convictions.
It comes as police-recorded shop theft fell four per cent in the year ending March 2026, following increased collaboration between police, retailers and the security industry.
National Police Chiefs’ Council retail crime lead ACC Alex Goss welcomed the announcement, highlighting the importance of tackling repeat offenders who continue to cause significant harm to businesses and retail workers.
“We welcome the Home Secretary’s announcement today, which provides policing and partners with additional support to tackle some of the most prolific retail crime offenders who continue to cause harm to businesses, retail workers and local communities,” he said.
“The programme aims to develop and test a more intensive, multi-agency approach to a small cohort of prolific offenders to reduce repeat offending, improve outcomes for retailers and communities, and provide an evidence base for future national policy.”
The pilot will involve forces including the Metropolitan Police, Greater Manchester Police, West Midlands Police, Merseyside Police and West Yorkshire Police.
Meanwhile, policing’s national intelligence unit for serious organised acquisitive crime, Opal, has reported further progress in its efforts to disrupt organised retail crime gangs operating across police force boundaries.
Since launching its dedicated organised retail crime capability in May 2024, the unit has supported 103 criminal investigations, resulting in 287 arrests and 221 court outcomes, including custodial sentences totalling more than 129 years.
The unit has also identified 750 offenders linked to more than 10,000 offences, responsible for an estimated £9.7m in losses to retailers.
In the six months to November, Opal received 69 referrals from police forces and retailers, leading to 19 operations being adopted and 30 arrests.
Police said offending among organised crime groups identified and monitored by Opal had fallen by 73%, highlighting the impact of coordinated intelligence-led operations.
Opal head Chief Superintendent Owain Llewellyn said the unit played a crucial role in identifying offenders targeting multiple retailers and operating across county borders.
“The work of Opal is crucial in providing support to police forces and coordinating working with retailers to tackle those offenders who are operating across county borders and causing the most harm,” he said.
The new pilot builds on the Retail Crime Action Plan introduced three years ago, which has sought to improve information sharing, strengthen relationships between police and retailers, and increase enforcement against shoplifting and violence towards retail workers.

items.title: New Asda boss orders stores to open more staffed checkouts
items.summary: David Potts told the supermarket's 1,100 store managers to spend more time on the shop floor helping staff and checking stores are ready for customers.
items.body:
New Asda boss orders stores to open more staffed checkouts
The new boss of Asda has ordered stores to open more staffed checkouts as part of turnaround efforts at the supermarket.
David Potts, who was appointed chief executive this month, told the supermarket's 1,100 store managers to spend more time on the shop floor helping staff and checking stores are ready for customers.
Speaking at Asda's Pudsey store in West Yorkshire yesterday, Potts said: 'We're making it harder than it should be for customers to get what they want, move around the store and pay for their shopping.
'We need to change that, starting now, which is why I've instructed all our general store managers to open more full-service checkouts, spend more time on the shop floor and get more product on shelves and well-presented throughout the day.'
Asda's new boss David Potts has asked staff to open more staffed checkouts
The retail veteran instructed staffed checkouts open more often to help those doing bigger shops.
They must be available from at least 8am, alongside self-service and Scan and Go tills.
Asda has around 3,400 staffed tills, compared with 8,100 self-scan and 2,000 Scan and Go checkouts across 611 of its larger stores.
Potts told Asda staff yesterday: 'More than anything Asda shoppers want great value which is why the business has invested to get back on the pitch when it comes to low prices.
'But visiting stores as a customer over the last few weeks has shown me we aren't as focused on the rest of the shopping trip as we need to be.'
He added: 'The shopping trip is everything and by making Asda easier to shop so customers can find what they came for and get through the checkouts easily, they'll come back and shop more with us.'
After a long search for a new boss, Asda last week said Potts had joined the ailing supermarket with immediate effect.
For the past two years, the business has been run by retail veteran and former Asda boss Allan Leighton, who now holds a non-executive chairman role.
Potts faces the task of turning Asda around after a long period of falling sales since private equity firm TDR Capital helped finance a debt-fuelled £6.8billion takeover by the billionaire Issa brothers in 2021.
The supermarket swung back to quarterly sales growth for the first time in more than two years in September, but continues to lose out to discounters Lidl and Aldi.
It has also grappled with debt pressures and severe disruption linked to an IT upgrade.
Analysts welcomed the appointment of Potts, regarded as one of the finest retailers of his generation.
He began his career at Tesco on the shop floor aged 16, after failing his O-Levels. He worked his way up to run its Ireland, UK and Asia businesses.
He then led Morrisons from 2015 to 2023, a period which included the group's £10billion sale to private equity group Clayton Dubilier & Rice in 2021.

items.title: Boots set to rival Currys for Black Friday searches as beauty gains ground
items.summary: Boots is on track to become one of the UK’s most searched-for retailers this Black Friday. Searches for Boots are forecast to jump 17 per cent year on year to 1.78 million during Black Friday week, putting it alongside Currys in joint fourth place, according to new data from MediaVision. It’s a shift in the...
items.body:
Boots is on track to become one of the UK’s most searched-for retailers this Black Friday.
Searches for Boots are forecast to jump 17 per cent year on year to 1.78 million during Black Friday week, putting it alongside Currys in joint fourth place, according to new data from MediaVision.
It’s a shift in the traditional Black Friday pecking order, which has long been dominated by electronics retailers and big-ticket purchases.
Amazon is still expected to comfortably hold the top spot with 7.19 million searches, although that represents a one per cent decline on last year.
Argos is forecast to remain second with 2.83 million searches, down two per cent, while Currys is also expected to see interest slip two per cent.
Next, meanwhile, is gaining ground, with searches predicted to climb 10 per cent to 1.9 million, making it the only other retailer in the top five expected to achieve double-digit growth.
The findings, based on four years of consumer search behaviour analysed through MediaVision’s Metis platform, suggest shoppers are broadening their focus beyond the traditional Black Friday heavyweights.
MediaVision chief executive Louis Venter said: “Black Friday has traditionally been dominated by retailers offering big-ticket discounts, particularly in technology and electronics. But consumer interest is no longer concentrated in those categories alone.
“Brands that have built strong relationships with shoppers throughout the year are in a good position to capitalise when the sales period arrives.”
Beauty brands face mixed fortunes
Beauty is expected to see the biggest seasonal boost in search interest of any retail category this Black Friday, with demand forecast to reach 1.6 times the level of a typical week.
However, not every retailer is set to benefit.
Boots is expected to attract more than three times as many searches as its nearest beauty rival Superdrug, which is forecast to grow seven per cent to 527,000 searches.
Sephora is also expected to perform well, with searches rising eight per cent, while Rituals is tipped for an 18 per cent jump.
The picture is less encouraging for Charlotte Tilbury, where searches are predicted to fall 14 per cent, while Cult Beauty and The Perfume Shop face declines of nine per cent and eight per cent respectively.
Sol de Janeiro, which enjoyed a surge in popularity last year, could see search demand plunge 45 per cent.
MediaVision senior manager Molly Goffin said beauty’s reliance on social media trends and new product launches could make it difficult for brands to maintain momentum.
“Black Friday gives brands opportunity to convert existing interest into sales, but discounts alone won’t necessarily bring shoppers back year after year,” she said.
“The brands best positioned to succeed are those giving customers reasons to engage beyond promotional periods, whether that’s through products people genuinely want, cultural relevance or strong sense of brand identity.”
As reported earlier this month, separate research from Omnisend found that UK shoppers are expected to spend 32 per cent less across Black Friday and Cyber Monday this year, despite more consumers planning to take part.
Meanwhile, latest BRC figures show shoppers held back on big-ticket purchases in October as they waited for November discounts.
MediaVision’s forecasts are based on UK Google search demand for 1,006 retail brands and 471 products, drawing on Black Friday search trends between 2022 and 2025 alongside more recent consumer interest.
While the figures measure search demand rather than actual sales, they offer an early indication of which retailers are capturing shoppers’ attention ahead of Black Friday on 27 November.

items.title: Sales of bottled water and tinned food surge after government stockpiling advice
items.summary: UK supermarkets have seen a sharp rise in sales of bottled water, tinned food and other essentials after the government’s ‘Be Ready’ campaign urged households to prepare for emergencies. Sales…
items.body:
Sales of bottled water and tinned food surge after government stockpiling advice
UK supermarkets have seen a sharp rise in sales of bottled water, tinned food and other essentials after the government’s ‘Be Ready’ campaign urged households to prepare for emergencies.
Sales of hand sanitiser jumped 83 per cent, bottled water rose 67 per cent and tinned and jarred goods increased 37 per cent in the 10 days following the campaign’s launch on 22 October, according to new data from Worldpanel by Numerator.
The number of shoppers buying tinned meat rose 43 per cent, equivalent to an additional 400,000 customers a day, although the average quantity purchased remained at around 500g.
The data suggest shoppers are gradually building up emergency supplies rather than panic buying.
Worldpanel by Numerator head of retail and consumer insight Fraser McKevitt said shoppers had clearly responded to the government’s advice, but stressed that the increase in sales was not driven by panic buying.
He noted that fewer than a third of households bought bottled water during October, with consumers instead adding recommended products to their regular grocery shops.
The government’s Be Ready campaign encourages households to keep three days’ worth of essentials, including nine litres of water per person, non-perishable food, batteries, torches and first aid supplies, in case of disruption caused by extreme weather, cyberattacks or other emergencies.
Food manufacturer Princes has also reported increased demand for canned products, including fish, meat and vegetables, since the campaign launched.
Separate Barclays research found that 27 per cent of consumers were either stockpiling or considering building up emergency food and drink supplies.
The findings come as grocery inflation edged up to 2.6 per cent in the four weeks to 1 November, compared with 2.5 per cent the previous month.
Overall grocery sales rose 2.2 per cent year on year in October, according to Worldpanel.
As Retail Gazette reported earlier this week, IGD chief executive Sarah Bradbury suggested the government’s Be Ready campaign may have contributed to stronger food sales during October.
However, she warned that shoppers remained pessimistic about their finances as they headed into the crucial Christmas trading period.

items.title: Asda turnaround falters as market share slips to 11.3%
items.summary: Asda’s turnaround has suffered another setback after it emerged as the only major UK grocer to report falling sales in the latest market figures. It recorded £4bn in sales during…
items.body:
Asda turnaround falters as market share slips to 11.3%
Asda’s turnaround has suffered another setback after it emerged as the only major UK grocer to report falling sales in the latest market figures.
It recorded £4bn in sales during the 12 weeks to 1 November, down 0.5 per cent year on year, according to Worldpanel by Numerator data reported by City AM.
Its share of the grocery market also slipped from 11.6 per cent to 11.3 per cent over the period.
Asda’s rival supermarkets continue to attract shoppers, with Lidl reporting a 6.6 per cent increase in sales and Morrisons posting growth of two per cent.
Online grocer Ocado also recorded a 12.3 per cent jump in sales, taking its market share to a record 2.3 per cent.
The figures mark a setback for Asda, which had shown signs of recovery over the summer after reporting its first underlying sales growth in more than two years.
In August, the supermarket posted a 0.2 per cent increase in like-for-like sales excluding fuel during the seven weeks to 18 August, which then-executive chairman Allan Leighton described as a ‘major milestone’ in its turnaround.
However, the latest figures suggest that Asda is struggling to maintain that momentum as competition intensifies across the grocery sector.
The update comes just days after Asda appointed former Morrisons boss David Potts as its new group chief executive, with Leighton stepping back into a non-executive chairman role.
Potts has been tasked with accelerating the supermarket’s recovery under its Formula for Growth strategy, which focuses on improving prices, product availability and the overall customer experience.
As Retail Gazette previously reported, Asda’s turnaround has been complicated by falling sales, mounting financial pressures and the disruption caused by its £1bn-plus separation from Walmart’s legacy IT systems.
Asda has also been investing in technology to strengthen its position, including a partnership with Ocado to overhaul its online grocery operations from 2027.
However, with market share continuing to decline, the latest figures show the scale of the challenge facing Potts as he aims to restore growth and win back customers from Asda’s rivals.

items.title: Cadbury launches new online gifting shop with THG Ingenuity ahead of Christmas
items.summary: Cadbury has teamed up with THG Ingenuity to launch a new direct-to-consumer gifting platform ahead of Christmas. The new Cadbury Shop allows shoppers to create their own chocolate gifts, including…
items.body:
Cadbury launches new online gifting shop with THG Ingenuity ahead of Christmas
Cadbury has teamed up with THG Ingenuity to launch a new direct-to-consumer gifting platform ahead of Christmas.
The new Cadbury Shop allows shoppers to create their own chocolate gifts, including a Heroes Pick & Mix box where customers can choose their favourite miniature chocolates.
Shoppers can also build personalised letterbox gifts by selecting six Cadbury chocolate bars, which are packaged and delivered directly to the recipient.
The launch marks a fresh push into direct-to-consumer sales for Cadbury owner Mondelēz International, giving it greater control over how its products are sold and presented online.
Manchester-based THG Ingenuity has been brought in to run the platform, handling everything from the website and product personalisation to warehousing, deliveries and customer service.
Its THG Commerce division will power the online shop, while THG Studios will oversee creative content and digital merchandising.
THG Fulfil will manage the logistics operation, including temperature-controlled chocolate storage, picking and packing, and courier deliveries.
The partnership will allow Cadbury to expand its personalised gifting range while managing the additional demand expected during the busy festive trading period.
Cadbury marketing director Philip Warfield said: “Cadbury has always been about generosity and bringing people closer together.
“Appointing THG Ingenuity and launching the new Cadbury Shop gives us an exciting way to do exactly that ahead of Christmas — combining the chocolate the nation loves with beautifully personal gifting experiences, from the moment you choose it to the moment it’s opened.”
The new platform also gives Mondelēz a direct route to shoppers, separate from the independently operated Cadbury Gifts Direct business, which sells products under licence.
THG Ingenuity chief revenue officer Darren Rajanah said the partnership would give Cadbury the infrastructure to grow its personalised gifting business.
“Delivering exceptional direct-to-consumer experiences requires more than just a storefront; it demands an integrated operating environment where engaging creative content and intelligent digital technology connect seamlessly with automated fulfilment.”

items.title: Unilever’s $65bn McCormick merger faces competition probe over supermarket sauces
items.summary: Unilever’s planned $65bn merger of its food business with US spice giant McCormick has hit a regulatory hurdle after the UK’s competition watchdog warned the deal could leave supermarkets with…
items.body:
Unilever’s $65bn McCormick merger faces competition probe over supermarket sauces
Unilever’s planned $65bn merger of its food business with US spice giant McCormick has hit a regulatory hurdle after the UK’s competition watchdog warned the deal could leave supermarkets with fewer suppliers to choose from.
The Competition and Markets Authority has given the two businesses until 18 November to address its concerns or face an in-depth investigation that could delay the blockbuster deal.
The merger, announced in March, would bring Unilever’s food brands, including Hellmann’s, Knorr and Marmite, together with McCormick’s portfolio of Schwartz, French’s mustard and Frank’s RedHot.
However, the watchdog’s initial investigation found that combining the businesses could significantly reduce competition in the UK market for dry cooking mixes and sauces.
The CMA said the deal would bring together the two largest branded suppliers in both categories, leaving the combined business with a dominant position on supermarket shelves.
While rival brands such as Nestlé’s Maggi and Premier Foods’ Bisto, alongside supermarket own-label products, would continue to compete, the regulator found they provided only limited competitive pressure.
It also warned that limited supermarket shelf space and the established positions of major suppliers could make it difficult for new competitors to enter the market.
It’s a significant setback for Unilever, which has been reshaping its portfolio to focus on higher-growth beauty, personal care and household products.
As previously reported, the deal is expected to create one of the world’s largest food businesses, with annual revenues of around $20bn.
The transaction is currently expected to complete by mid-2027, subject to regulatory and shareholder approval.
Unilever has already moved to address potential competition issues, putting its historic Colman’s mustard brand up for sale in August.
However, the CMA said it had not identified competition concerns in the mustard market, finding that English, French and American-style mustards were sufficiently different products that shoppers did not generally consider them interchangeable.
Unilever said it was continuing discussions with potential buyers for Colman’s and was working constructively with the regulator. McCormick also confirmed it was cooperating with the watchdog.
The latest development comes just a week after Unilever unveiled plans to save €1bn by 2029 through a wider restructuring of its business.
The merger is a central part of that strategy, with Unilever looking to exit most of its food operations while retaining a stake in the enlarged McCormick business.
The CMA must now decide whether any remedies offered by the companies are sufficient to address its concerns.
If the regulator is not satisfied, the deal will be referred for a more detailed Phase 2 investigation, putting another hurdle in the way of one of the biggest transactions in the global food industry.

items.title: Bensons for Beds pumps £1m into reviving 131-year-old Staples & Co brand
items.summary: Bensons for Beds has invested more than £1m in bringing its historic Staples & Co brand back to life. The bed specialist has given the 131-year-old brand a makeover, introducing three new mattress collections that combine traditional British bedmaking techniques with contemporary designs and natural materials. The range, which launched on 1 November, is available...
items.body:
Bensons for Beds has invested more than £1m in bringing its historic Staples & Co brand back to life.
The bed specialist has given the 131-year-old brand a makeover, introducing three new mattress collections that combine traditional British bedmaking techniques with contemporary designs and natural materials.
The range, which launched on 1 November, is available in 55 Bensons stores and online, with prices starting at £1,399.99 for a double mattress and rising to £4,999 for its top-end Iconic collection.
The relaunch marks another step in Bensons’ efforts to move further into the premium end of the market, as it builds on its turnaround and looks to make more of its British manufacturing heritage.
Founded in 1895, Staples & Co has a long history in British bedmaking, including links to the former Staples Corner factory in north London.
Bensons is now hoping to give the name a new lease of life, using its factory in Huntingdon, Cambridgeshire, to produce mattresses featuring traditional techniques such as hand side-stitching and hand-tufting.
The new collections also use regeneratively farmed British wool sourced from around 50 to 60 farmers, who are paid a premium for their fleeces.
Bensons chief executive Nick Collard said: “Staples & Co represents something very important to the future of Bensons. We have a remarkable heritage in British bedmaking, and the opportunity now is to build on that with a brand that can stand confidently alongside the very best in the market.
“We believe customers are increasingly thoughtful about the things they bring into their homes. They’re looking for products that are beautifully made, that stand the test of time and have a story worth telling.”
He added: “Our ambition is to make Bensons a destination for exceptional sleep, with brands that customers actively seek out. Staples & Co is an important step towards that future.”
Bensons is hoping to build on the progress made under its turnaround strategy, which has seen it focus on improving its product ranges, expanding its store estate and strengthening its own-brand offering.
As Retail Gazette previously reported, the business returned to profitability in 2024 following a period of restructuring.
The Staples & Co relaunch is being backed by a marketing push, refreshed in-store displays and staff training aimed at helping shoppers navigate the new premium ranges.
Bensons owned brands director Emma Forbes said: “We wanted Staples & Co to feel as considered as a piece of furniture you would treasure for a lifetime. Not just somewhere to sleep, but something beautifully made that becomes part of your home.”
It is also looking to nurture the next generation of British furniture makers, sponsoring the Furniture Makers’ Company’s New Furniture Makers Exhibition and offering a £1,000 commission to an emerging designer to create a headboard.

items.title: Asos extends GXO logistics partnership until 2034 in major deal
items.summary: Asos has extended its long-standing partnership with GXO Logistics until 2034, securing a new agreement covering warehouse fulfilment and transportation services. The relationship between the two firms began in 2013, and now supports more than 16 million Asos customers each year. The deal will see GXO continue to operate Asos’s highly automated fulfilment hub in...
items.body:
Asos has extended its long-standing partnership with GXO Logistics until 2034, securing a new agreement covering warehouse fulfilment and transportation services.
The relationship between the two firms began in 2013, and now supports more than 16 million Asos customers each year.
The deal will see GXO continue to operate Asos’s highly automated fulfilment hub in Barnsley, which has undergone significant technology and operational improvements over the past 13 years.
The partnership has reportedly helped Asos streamline its fulfilment operations and extend customer order cut-off times to 11pm, giving shoppers greater flexibility when placing orders.
GXO UK and Ireland managing director of fashion Russell Atkinson said: “Our partnership with ASOS is built on a shared commitment to delivering outstanding service and value.”
He added: “By combining the expertise of our colleagues with technology and automation, we’ve continued to adapt to changing customer expectations and support ASOS’ growth.”
As Retail Gazette reported last week, the fashion retailer swung to a £24.4m pre-tax profit in its latest financial year, compared with a £281.6m loss the previous year, while returning to quarterly sales growth for the first time since 2022.
The business has been working to improve supply chain efficiencies and reduce costs, including through warehouse automation and changes to its fulfilment network.
Asos logistics director Jonny O’Hara said: “Delivering that experience relies on strong, flexible and reliable operations, and GXO, as leaders in the industry, have been a trusted partner for more than 13 years.”
He added: “As we extend our partnership for the years ahead, this renewal will support our growth while helping us continue to deliver the excellent service our customers expect.”
The renewed agreement will see both companies explore further operational improvements and technology investments to support faster, more reliable deliveries.
It follows Asos’s return to sales growth in September, when the retailer highlighted supply chain efficiencies and warehouse automation as key contributors to its recovery.

items.title: Asda turnaround falters as market share slips to 11.3%
items.summary: Asda’s turnaround has suffered another setback after it emerged as the only major UK grocer to report falling sales in the latest market figures. The retailer recorded £4bn in sales during the 12 weeks to 1 November, down 0.5 per cent year on year, according to Worldpanel by Numerator data reported by City AM. Its...
items.body:
Asda’s turnaround has suffered another setback after it emerged as the only major UK grocer to report falling sales in the latest market figures.
The retailer recorded £4bn in sales during the 12 weeks to 1 November, down 0.5 per cent year on year, according to Worldpanel by Numerator data reported by City AM.
Its share of the grocery market also slipped from 11.6 per cent to 11.3 per cent over the period.
Asda’s rival supermarkets continue to attract shoppers, with Lidl reporting a 6.6 per cent increase in sales and Morrisons posting growth of two per cent.
Online grocer Ocado also recorded a 12.3 per cent jump in sales, taking its market share to a record 2.3 per cent.
The figures mark a setback for Asda, which had shown signs of recovery over the summer after reporting its first underlying sales growth in more than two years.
In August, the supermarket posted a 0.2 per cent increase in like-for-like sales excluding fuel during the seven weeks to 18 August, which then-executive chairman Allan Leighton described as a ‘major milestone’ in its turnaround.
However, the latest figures suggest that Asda is struggling to maintain that momentum as competition intensifies across the grocery sector.
The update comes just days after Asda appointed former Morrisons boss David Potts as its new group chief executive, with Leighton stepping back into a non-executive chairman role.
Potts has been tasked with accelerating the supermarket’s recovery under its Formula for Growth strategy, which focuses on improving prices, product availability and the overall customer experience.
As Retail Gazette previously reported, Asda’s turnaround has been complicated by falling sales, mounting financial pressures and the disruption caused by its £1bn-plus separation from Walmart’s legacy IT systems.
Asda has also been investing in technology to strengthen its position, including a partnership with Ocado to overhaul its online grocery operations from 2027.
However, with market share continuing to decline, the latest figures show the scale of the challenge facing Potts as he aims to restore growth and win back customers from Asda’s rivals.

items.title: Sales of bottled water and tinned food surge after government stockpiling advice
items.summary: UK supermarkets have seen a sharp rise in sales of bottled water, tinned food and other essentials after the government’s ‘Be Ready’ campaign urged households to prepare for emergencies. Sales of hand sanitiser jumped 83 per cent, bottled water rose 67 per cent and tinned and jarred goods increased 37 per cent in the 10...
items.body:
UK supermarkets have seen a sharp rise in sales of bottled water, tinned food and other essentials after the government’s ‘Be Ready’ campaign urged households to prepare for emergencies.
Sales of hand sanitiser jumped 83 per cent, bottled water rose 67 per cent and tinned and jarred goods increased 37 per cent in the 10 days following the campaign’s launch on 22 October, according to new data from Worldpanel by Numerator.
The number of shoppers buying tinned meat rose 43 per cent, equivalent to an additional 400,000 customers a day, although the average quantity purchased remained at around 500g.
The data suggest shoppers are gradually building up emergency supplies rather than panic buying.
Worldpanel by Numerator head of retail and consumer insight Fraser McKevitt said shoppers had clearly responded to the government’s advice, but stressed that the increase in sales was not driven by panic buying.
He noted that fewer than a third of households bought bottled water during October, with consumers instead adding recommended products to their regular grocery shops.
The government’s Be Ready campaign encourages households to keep three days’ worth of essentials, including nine litres of water per person, non-perishable food, batteries, torches and first aid supplies, in case of disruption caused by extreme weather, cyberattacks or other emergencies.
Food manufacturer Princes has also reported increased demand for canned products, including fish, meat and vegetables, since the campaign launched.
Separate Barclays research found that 27 per cent of consumers were either stockpiling or considering building up emergency food and drink supplies.
The findings come as grocery inflation edged up to 2.6 per cent in the four weeks to 1 November, compared with 2.5 per cent the previous month.
Overall grocery sales rose 2.2 per cent year on year in October, according to Worldpanel.
As Retail Gazette reported earlier this week, IGD chief executive Sarah Bradbury suggested the government’s Be Ready campaign may have contributed to stronger food sales during October.
However, she warned that shoppers remained pessimistic about their finances as they headed into the crucial Christmas trading period.

items.title: Aldi cuts hundreds of UK head office and logistics roles as part of global cost trimming
items.summary: Supermarket’s move labelled ‘shortsighted’ by worker who calls upper management ‘woefully out of touch with reality’ Aldi’s UK business is cutting hundreds of head office and logistics roles as part of a global effort to trim costs at the budget grocer. The retailer is consulting with its technology team on the loss of up to 150 roles after 103 redundancies in its finance and administration team earlier this year and almost 20 more redundancies among buying directors. Continue reading...
items.body:
Aldi’s UK business is cutting hundreds of head office and logistics roles as part of a global effort to trim costs at the budget grocer.
The retailer is consulting with its technology team on the loss of up to 150 roles after 103 redundancies in its finance and administration team earlier this year and almost 20 more redundancies among buying directors.
One affected worker described the cuts as “shortsighted” and said they showed that “upper management [are] woefully out of touch with the reality”.
Jobs in stores have not been affected, although Aldi said it had reduced the number of regional managers slightly, affecting a handful of high-paying roles.
The German-owned group is reducing the number of people in local country operations as it centralises more work.
Aldi is outsourcing finance, procurement and administration roles to India, among other countries, as part of a deal with Genpact, a company that helps businesses develop the use of AI technology.
Sources said consultation was set to begin on redundancies in payroll in the coming months. The company has also recently reduced the number of cleaning hours for the agency workers at its head office in Atherstone, Warwickshire.
A spokesperson for Aldi said: “At Aldi, our promise to customers is that we will always offer great quality products at unbeatable prices. Across our international business, we continuously review all aspects of our operations to ensure we operate simply, efficiently and use our global scale to deliver on that promise.
“We are therefore making some adjustments to the way parts of our UK business are structured. Any changes are being introduced gradually and following a consultation period. We recognise that this is difficult for those involved, so we are giving colleagues as much notice as possible, with full support available to everyone affected.”
The company said it had invested £300m in lowering prices on 900 products in the UK this year.
The cuts in the UK come as Aldi struggles to keep up the pace of growth. UK sales at the chain rose only 0.4% in the 12 weeks to 1 November, according to the latest industry data from Worldpanel by Numerator, with Aldi’s market share falling back by 0.1 percentage point year on year.
The fall came as the average unit price at Aldi fell by 0.1%, making Aldi the only retailer reducing overall prices during the period.
The retailer has faced tougher competition from the traditional supermarkets, several of which now match it on price on key items alongside their much wider range of other products.
Morrisons cut hundreds of head office roles this spring shortly after Sainsbury’s eliminated 300 head office jobs as it restructured its technology team and Argos delivery network, and Tesco laid off a similar number of people as it changed the way it operated bakeries. This summer, Asda said up to 1,000 jobs were at risk as it introduced more automation into its logistics operation.

items.title: Morrisons Media Group announces retail media proposition expansion across 1,700 convenience stores
items.summary: Morrisons Media Group (MMG) is expanding its retail media proposition to include Morrisons' approximately 1,700 convenience stores, with the aim of giving brands and suppliers a more joined up approach to planning campaigns across the grocery retailer's supermarket and convenience estates.Steve Newb
items.body:
Morrisons Media Group (MMG) is expanding its retail media proposition to include Morrisons' approximately 1,700 convenience stores, with the aim of giving brands and suppliers a more joined up approach to planning campaigns across the grocery retailer's supermarket and convenience estates.
Steve Newbould, Head of Commercial Data & Media, Morrisons Media Group, says: "Expanding our proposition into convenience is an important step in how we support our supplier partners. Our customers shop across different formats for different reasons, and bringing these opportunities together allows us to offer brands a more comprehensive way to engage with them. This is about building on the strength of our existing retail media proposition while recognising the growing importance of convenience."
The expanded proposition combines Morrisons' first-party customer insights with SMG's retail media capabilities. Suppliers will benefit from MMG's existing support, including insights informed by Morrisons' first-party data ecosystem, MoreViu, to help shape campaign planning around relevant customer missions and commercial objectives.
Katie Jackson, Morrisons Media Group, says: "For suppliers, the opportunity is to plan more effectively across the Morrisons estate without taking a one-size-fits-all approach. We're bringing the same strategic support and expertise to convenience, helping brands identify relevant opportunities and develop campaigns that reflect the needs of customers in each shopping environment."
Rosie Houston, Managing Director, UK Retail Media Networks, SMG, says: "As retail media continues to evolve, there's an increasing opportunity to connect brand activity across different shopping environments. Our partnership with Morrisons is focused on making those opportunities moreaccessible and actionable for suppliers, combining retail expertise, customer insights and strategic planning to help brands make the most of every customer interaction."
2026 RTIH Innovation Awards
Morrisons was named Overall Winner at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, which took place in Central London last week. And it also emerged victorious in the RTIH Editor's Choice category for its partnership with Gatekeeper Systems.
In a LinkedIn post, the retailer said: "We’re delighted to have been named Overall Winner, selected by the judging panel as the standout entry from across all of the event's 23 categories. Great recognition for some of the brilliant and innovative cross functional projects that have been delivered over the last few months!"
It added: "We were also recognised in the Editor’s Choice Award, alongside Gatekeeper Systems for our Cart Control programme across five Morrisons stores. The programme has delivered some fantastic results: An estimated 82.1 tonnes of CO₂e saved each year; 1,170 fewer replacement trolleys needed; 7,696 fewer trolleys ending up in local communities and waterways. Congratulations to everyone involved in making this possible!"
Scott Thompson, Editor and Founder at RTIH, said: "Congratulations to Morrisons. We received a record number of entries this year, showcasing truly impressive innovation across both traditional and digital retail spaces."
"To quote a member of our judging panel: Reviewing such inventive, high impact solutions has been a truly rewarding experience. The depth of engineering, scalable architecture, and strategic vision displayed throughout the submissions underscores the rapid transformation happening across modern retail technology."
"A number of companies were in the running for Overall Winner but ultimately the judges picked Morrisons for launching several innovative initiatives encompassing major technological upgrades to enhance its customers’ shopping experience."

That's why we are confident we will capture the full end-to-end benefits, not just switch systems,with real credit to the strong collaboration with the Blue Yonder Professional Services team along the way."

items.body:
Crew Clothing Company has gone live with its online store on Shopify. The retailer worked with Voyado and Shopify partner, fusefabric, on this.
In a LinkedIn post, Raine Peake, Group Digital Director - Crew Clothing, Ben Sherman, Saltrock and Pringle, said: "It was a huge team effort and shows what can be achieved by brilliant people in a very short time frame just before Black Friday. Also to our fantastic partners who delivered on time and on budget, no mean feat and also made the whole migration a joy."
Voyado and H&M
H&M has overhauled its onsite search across more than 60 markets, working with Voyado. The retailer says that the move away from keyword matching to an intent driven model has reduced soft exits (where shoppers drift off because of friction rather than choice) by 80% and cut customer exits from search by 30%.
Rather than matching search terms to product names, the new setup reads a range of signals at once: stock availability, add to bag actions, purchase behaviour, product newness, revenue performance and customer intent and updates rankings in real-time.
“As our business grew, we needed a more intelligent approach to search, ranking, and discovery. We found Voyado to be the best fit for us.” said Lars Gezelius, Acting Global Head of Digital at H&M.
Erica Sandelin Ekelund, CEO at Voyado, said: "Search is a clear signal of what customers actually want. When a customer searches, they’re not browsing - they’re telling you. And many retailers are throwing that signal away. H&M recognised the value and used it to rebuild their customer experience from the ground up, and the numbers confirm they were right. The most successful retailers won’t be those with the most extensive catalogues. They’ll be the ones who understand their customers and what they actually came for.”

items.title: Monsoon Accessorize boosts in-store technology infrastructure with PMC Raptor platform
items.summary: Monsoon Accessorize has deployed PMC’s Raptor remote monitoring and management platform to prevent and fix technical issues, improving operations and ensuring consistent CX across its store estate.  The retailer’s mixture of legacy hardware and software had started to create challenges in
items.body:
Monsoon Accessorize has deployed PMC’s Raptor remote monitoring and management platform to prevent and fix technical issues, improving operations and ensuring consistent CX across its store estate.
The retailer’s mixture of legacy hardware and software had started to create challenges in maintaining availability, managing technical issues and deploying changes safely across its store network. Seeking to create more stable and resilient store environments while continually improving operational efficiency and reducing avoidable incidents, Monsoon Accessorize partnered with PMC to shore up its digital infrastructure.
Deploying the Raptor remote monitoring and management platform across its transactional tech stack, it says it can now proactively monitor devices and software. This allows its team to identify potential technical conditions and issues that could lead to service disruption ahead of time and, where possible, resolve them automatically.
“PMC has played an important role in helping us maintain a stable and resilient operating environment, even as some of our underlying hardware and software has aged,” says David West, Chief Technology Officer at Monsoon Accessorize. “Its Raptor monitoring technology, and the continuous improvement of the automation behind it, have helped us prevent incidents and reduce the operational impact of technical issues on our stores."
Since roll-out, the solution has prevented over 2,000 technical incidents annually through proactive identification and automated resolution of issues. It has also now scaled to automate in excess of 20 million procedures each year.
“Robust technology foundations are essential to creating the reliable, responsive store environments that underpin great customer experiences,” says Jake Allmond, Managed Services Director at PMC. “When systems work seamlessly, colleagues can focus on serving customers, rather than resolving technical issues, helping deliver consistent and compelling experiences that drive CX, conversion and sales.”
“By proactively identifying and resolving issues before they impact store operations, we’re helping Monsoon Accessorize build greater resilience within its tech stack, ensuring its stores have the stability and agility needed to support its continued growth."

items.title: OneRail brings in Amit Batra as SVP of Supply Chain and Nathan Rucker as SVP of Strategic Growth & Partnerships
items.summary: OneRail, an AI technology platform powering unified commerce for enterprise retailers, wholesalers, and distributors, has announced two additions to its leadership team.Amit Batra has joined as Senior Vice President of Supply Chain and Nathan Rucker as Senior Vice President of Strategic Growth and P
items.body:
OneRail, an AI technology platform powering unified commerce for enterprise retailers, wholesalers, and distributors, has announced two additions to its leadership team.
Amit Batra has joined as Senior Vice President of Supply Chain and Nathan Rucker as Senior Vice President of Strategic Growth and Partnerships.
"For most of its history, parcel shipping has been built around the carrier. You pick a carrier, you fit your business to their network, and you manage the tradeoffs yourself," says Bill Catania, Founder and CEO at OneRail.
"We think that model is backwards. The order should come first, and the technology should find the best way to fulfil it, regardless of shipping mode. Amit has led supply chain and delivery operations at some of the country's largest retailers."
"He has sat in the seat our customers sit in, and he knows what it takes to make fast delivery work at scale. Nathan has spent his career building the parcel systems those retailers depend on. Both came to OneRail because they want to build what comes next. Their expertise puts us years ahead in becoming the single orchestration layer for every shipment a retailer makes."
Batra will lead its supply chain strategy and help enterprise customers design and execute their omnichannel fulfillment, with a remit that spans the full journey from order sourcing through delivery and returns.
He has held senior leadership roles at The Home Depot, Walmart, and Amazon, where he developed and executed supply chain strategies and used technology and strategic partnerships to strengthen delivery capabilities and the customer experience.
Rucker, meanwhile, will lead the growth of OneRail’s parcel business across existing and prospective enterprise customers while advancing the company’s partnership strategy. He previously served on the executive leadership team at EasyPost, where he drove enterprise sales, customer expansion, mergers and acquisitions, and carrier partnership strategy. Before that, he built the enterprise business at ProShip, closing new software deals with 20% of the top 100 US retailers.

items.title: How independent stores can cut their waste bills in 2027
items.summary: Independent stores are increasingly looking for ways to minimise operating costs as 2027 approaches. Managing waste can be a significant expense for small retailers, but there are practical steps shops can take to keep bills under control. By reviewing bin size, sharing waste services, and annually
items.body:
Independent stores are increasingly looking for ways to minimise operating costs as 2027 approaches. Managing waste can be a significant expense for small retailers, but there are practical steps shops can take to keep bills under control.
By reviewing bin size, sharing waste services, and annually assessing contracts, shop owners can improve efficiency and prevent unnecessary charges.
Cutting waste bills has become a top priority for many independent shops, especially as costs continue to rise. Small changes in waste management can make a big difference to a shop’s bottom line. Key strategies include right-sizing waste bins and collections, sharing services with nearby businesses, preventing overfill and contamination fees, and checking contract terms regularly. With options for flexible contracts and transparent pricing, shops can avoid financial surprises and keep waste management both simple and cost-effective. Regularly assessing retail waste management arrangements is essential for making sure shops only pay for what they need in 2027 and beyond.
Right-sizing bins and collection schedules
For many shops, one of the fastest ways to reduce waste bills is to check whether their current bin sizes and collection frequency match actual waste volumes. Bins that are too large or collected too often can result in excess charges for unused capacity, while bins that are too small or emptied infrequently may lead to costly overfill penalties. Reviewing recent waste patterns can help shop owners adjust to the right service level.
Using accurate data to match bin types and collection days to busy trading periods ensures efficient waste handling. Shops can work with their provider to trial different sizes or change collection frequency as business needs shift. Regular reassessment prevents paying for more service than necessary and also keeps shops in line with local compliance requirements.
Collaborating with neighbouring businesses
Independent retailers located near each other often face similar waste management challenges. Sharing waste services, such as joint bin collections, can help neighbouring shops split costs and reduce individual bills. These shared arrangements also make collections more efficient, cutting down on the number of truck visits to the same area.
By documenting responsibilities and ensuring everyone understands rules for bin use and contamination, shops can avoid disputes and keep charges predictable. Digital recordkeeping makes it clear which shops have used which bins and which are responsible for contamination, preventing unexpected fees and supporting transparent service agreements among participants.
Preventing charges and optimising performance
Overfill and contamination charges can quickly push waste bills higher than expected. Shops can reduce these charges by educating staff on correct segregation, regularly checking bin levels, and acting quickly if a bin is near full. Many waste providers now offer alerts or digital dashboards that notify shop owners when a bin is full or if there’s a risk of contamination.
Annual reviews are also key to controlling costs. By looking at service records, noting recurring issues, and benchmarking different providers, shops can adapt their contracts to match real needs. Often, comparing waste management quotes once a year can save more than you’d expect. Clear audit trails and documented performance make it simpler for shops to negotiate better deals or update arrangements.
Choosing a flexible and transparent provider
Finding the right waste management partner can deliver long-term savings and operational simplicity. Shops should look for providers offering flexible contracts that accommodate changes in bin size, collection frequency, and business growth. Transparent pricing is essential, so that shops can easily see how charges are calculated and what services are included.
Good providers will also support digital recordkeeping, enabling easier contract reviews and quicker responses to billing or compliance questions. This approach gives independent shop owners confidence in their waste arrangements and helps ensure that costs are always aligned with actual usage, allowing shops to focus on their core business in 2027 and beyond.

items.title: WH Smith faces turnaround test to deter shortsellers
items.summary: New WH Smith boss Leo Quinn is preparing to face shareholders. Felix Armstrong unpicks the many troubles facing the travel retailer Announcing the sale of its high street business in March last year, Carl Cowling, then WH Smith’s chief executive, hailed a “pivotal moment” for the retailer, promising “substantial growth and value for all stakeholders”.  [...]
items.body:
WH Smith faces turnaround test to deter shortsellers
New WH Smith boss Leo Quinn is preparing to face shareholders. Felix Armstrong unpicks the many troubles facing the travel retailer
Announcing the sale of its high street business in March last year, Carl Cowling, then WH Smith’s chief executive, hailed a “pivotal moment” for the retailer, promising “substantial growth and value for all stakeholders”.
WH Smith claimed the sale of its 480 high street stores to private equity firm Modella Capital would simplify the business that remained, positioning it as a travel-only retailer well placed to cash in on the fast-growing demand for quick food and convenient accessories at train stations and airports.
But in the period since, the retailer has been troubled by a stream of profit warnings, a steady decline in its share price and the unwelcome attention of City shortsellers.
WH Smith, which delivers its full-year results on Thursday, is currently London’s 10th most-shorted listed firm, as traders bet that its woes are set to continue. The group has shed 63 per cent of its value since competing its deal with Modella, and is 35 per cent down in the year to date.
More than 18 months on from WH Smith’s high street demerger, Cowling’s decision hail it as “pivotal” have proven premature. Even the transaction itself proved to be far more complicated than hoped. The retailer slashed its initial £76m asking price to about £40m to account for “a more cautious outlook” and “softer trading”, and eventually made just £10m from the sale.
Though WH Smith was hoping to escape the myriad issues facing British high streets, this decline ended up marring its exit. And just as So too have WH Smith’s travel outposts have struggled, so too has the high street business – now renamed TG Jones under its new ownership.
Travel chaos hits profit
The retailer has cut its profit outlook twice in recent months and is now forecasting a pre-tax return of about £75m, in what would be a 40 per cent year-on-year decline. The firm has repeatedly blamed the dip in airline passengers caused by the Iran war, which sparked chaos across crucial travel routes at the start of this year.
Travellers that have passed through WH Smith’s shops have been more parsimonious than usual, the retailer has told shareholders, because airlines have passed on rising jet fuel costs in the form of higher prices.
Though WH Smith could usually hope to make a tidy profit from high-margin items like headphones and pillows, lower store footfall and softer spend per passenger is bad news for its takings.
These pressures are unlikely to ease in the near term, even as oil prices dip as President Trump signals he is keen to bring an end to the Iran war. Energy costs are staying high despite renewed shipping levels and multiple top airlines have warned that their fuel woes are unlikely to disappear any time soon.
Michael O’Leary, chief executive of budget carrier Ryanair, has warned that air fares could rise by as much as a fifth next year, while British Airways owner IAG said last week that its protection against higher fuel prices will lessen significantly next year. These factors will put more pressure on tourists’ holiday purses.
Aside from the impact of the Middle East conflict on its trading, WH Smith has been dealing with an entirely self-inflicted worry: the accounting error which had flattered the profit figures of its North American division for years.
The scandal, which attracted an ongoing probe from the Financial Conduct Authority, wiped £600m off WH Smith’s valuation in its biggest ever single-day stock decline and forced Cowling’s exit.
His successor Leo Quinn, who has led successful turnarounds at construction firm Balfour Beatty and defence group Qinetiq, will hope to convince investors that WH Smith is finally delivering on Cowling’s promise.

items.title: Poundland hopeful for last-minute rescue deal to stave off collapse
items.summary: The BBC understands the discount chain, which has been edging towards administration, will be given more time to find a buyer.
items.body:
Poundland hopeful for last-minute rescue deal to stave off collapse
- Published
Poundland and its 11,000 employees are hopeful that the retailer's impending collapse can be delayed to allow time for a last-minute rescue deal.
The discount chain has been edging towards administration after being blocked by its owners from accessing cash in its bank accounts.
A deadline to secure a buyer for the business is set to expire at midnight, but sources close to the situation have told the BBC that they expect more time will be given, thanks to the release of Â£10m in funding.
A committee of MPs is set to question Gordon Brothers, Poundland's US owners, on Wednesday following accusations that the investment firm hopes to profit from selling off Poundland's 600 stores and stock piecemeal.
Gordon Brothers - which bought the chain for just Â£1 last year - is accused of forcing that outcome by restricting Poundland's access to available cash needed to restock stores and pay wages and rent, ahead of the crucial Christmas trading period.
The investment firm has denied the claims.
But pressure remains on Poundland's owners after a takeover bid was rejected. The decision prompted calls for answers from politicians, including Prime Minister Andy Burnham.
About Â£50m had been frozen by Gordon Brothers, the BBC understands, meaning Poundland bosses were unable to restock shelves across its 600 shops.
However, sources close to the matter told the BBC on Tuesday that a release of Â£10m by its owners, while "small in the scale of things" could help at least postpone the chain's collapse while a longer term solution was explored.
Views on Poundland performance differ
The 10-day moratorium to protect Poundland from its creditors expires on Thursday, but if there is a prospect of a solvent deal, the deadline could be extended.
Views on the chain's performance differ between those running operations and the owners.
Poundland boss Barry Williams told staff last week that like-for-like sales, which exclude new store openings, were up 11.4%. The sales period included Halloween, but Williams said this was Â£1.5m ahead of budget.
He added the business made a profit of Â£18.1m in the year to September, which was a "strong recovery" from the previous year where there were losses of Â£68m.
However, Gordon Brothers has painted a different picture, saying the chain remains "challenged and vulnerable to any potential downturn in future trading".
There has been interest from the likes of Poundstretcher, Tesco and B&M in picking up Poundland stores which could mean continuing employment for workers in the event the chain is broken up and sold off in chunks.
The main issue is whether a piecemeal sale would protect more jobs than a buyer willing to keep Poundland as a national chain.
