items.title: The £40 cashmere jumpers my mum bought online are polyester - and the seller won't give a refund: Consumer lawyer DEAN DUNHAM replies
items.summary: The retailer won't give her a returns address and keeps offering her an exchange or partial refund to keep the jumpers. What would you suggest?
items.body:
The £40 cashmere jumpers my mum bought online are polyester - and the seller won't give a refund: Consumer lawyer DEAN DUNHAM replies
Updated:
My elderly mother bought what she thought were cashmere jumpers online for £40 each.
The jumpers that arrived were 100 per cent polyester and terrible quality.
The retailer won’t give her a returns address and keeps offering her an exchange or partial refund to keep the jumpers.
What would you suggest?
C.K.M., West Midlands.
I am sorry your mother has been treated this way, but she has strong legal rights and should not settle for this runaround.
The heart of it is the jumpers were plainly misdescribed. Sold as cashmere but being 100 per cent polyester, they simply aren’t what she paid for.
An online retailer is refusing to allow a reader's elderly mother return some unwanted jumpers
Under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, goods must match their description and be of satisfactory quality. In these circumstances your mother is entitled to a full refund.
Though she doesn’t need it, an additional route is available. Because she bought online, the Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013 give her a separate right to cancel most online purchases within 14 days of receipt, without giving any reason.
She doesn’t even need to rely on the misdescription argument to exercise this right.
Now for the retailer’s tactics. Refusing to provide a returns address while offering partial refunds is unacceptable.
Where goods are misdescribed, the retailer must bear the reasonable cost of returning them.
Share this article
HOW THIS IS MONEY CAN HELP
If she cancels under the online cancellation regulations instead, your mother may have to pay return postage, but only if the retailer properly informed her of that obligation before the purchase.
So here’s what I’d advise. Write to the retailer, keeping a copy of your message, stating that your mother is rejecting the goods as misdescribed under the Consumer Rights Act 2015 and demanding a full refund.
The letter or email should also seek clear instructions for returning the jumpers. Your mother should also keep proof of sending them back.
If the seller still refuses to cooperate, her next step is to contact her card provider. If she paid by credit card with the sum more than £100 but no more than £30,000, she may be able to make a Section 75 claim.
If she paid by debit or credit card, she can also ask for a chargeback. Neither route is automatic, but both are worth pursuing.
My bird table has got the neighbours in a flap
I feed the pigeons in my front garden. I put out seed at seven each morning and after a couple of hours it is all gone.
My neighbours have said this could attract vermin, and have reported me to the council’s environmental health department.
I disagree. I put the food on a bird table and make sure no excess is left out, cleaning it regularly. I have never seen vermin. How can I fight my corner?
H.F., address supplied.
Feeding wild birds is not in itself unlawful, and the responsible approach you’ve described puts you in a strong position.
Environmental health cannot take action simply because a neighbour is concerned about what might happen. There needs to be a legal basis for intervention.
Under the Environmental Protection Act 1990, the relevant consideration is whether your activities create a statutory nuisance.
This could include an accumulation of food or waste that is prejudicial to health, or conditions that attract rats or mice.
The council does not have to wait until an infestation has occurred. It can act if it is satisfied that a statutory nuisance exists or is likely to occur or recur. However, a neighbour’s unsupported speculation that bird feeding might attract vermin is not, on its own, enough for formal action.
This is where your careful habits become your best defence. The fact that you use a bird table rather than scattering food on the ground, put out modest quantities that are consumed within a couple of hours, leave no excess, clean regularly and have never seen vermin all help show that you are feeding birds responsibly.
So here’s how to protect yourself. Keep a dated log of what you put out, when and your cleaning routine. Take photos of your bird table and surrounding garden. If an environmental health officer visits, be cooperative and invite them to inspect.
You appear to have a strong case, but – as I always advise – you should do all you can to avoid a dispute with your neighbour, so a discussion to see if you can reach a compromise on the issue would be wise.
Can Dean Dunham help you?
Do you have a legal question for Dean Dunham? Email d.dunham@dailymail.co.uk, with brief details of your question or problem.

Premium tequila brand el Jimador has launched its new Sparkling Margarita RTD cocktail range in ASDA.
The expertly crafted Sparkling Margaritas turn the classic margarita experience into a high-quality ready to drink option for consumers. The Lime flavour is a full margarita moment with tangy citrus and a subtle sweetness, resulting in a perfectly balanced sip of crisp lime and smooth tequila. The Mango flavour infuses vibrant, juicy mango with a hint of lime, providing a refreshingly exotic twist on the classic margarita. Both varieties deliver an ABV of 6.5%.
Bethan Roberts, brand manager at el Jimador said:  “We are thrilled to partner with ASDA to bring our brand-new Sparkling Margaritas to 373 supermarkets nationwide. This exciting news comes as we see a huge rise in popularity for tequila as a category across Great Britain. The category growth we are seeing is driven by the soaring popularity of the Margarita, so this is perfect timing for the el Jimador Sparkling Margarita RTDs to be available across the country.
With el Jimador Blanco recently named the #1 tequila by value in Great Britain across Total Trade [1], it is clear that momentum is firmly behind us as a brand. Major retailers are taking serious notice right now because tequila is no longer just a niche option —it’s actively driving value and volume across the total spirits category.
As the RTD market value reaches £818 million (+25.3% vs YA) [2], consumers are seeking convenient, bar-quality options at home. Partnering with ASDA allows us to meet that demand head-on, giving shoppers easy access to a premium, refreshing Lime or Mango Sparkling Margarita – alongside driving the next phase of growth for the category.”
The flavourful Lime and Mango options were selected as key flavours for launch following rigorous consumer testing. Lime delivered outstanding consumer desire and trial interest, thanks to its crisp flavour and ‘hint of lime’. Meanwhile Mango was a hit as 83% of consumers stated they would ‘definitely’ or ‘probably’ purchase, with consumers specifically enjoying the ‘citrusy zing’ of the product[7].
The Sparkling Margarita cans join the el Jimador UK portfolio which includes Blanco, Reposado, and Anejo.
18+. Please drink responsibly.

items.body:
Young managing director of Abu Bakr Supermarkets celebrates another major career milestone after being crowned winner of the Next Gen Award at the Asian Trader Awards.
Britain’s youngest supermarket boss is celebrating another major career milestone after winning a prestigious national award recognising the next generation of talent in the retail industry.
Hamza Hussain, managing director of Leeds head quartered Abu Bakr Supermarket, took home the Next Gen Award at the 2026 Asian Trader Awards, following a glittering ceremony at the Westminster Park Plaza Hotel in London.
The 23-year-old was named the winner on November 4, beating competition from across the UK to secure the accolade.
The achievement marks another significant moment for Hamza, who has enjoyed an impressive run of recognition after previously being named among the industry’s 30 Under 30.
His latest success follows his shortlisting for the Next Gen Award, which recognises emerging leaders making their mark on the UK’s convenience retail sector.
Reflecting on his achievement, Hamza Hussain said: “Winning the Next Gen Award is an incredible honour and something I am genuinely proud of. To have our work recognised on a national stage, among so many talented people in the retail industry, means a great deal to me.
“However, this award is about much more than one individual. It represents the hard work, commitment and dedication of everyone at Abu Bakr Supermarket, as well as the support we receive from our customers and the communities we serve.
“I am incredibly fortunate to be part of a family business with such strong foundations, and I am excited about what we can achieve in the future. We have big ambitions, and this recognition gives us even more motivation to keep pushing forward.”
The Asian Trader Awards, now in their 38th year, bring together leading independent retailers, suppliers and industry figures to celebrate excellence, innovation and achievement across the convenience retail sector.
For Hamza, the award represents recognition not only of his own development as a young business leader but also of the work taking place behind the scenes at Abu Bakr Supermarkets.
The family-run business has established a strong presence across West Yorkshire, serving diverse communities through its stores and offering a wide selection of groceries, fresh produce, world foods and everyday essentials.
Hamza has taken a hands-on approach to leadership, gaining experience across different areas of the business, from customer service and stock management to commercial development and future expansion.
His approach combines the traditional values of independent retailing with a modern outlook, as the business continues to develop its offering and strengthen its relationship with the communities it serves.
The latest award adds to a growing list of achievements for the young managing director and puts further recognition on Abu Bakr Supermarkets as it continues its ambitions for growth.

items.body:
Harrods unveils its plans for Christmas 2026 with ‘Where the Stars Align’, transforming the Knightsbridge store into a festive destination with Christmas displays, exclusive luxury brand activations, personalised gifting and seasonal experiences.
Inspired by the stars that shine throughout the festive season, and with a nod to Harrods’ iconic Christmas lights, the campaign celebrates moments of joy, discovery and wonder that define Christmas.
Looking ahead to an exciting 2027, this Christmas presents a unique opportunity to celebrate everything that makes Harrods an iconic festive destination. Bringing together its world-famous façade and festive windows with exclusive activations, hospitality and gifting experiences, this year’s campaign places Harrods at the heart of the Christmas season.
Michael Ward, managing director of Harrods, said: “Christmas has always been a defining moment for Harrods and a special tradition for Londoners and visitors from around the world. With more than a third of our customers visiting during the festive season, Where the Stars Align celebrates everything that
makes Harrods extraordinary.
“As our first wholly Harrods-created festive campaign in several years, it allows us the opportunity to celebrate the craftsmanship behind our iconic displays, exceptional brand partnerships and the moments of discovery, wonder and gifting that make Christmas
in Knightsbridge so special. It is a celebration of our brand, our heritage and the role we continue to play at the heart of the festive season.
“As we look ahead to 2027, we are proud to showcase the best London has to offer at Christmas, creating moments of joy, wonder and connection for everyone who visits us.”
A spectacular Christmas transformation
The iconic Harrods façade and festive windows will undergo a celestial-inspired transformation, featuring 600 handcrafted stars, four kilometres of gold leaf and 500 sets of fairy lights creating a starlit spectacle across Harrods that will illuminate Knightsbridge
and inspire visitors to look up in wonder.
By night, more than 17,000 bulbs will light up the Harrods estate, creating a glittering backdrop to this year’s celestial-inspired Christmas display.
Bringing the installation to life has involved more than 60 specialists and 40,000 hours of work, with all production taking place in the UK, including London, reflecting Harrods commitment to championing British creativity and manufacturing expertise.
The Christmas windows will showcase creations from leading maison, including Schiaparelli, Balenciaga, Gucci, Bottega Veneta, Valentino, Ralph Lauren and Balmain.
Exclusive festive experiences
Throughout November and December, Harrods will host a programme of festive activations and immersive retail experiences, including collaborations with Dior, Ralph Lauren, Van Cleef & Arpels, Chopard, Graff, Cartier and Chanel Beauty. The programme will also
feature appearances from renowned artists and creative directors from some of the world’s leading luxury brands, offering customers exclusive opportunities to engage with the creative talent behind the season’s most exciting experiences.
Harrods Rewards members will also enjoy access to exclusive experiences, from live illustration and luxury engraving to leather personalisation and bespoke calligraphy. Additional highlights include gold-leaf and bauble personalisation with Acqua di Parma and
illustration workshops with Clé de Peau Beauté.
The ultimate Christmas gifting destination
From the iconic teddy bear and signature Christmas hampers to exclusive fashion, beauty, fine jewellery and watches, Harrods offers an exceptional selection of gifts for loved ones and self-gifting alike.
Customers can also benefit from Harrods’ renowned services, including Personal Shopping, gift wrapping, hands-free shopping, concierge support and delivery options, making Christmas shopping effortless.
Beyond gifting, Harrods offers over 18 dining destinations, alongside the arrival of the world’s first Jellycat Brunch, an immersive concept exclusive to the Knightsbridge store. Younger visitors can also enjoy festive activities, including writing and posting
letters to Father Christmas.
Where the Stars Align launches at Harrods in early November 2026, with further details of the Christmas illuminations and festive programme to be announced.

Cotswolds-based Hawkstone Brewery has announced their hop onto renewables, by instructing Nottinghamshire-based Geo Green Power to complete their first solar PV installation on their brewing premises in Bourton-on-the-Water, Gloucestershire.
Hawkstone Brewery – famously founded back in 2021 by broadcaster and TV farmer Jeremy Clarkson – says work on the installation is set to begin in November of this year and the systems will be used to power processes within the brewery, from milling machines through to heating and cooling systems.
The rooftop solar PV system will comprise of Canadian Solar solar PV modules secured with Renusol fixings, a SolarEdge inverter and SolarEdge Optimizers. When fully operational, it will generate 24.25MWh of energy per annum and save 4.9 tonnes of CO₂ each year – the equivalent of planting 215 trees. The brewery will subsequently see substantial savings on its energy costs, alongside reduced Scope 2 emissions and increased energy security against the backdrop of continued rising energy prices that have seen many hospitality businesses struggling to make ends meet.
Geo Green Power’s appointment comes in part from the firm’s strong ties to both Britain’s agricultural and hospitality sectors – something the company of course shares with Hawkstone.
When speaking about the new solar project, Ben Bonham the Head Brewer of Hawkstone Brewery said:
“We’re always looking for ways to improve how we operate, and investing in solar energy is a natural next step for us. Brewing is an energy-intensive process, so generating our own renewable electricity will help us reduce our environmental impact while making the brewery more efficient and resilient.”
James Cunningham, the managing director of Geo Green Power, also offered these comments on the upcoming project:
“We’re incredibly excited to get started on this fantastic project and with our extensive solar experience within the hospitality industry, we know what a great opportunity this is for Hawkstone Brewery.
“It’s also brilliant to be working with a business which also champions agriculture and Britain’s farms. This is something we’ve also seen first-hand, having shared an adjacent tent to the Hawkstone team at this year’s ‘Cereals Event’ held at Jeremy Clarkson’s Diddly Squat Farm.
“This approach is something we highly value at Geo Green Power as we proudly support farmers and farms across the country with commercial solar, and again, we have seen the positive impact investment in renewables has had for these communities.”
Alongside manufacturers SolarEdge and Renusol, Geo Green Power’s supplier partners for this project are UK Greentech, Yardlink and CJW Scaffolding with Geo Green Power’s own team delivering installation and ongoing service & maintenance support.

items.summary: The owner of Poundland has agreed to release around £10m of funding in order to pay the firm’s suppliers a day before its bosses are grilled by the government. Gordon Brothers, the US investment firm which owns the retail group, will unlock the funds held on Poundland’s balance sheet as the first in a series [...]
items.body:
Poundland owner set to release £10m to retailer ahead of MP questioning
The owner of Poundland has agreed to release around £10m of funding in order to pay the firm’s suppliers a day before its bosses are grilled by the government.
Gordon Brothers, the US investment firm which owns the retail group, will unlock the funds held on Poundland’s balance sheet as the first in a series of payments, City AM understands.
Gordon Brothers pledged earlier today to protect jobs at the embattled retailer after pressure from the business secretary and mounting political backlash over its handling of a sale process, a source told City AM.
The US investment firm met with Jonathan Reynolds this afternoon to discuss the future of the company and its 12,000 staff.
A source close to Reynolds said the minister had stressed the group “must do everything in [its] power to protect jobs and provide certainty for workers”.
Sky News first reported the news of the injection for Poundland.
The source said Reynolds “is pleased to have secured this commitment from Gordon Brothers in the meeting and will continue to hold the company to account and closely monitor developments.”
City AM revealed last week Poundland is on course for an £18m profit despite its owner pushing for a sale and claiming that the retailer remains “challenged and vulnerable”.
Industry sources said the release of funds is a “vital step” but warned it did not necessarily mean the discount retailer could avoid falling into administration as soon as this week, according to Sky News.
Little-known ‘frontrunner’ emerges
The move from Gordon Brothers comes after it was revealed on Monday that little-known investment firm, Xyra Group Holdings, emerged as a “frontrunner” to buy Poundland has called on Steve Smith, the retailer’s founder, to bolster its bid for the struggling firm.
The investment firm, founded by 23-year-old Manvedeep Singh, has asked Smith to lend support to their £12.5m bid to keep Poundland afloat as the discount retailer veers towards collapse.
Smith has had conversations with Xyra Group in recent days but does not plan to take part in any takeover efforts until a deal has been completed, it is understood.

items.body:
Jam Shed, the disruptive wine brand worth £94m, is turning up the heat in the wine fixture with Chilli Jam Spicy Chilli Rosé, available now in Asda.
Launching under the call to ‘Spice up your Jam’, Chilli Jam pairs a dry rosé and ripe berry flavours with a warm chilli finish, giving the spicy drinks trend a distinctly Jam Shed take.
As an established disruptor, Jam Shed has the permissibility and personality to lead the charge and inject the brand’s playfulness into the wine category. Chilli continues to gain traction across UK drinks, with consumer interest in spicy alcoholic drinks rising 6% year-on-year. While cocktails and RTDs have been quick to experiment with heat, Chilli Jam takes the flavour trend into a new part of the alcohol fixture, giving wine shoppers a more unexpected way into the trend.
It also follows a wave of spicy rosé serves and chilli-infused wine content across social media, giving Jam Shed an opportunity to translate a behaviour already generating interest into an off-the-shelf format.
Chilli Jam also joins Jam Shed’s newly launched premium range, adding a distinctive new flavour to the brand’s growing portfolio and giving retailers another way to tap into shoppers’ appetite for experimentation.
Grace Robertshawe, Jam Shed brand manager at Vinarchy, said: “With innovative flavours now the second most-cited attribute shoppers say they’d pay more for in wine, bringing something genuinely new to the fixture has never mattered more.”
“Jam Shed is the perfect brand to shake up the category with trend-led NPD like Chilli Jam – we’ve built our name on being the fun, playful disruptor our loyal shoppers keep coming back to, and Chilli Jam is the boldest expression of that yet. It’s exactly the kind of flavour moment that gets people talking, sharing and trying something new.”

items.body:
B&Q, the UK’s leading home improvement retailer, has launched its latest Build a Life Project Report, showcasing its efforts to reduce environmental impact, help customers make more sustainable choices and support the communities it serves.
As B&Q continues to evolve its responsible business strategy, the annual report provides a framework for measuring progress, celebrating achievements and identifying opportunities to do more.[BL1]
Among the key achievements are the opening of B&Q’s Cheltenham Sustainable Store – bringing more sustainable choices to customers and a 67.2% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 carbon emissions since 2016/17 with initiatives such as the decarbonisation of its logistics fleet.
The brand also launched Pennies into its stores across the UK and Ireland, enabling customers to make micro donations at the till and which raised £2.7 million since its launch. The fundraising efforts of B&Q’s colleagues also raised £4.6 million for charity partners and local communities in 2025/26.
The report also highlights the expansion of the Refurb by B&Q programme to include more products like power tools and taps along with improving the knowledge of our colleagues about our net zero plans through the carbon literacy programme.
Further progress includes:
- 67.3% of sales come from products with more sustainable features or benefits.
- 99.7% of wood and paper used in products being responsibly sourced.
- 99% of waste diverted from landfill.
- A 41% reduction in energy use since 2014/15, with 99% of electricity now sourced from renewable sources.
- All bagged composts and own-brand plants delivered to stores using 100% peat-free compost.
- New sustainable packaging guidelines, targeting at least 30% recycled plastic in packaging and 100% recyclable, reusable or compostable packaging by 2030.
- B&Q Foundation grants awarded to 203 charities, helping more than 101,000 people benefit from spaces that feel more like home.
- B&Q colleagues completed 300+ Community Day projects, helping 310,219 people benefit from a better community space.
- More than 90,000 items donated through B&Q’s Community Reuse initiative.
- More than 3,000 colleagues having completed or undertaking apprenticeships through the Learning for Life programme.
Samantha Dyer, B&Q’s Head of Responsible Business, said:
“Our latest Build a Life Project Report is an important way for us to measure the progress we are making in reducing our environmental impact and understanding the difference we make to people across our business and communities. It helps us recognise and celebrate what we have achieved, while identifying where we can do more to create positive change.
“Over the last year, we’ve taken a more joined-up, people-centered approach to responsible business, with initiatives such as the opening of our Cheltenham Sustainable Store – a first for B&Q, scaling the Refurb by B&Q programme which has expanded to more than 300 products, including taps and power tools, building carbon literacy among our colleagues and making a difference through community and charitable initiatives.
“By working together across our business and with our partners and suppliers, we can build on this progress and make a lasting difference for people and the planet.”

items.body:
As the biggest Christmas adverts hit our screens, first to launch, Debenhams has set the tone celebrating the magic of a good old-fashioned British Christmas, with a star-studded film bringing together Emily Atack, Mathew Horne, Kym Marsh and Gabrielle.
With the Christmas advertising season now in full swing, Britain’s biggest retailers are turning to familiar faces, iconic music and nostalgic storytelling to capture the nation’s festive spirit.
And while the likes of John Lewis have now joined the festive advertising line-up, Debenhams was among the first major retailers to kick-start the season, unveiling its star-studded Christmas film on 15 October.
Titled Christmas. For Everyone. Debenhams’ four-minute film is a nostalgic celebration of the quintessentially British Christmas party, complete with old flames, familiar faces, festive mishaps and a soundtrack guaranteed to get the nation singing along.
Starring Emily Atack, Mathew Horne, Kym Marsh and music icon Gabrielle, alongside Debenhams style ambassador Mark Heyes, the film brings a distinctly British sense of humour, glamour and nostalgia to this year’s festive advertising line-up.
At its heart is a simple reminder that Christmas isn’t about everything going perfectly to plan, but about the people, memories and unexpected moments that make the season special.
The film opens with Tina, played by Emily Atack, getting glammed up with friends ahead of the village Christmas party. Back in her childhood home for the festive season, she’s struggling to find her Christmas spirit until she unexpectedly comes face-to-face with Chris (Mathew Horne), an old childhood friend.
Once quiet, shy and barely on her radar, Chris suddenly catches Tina’s eye, and as the evening unfolds, it becomes clear that an old connection might just be rekindled. But in true British fashion, the festivities don’t quite go to plan.
When landlady Katie, played by Kym Marsh, announces that the headline act has been caught in a snowstorm, Chris reluctantly steps up to save the day, taking to the stage with his guitar.
As he begins to play, a flashback takes viewers back to the pair’s teenage years, sitting together on a park bench in their school uniforms, playing the very same song.
Just as Tina begins to reminisce about their connection, the entire village hall plunges into darkness, thanks to a power cut caused by a neighbour’s over-the-top Christmas light display.
With the celebrations hanging in the balance, the village rallies together to get the party back on track, before music icon Gabrielle makes a surprise entrance, taking to the stage as the lights come back on.
As Gabrielle performs her iconic 90s hit Dreams, Tina and Chris finally reunite with a kiss, and the village party erupts into a celebration of friendship, love and togetherness.
The film closes with the glamorous village revellers, including influencers Saffron Barker, Sammi Maria and Jay Beech, dancing the night away, capturing the joy of those spontaneous Christmas moments that often become the most memorable.
From getting dressed up for the annual Christmas party to reconnecting with old friends and making new memories with loved ones, Debenhams is celebrating everything that makes the festive season special.
And with nostalgia at the heart of its Christmas campaign, the retailer is bringing together its rich British heritage with a distinctly modern take on festive celebrations, reminding the nation that sometimes the simplest moments make the most magical memories.
The star-studded village party also showcases the very best of Debenhams’ festive fashion, beauty and homeware collections, including party-ready looks from Coast, Warehouse, Wallis, OASIS, Dorothy Perkins and Burton, alongside beauty favourites from YSL, Givenchy and Chloé and homeware from brands including Shark and Ninja.
From finding the perfect party outfit to adding those all-important finishing touches, Debenhams is helping shoppers look and feel their best throughout the festive season, wherever the celebrations take them.
Dan Finley, CEO at Debenhams Group, said: “Christmas is all about dressing up, making the home look amazing and celebrating.
“It’s a time for creating new memories and reconnecting with the people, places and traditions we hold dear. Nostalgia has always been part of Debenhams’ story, and as a retailer with such a rich British heritage, we understand the role that familiar moments and celebrations play in bringing people together.
“Whether it’s an old flame, connecting with long-standing friends or family around the table, it’s often the simplest moments, a laugh, a dance or a conversation, that become the memories we treasure most.
“That’s what we wanted to celebrate in this film: a familiar Christmas full of warmth, humour and a few surprises, with Debenhams right at the heart of the celebrations, bringing the very best of fashion, beauty, home and fragrance together in one place.”
Emily Atack said: “For me, Debenhams and Christmas go hand in hand, so it was great to be asked to be a part of the campaign this year especially as this is such an exciting Christmas for me personally. I loved filming it, the warm, nostalgic vibe of the party in the film felt just perfect and what a fantastically talented and lovely cast to be a part of.
“I can’t wait for this Christmas season, and I adore the theme of the campaign which is to remind everyone to reconnect with family and friends at this wonderful time of the year.”
Mathew Horne added: “I’m often associated with Christmas due to a certain TV programme! I know many fans have associated memories around that show and the festive period. Families, friends and loved ones would gather round the TV to watch the Christmas specials and I’m delighted to be a part of another festive film that celebrates similar themes of togetherness.”
Gabrielle said: “I’m absolutely thrilled to be working with Debenhams this Christmas! It’s a brand I’ve loved for years, so being part of their Christmas campaign feels really special. I’m excited for everyone to see it.”
The Christmas. For Everyone. campaign was created in-house by Debenhams, with production by Pulse Films and direction from award-winning commercial director Tom Day.
First unveiled on 15 October, the film forms part of Debenhams’ wider festive campaign, spanning online, social, out-of-home and media activations throughout the Christmas season.

items.body:
Monsoon Accessorize has underpinned its in-store technology infrastructure, deploying PMC’s Raptor remote monitoring and management platform to proactively prevent and fix technical issues to improve operations and ensure consistent CX across its estate.
The investment in store technology resilience comes as Monsoon Accessorize continues to build on its commercial turnaround and expand its physical footprint.
Last year, Monsoon Accessorize said it had returned to profitability, reporting a +3.7% rise in sales to £212million, thanks to “solid growth” from its core Accessorize business across sales and new store openings, as well as “significant gains” made by Monsoon’s ecommerce operations and marketplace performance.  The retailer’s expansion strategy is focused on further extending its store footprint, amid a wave of new store openings and refurbishments across both the High Street and travel retail locations.
With this growing store footprint, maintaining reliable and resilient transactional systems remains critical to supporting the retailer’s growth and delivering consistent customer experiences across its estate.
However, the retailer’s mixture of legacy hardware and software had started to create challenges in maintaining availability, managing technical issues and deploying changes safely across its store network.  Seeking to create more stable and resilient store environments while continually improving operational efficiency and reducing avoidable incidents, Monsoon Accessorize partnered with PMC to shore up its digital infrastructure.
Deploying PMC’s Raptor remote monitoring and management platform across its transactional tech stack, the retailer can now proactively monitor devices and software. This allows Monsoon Accessorize’s team to identify potential technical conditions and issues that could lead to service disruption ahead of time and, where possible, resolve them automatically.
By addressing recurring issues at source and reducing the need for manual intervention, this continual improvement has created a more robust store infrastructure, as well as helping to maintain the stability of the legacy POS environment.
“PMC has played an important role in helping us maintain a stable and resilient operating environment, even as some of our underlying hardware and software has aged,” David West, chief technology officer at Monsoon Accessorize, said. “Its Raptor monitoring technology, and the continuous improvement of the automation behind it, have helped us prevent incidents and reduce the operational impact of technical issues on our stores.”
Since rollout, the solution has prevented over 2,000 technical incidents annually through proactive identification and automated resolution of issues.  It has also now scaled to automate in excess of 20 million procedures each year. This has helped improve operational efficiency through automated remediation while creating a more stable architecture upon which controlled software updates can be deployed.
“Robust technology foundations are essential to creating the reliable, responsive store environments that underpin great customer experiences,” said Jake Allmond, managed services director at PMC. “When systems work seamlessly, colleagues can focus on serving customers, rather than resolving technical issues, helping deliver consistent and compelling experiences that drive CX, conversion and sales.”

items.body:
With Black Friday just around the corner and wishlists already taking shape, new sales data from Cult Beauty reveals exactly what’s topping everyone’s basket, and it turns out shoppers are saving their splurge for the luxury fragrance they won’t pay full price for.
During last year’s Cyber event, sales of Creed Aventus 50ml soared by 15,700% compared with an average week. That’s around 158 bottles sold for every one sold in a normal week.
The cult men’s fragrance led a wider rush on scent, with fragrance the fastest growing category of the entire Cyber period. Sales jumped by 1,383% on a typical week, almost 15 times the usual volume, as shoppers used the discounts to trade up to designer and niche bottles, many of them destined to be wrapped and placed under the tree.
Makeup fills the baskets, Charlotte Tilbury tops the charts
While fragrance saw the biggest spike, makeup was what shoppers bought in the greatest volume. Cosmetics was Cult Beauty’s bestselling category across Cyber, with nearly 475,000 units sold.
The single bestselling product of the event was the Charlotte Tilbury Airbrush Flawless Setting Spray 100ml, with more than 11,000 units sold.
Charlotte Tilbury also claimed the fastest sell-outs of the sale. The limited edition Pretty Glowing palette, one of the brand’s Christmas sets, sold out after just one day, while the Charlotte Tilbury Bronzer in Medium, a core line, was gone within two days.
The surprise repeat purchase is… toothpaste
The data from Cult Beauty also reveals which products Cyber shoppers loved enough to buy again. Among customers who shopped Cyber 2025, the most repurchased product so far this year isn’t a serum or a lipstick, it’s Marvis Whitening Mint Toothpaste, reordered 2,033 times. The Italian brand, known for its retro packaging and unusual flavours, has become a cult bathroom shelf staple.
The most repurchased Cyber products of 2026 so far
| Rank | Product | 
| 1 | Marvis Whitening Mint Toothpaste (85ml) | 
| 2 | Charlotte Tilbury Airbrush Flawless Setting Spray 100ml | 
| 3 | Paula’s Choice Skin Perfecting 2% BHA Liquid Exfoliant (118ml) | 
| 4 | Huda Beauty Easy Bake Loose Powder, Pound Cake | 
| 5 | Danessa Myricks Beauty Yummy Skin Blurring Balm Powder, Universal | 
The most popular time to shop over Black Friday weekend
Orders peaked across four key days: the Thursday before Black Friday, Black Friday itself, the Tuesday when Cult Beauty’s main Cyber offer launched, and Cyber Monday. The busiest hours were in the evening and immediately after Cult Beauty’s morning email landed in inboxes.
How to shop Cyber like a pro
With this year’s event fast approaching, Cult Beauty’s in-house beauty expert Trifonia Spiers shares her tips for making the most of it.
- Start early
The Thursday before Black Friday is one of our busiest days of the whole event, so the best stock can be gone before the weekend even starts, If there’s something you’ve had your eye on, don’t wait until Friday.
- Check your inbox first thing
Orders spike straight after Cult Beauty’s morning email lands, so be ready when it arrives.
- Don’t leave Christmas sets sitting in your basket.
Limited edition gift sets are the first to go, last year’s bestselling Charlotte Tilbury palette sold out in a day, so if it’s on your list, check out rather than coming back to it later.
- Go big on fragrance
It’s where shoppers find the biggest Cyber savings on the products they’d rarely buy at full price, and it makes for an easy, crowd-pleasing Christmas present.
- Stock up on your staples
Our repurchase data shows people aren’t just buying treats, they’re buying the things they use every single day. If you know you’ll buy it again anyway, whether that’s a setting spray, an exfoliant or even your toothpaste, Cyber is the time to buy two.
Beauty expert Trifionia Spiers at Cult Beauty said, “Black Friday has become the moment our customers buy the things they’ve been wanting all year. Fragrance is the clearest example as shoppers have had a bottle like Creed Aventus on their wishlist for months, and Cyber is when they finally treat themselves or tick off a big Christmas present. At the same time, we see people using it to stock up on the hardworking products they genuinely can’t be without, whether that’s a setting spray or, it turns out, their favourite toothpaste.”

In a message to store managers across the country, David Potts asked […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
The newly appointed Asda CEO, David Potts, has started his first official day in the role with a call to action for its 1,100 Store Managers, telling them to focus on fixing the things that matter most to customers shopping in its stores.
In a message to store managers across the country, David Potts asked them to focus on three fundamental areas that will make the biggest difference to the shopping trip:
- Open more full-service checkouts so customers, especially those doing bigger shops can get help from a colleague when they need it.
- Spend more time on the shop floor supporting colleagues, and making sure the store is in good shape for customers throughout the day.
- Get more product on shelves and presented well so the things customers come in for are easy to see and pick-up.
Speaking from Asda’s store in Pudsey on his first day as CEO, David Potts said: “More than anything Asda shoppers want great value which is why the business has invested to get back on the pitch when it comes to low prices. But visiting stores as a customer over the last few weeks has shown me we aren’t as focused on the rest of the shopping trip as we need to be.
“We’re making it harder than it should be for customers to get what they want, move around the store and pay for their shopping.
“We need to change that, starting now, which is why I’ve instructed all our General Store Managers to open more full-service checkouts, spend more time on the shopfloor and get more product on shelves and well-presented throughout the day.
“The shopping trip is everything and by making Asda easier to shop so customers can find what they came for and get through the checkouts easily, they’ll come back and shop more with us.
“I’ll be out in stores again this week and over the weekend listening to customers to see how we’re doing, and making sure our colleagues have what they need to deliver the improvements our customers expect.”

This helped drive unit sales growth to […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Total Till sales at UK major supermarkets increased by +3.2% in the four weeks ending 31st October 2026, according to the latest data released today by NielsenIQ (NIQ).
NIQ data shows that sales momentum strengthened throughout October, with growth reaching +4.1% in the final week of the month. This helped drive unit sales growth to +1.5% over the four-week period, the strongest performance recorded this year outside of Easter.
The latest data also shows the frequency of shopping increased (+2.1%) compared with last year, while the average spend per visit rose (+1.5%) to £18.96. 2 This came as food inflation increased to +2.9% in October, up from +2.4% in September.
Canned goods drive category growth
Ambient grocery was the fastest-growing supermarket super-category in October, with sales up +6.9%. Growth gathered pace as the month progressed, rising from +3.3% in the first fortnight to +10.6% in the second.
Canned goods, within ambient grocery, surged +27% in the second half on the month. This coincided with the Be Ready government advice, which may have contributed to changing grocery shopping patterns.
Halloween provides an Autumnal boost
The recovery in Total Till sales emerges despite weakening consumer confidence which fell 11 points to -24. The last time we saw a drop of this size was following the Brexit vote. 4 Rising energy and fuel costs are also continuing to put pressure on household budgets. While shoppers remained mindful of their spending, the half-term holidays and Halloween provided a welcome boost for supermarkets, as families embraced seasonal celebrations while continuing to seek value.
Pumpkins were a standout seasonal purchase, with unit sales growing +8% year on year highlighting the importance of affordability in encouraging Halloween spending.
The impulse super-category recorded value growth (+5.4%), supported by demand for sweets, chocolate sharing multipacks and snacks. While the value sales of multipack confectionery were broadly flat (-0.5%), unit sales increased (+4.5%), suggesting shoppers were buying more packs without a corresponding increase in spend.
Elsewhere, alcoholic ready-to-drink beverages (RTDs) recorded strong value growth of +28%, despite overall alcohol sales remaining largely flat (+0.1%). Cosmetics sales also increased +3.5%, although some categories traditionally associated with Halloween failed to grow compared with last year, suggesting shoppers continued to make selective trade-offs on discretionary purchases.
Online grocery accelerates as shoppers embrace rapid delivery
Online grocery continued to outperform the wider market in October, with ecommerce sales increasing +13.1%, compared with growth of just +1.5% for in-store sales.
NIQ data shows that ecommerce accounted for almost 59% of all FMCG value growth at the major supermarkets and 80% of incremental unit growth, underlining the growing importance of online shopping as households replenished grocery supplies.
Online also benefited from the Halloween demand, particularly in categories such as confectionery, as shoppers turned to digital channels for seasonal treats and last-minute purchases.
Rapid grocery delivery saw strong growth, accounting for +11.5% of all online FMCG sales on Saturday 31st October, reaching levels comparable with the highs seen during the summer months.
Tesco gains momentum as Ocado, M&S and Lidl outperform
In terms of retailer performance, Tesco gained momentum, with sales increasing +2.6% over the latest 12 weeks, ahead of Morrisons (+1.2%). Meanwhile, sales at Sainsbury’s and Asda were broadly flat over the same period.
Ocado (+16.8%) and M&S (+10.9%) continued to deliver double-digit growth, significantly outperforming the wider market, while Lidl also recorded strong sales growth of +6.7%.
The latest figures suggest that retailers offering a compelling combination of value, convenience and differentiated products remain well placed to capture shopper spending as the industry moves into the crucial festive trading period.
Mike Watkins, head of retailer and business insight at NielsenIQ, said: “There was improved growth in supermarket sales in October, helped by the half-term holidays and Halloween, which encouraged shoppers to spend more on special treats for the family. This is despite consumer confidence falling, suggesting shoppers are still willing to loosen the purse strings when there’s an occasion to celebrate.”
Watkins concluded: “Looking ahead, the industry needs to get shoppers in the mood to spend, so the launch of Christmas advertising campaigns will be important in showcasing what’s new, different, and, crucially, affordable. With Black Friday providing another focus for shoppers in November, we expect the acceleration in supermarket sales to begin in early December. Given the current momentum, we anticipate Total Till growth of around +2.5% to +3% this Christmas, as retailers look to make the most of the crucial final weeks of the year.”

items.title: La Plagne ski guide: Paradiski turns 65 with a new luxury chalet
items.summary: In 1961, the French Alps were in crisis: the traditional industries of agriculture and mining were shrinking and villages were depopulating as the young moved to find work in the cities. Dr Pierre Borrione, a former French Resistance fighter and the mayor of Aime, took a gamble, building two drag lifts in his town. Not [...]
items.body:
La Plagne ski guide: Paradiski turns 65 with a new luxury chalet
In 1961, the French Alps were in crisis: the traditional industries of agriculture and mining were shrinking and villages were depopulating as the young moved to find work in the cities. Dr Pierre Borrione, a former French Resistance fighter and the mayor of Aime, took a gamble, building two drag lifts in his town. Not only did he manage to reverse the Tarentaise Valley’s decline, but he set in motion the creation of what has become one of the largest and most popular ski areas in the world: Paradiski.
VIP Ski is marking this 65th anniversary season in style, opening Graciosa, a brand new ski-in, ski-out chalet development in La Plagne, Paradiski’s biggest resort. Set at a snow-sure 2,003m on the Mont St Sauveur piste, Stephanie Adams was among the first guests to check-in.
What to do in La Plagne
There are 225 km of runs at La Plagne, with another 200 km in connected resorts within the Paradiski area. 70% of these are at altitudes above 2,000 m so the powder is pretty much guaranteed.
To feel the wind on your face and get an adrenaline kick before you even click into your skis, take the Aérolive from Roche de Mio to Live 3,000. This is a gondola with two open-air cabins, L’Acrobate and La Funambule (meaning “tightrope walker”). Brace yourself if you are afraid of heights, as it’s more than a little daunting, but with no windows or walls to the cabins, you can lean out and experience a sensation that’s probably the closest you will ever get to flying. Aérolive departs every 15 minutes, as long as the weather is fair, and, reassuringly, passengers are clipped into a safety harness so you definitely won’t fall out!
One of the most scenic blue runs in La Plagne is accessible from the Plagne Bellecôte sector. It runs alongside the new Riders Nation snow park, where you can detour to try the four freestyle courses, and then down through forest to the villages of Montchavin and Les Coches. There are impressive views of Mont Blanc on the way.
Apres ski: La Folie Douce
Did you even visit Paradiski if you didn’t party at La Folie Douce? The Alps’ most famous apres ski venue is a Les Arcs institution, offering a festival-like atmosphere all winter long. New for this season is L’Atelier, a huge events space which changes purpose as the day goes on. Mornings are dedicated to sports, including indoor cycling; there are creative programmes for children in the afternoons; and in the evenings, the decks are open for amateur DJs to show the crowds what they’re made of.
L’Atelier’s offering complements La Folie Douce’s core events calendar, Unlimited Folie, which platforms the biggest DJs from Paris and Berlin, from international clubs to underground scenes. Dance until dawn – the shots will keep you warm – then grab an hour or two of sleep before catching the first lift of the day.
The world’s highest comedy festival
The Paradiski ski season runs until the end of April, so there’s still plenty of time to make an Easter booking. If you’re looking for a last-minute escape, plan your trip to coincide with Paradiski Comedy Club – the world’s highest stand-up comedy festival – from 16-27 February. Held in collaboration with Paris’ Metro Comedy Club, performers use the Vanoise Express cable car as their stage, delivering stand-up routines in English and French as you dangle 380m above the ground.
Where to stay in La Plagne: Graciosa
Get your gang together and book VIP Ski’s CLUB Sagarmatha Penthouse, which crowns the Graciosa and sleeps up to 15 guests. The chalet’s panoramic views stretch as far as Mont Blanc, and you can admire the snow-capped mountains and, later, the star-studded night sky from the private hot tub and sauna on the 6th floor terrace. The chef and chalet hosts will ensure your every need is taken care of, all you have to do is relax. Families can make use of Graciosa’s “Bear Cub” and nanny service, so you can be confident the kids are safe and well entertained as you take to the slopes and enjoy the subsequent apres ski.
Need to know
In February 2027, fully-catered accommodation at VIP Ski’s CLUB Sagarmatha Penthouse starts from £1,405 per person per week based on two sharing, including scheduled coach transfers from Geneva Airport. Book directly with VIP Ski (vip-chalets.com). A six-day adult ski pass for Paradiski costs £349 (en.la-plagne.com). For ski hire and ski school, visit Oxygene (oxygene.ski).

items.title: Football Leaks hacker who sparked Man City probe in talks with SFO over co-operation
items.summary: Rui Pinto, the Portuguese hacktivist whose Football Leaks prompted investigations into Manchester City, says he is in talks with British authorities over a co-operation deal. Pinto is seeking protection in exchange for helping to expose crime after being told at the height of the coverage of Manchester City’s bombshell financial cheating verdict that he will [...]
items.body:
Football Leaks hacker who sparked Man City probe in talks with SFO over co-operation
Rui Pinto, the Portuguese hacktivist whose Football Leaks prompted investigations into Manchester City, says he is in talks with British authorities over a co-operation deal.
Pinto is seeking protection in exchange for helping to expose crime after being told at the height of the coverage of Manchester City’s bombshell financial cheating verdict that he will be withdrawn from a witness safeguarding programme in his native Portugal.
He is being represented by feted French human rights lawyer William Bourdon, whose previous clients have included Edward Snowden and Julian Assange, the sources of other high-profile leaks.
“I can confirm that the process is under way,” Bourdon told The Guardian, which reported that the Serious Fraud Office had made contact with Pinto’s camp.
A Serious Fraud Office spokesperson told City AM: “In line with long established practice to avoid prejudice to law enforcement activity, we can neither confirm nor deny any investigation into this matter.”
It is understood that the SFO handles over 1,000 referrals a year and undertakes enquiries before deciding whether to progress to a formal investigation.
Pinto, 38, rose to prominence through Football Leaks, a website which obtained millions of secret documents about contracts relating to some of the game’s biggest clubs and players, including Real Madrid, Paris Saint-Germain, City, Cristiano Ronaldo and Neymar.
How Manchester City case traces back to Rui Pinto
He later collaborated with European media outlets including Der Spiegel to publish further materials, including those that sparked investigations by Uefa and the Premier League into Manchester City’s sponsorship agreements and contracts.
Pinto was arrested in Hungary in 2019 by Portuguese authorities and extradited. He was found guilty of five counts of cybercrime and handed a four-year suspended prison sentence. His supporters describe him as a whistleblower; his critics as a hacker or criminal.
He was told in late September that his six years in witness protection were coming to an end. He said he feared for his safety and is still appealing the decision.
Days earlier, Manchester City were found guilty on more than 100 counts of breaking the Premier League’s financial rules during a nine-year period from 2009 to 2018.
An independent commission accused the club of hiding more than £900m of contributions from their Abu Dhabi ownership as sponsorship income from related parties.
Manchester City have always denied wrongdoing and have appealed the findings. They face relegation, a huge financial penalty and, potentially, a forced sale of the club, if the guilty verdicts are upheld.

items.title: Boux Avenue sales rise 16% as EBITDA reaches £5m
items.summary: Lingerie retailer Boux Avenue has reported a 16 per cent increase in sales for the year to March 2026, with double-digit growth across its stores and online channels. The Theo Paphitis-owned retailer generated EBITDA of £5m during the financial year, with like-for-like sales increasing by 10.5 per cent across its stores and 14.9 per cent...
items.body:
Lingerie retailer Boux Avenue has reported a 16 per cent increase in sales for the year to March 2026, with double-digit growth across its stores and online channels.
The Theo Paphitis-owned retailer generated EBITDA of £5m during the financial year, with like-for-like sales increasing by 10.5 per cent across its stores and 14.9 per cent online.
The performance follows continued investment in its product ranges, marketing and physical estate, with the retailer crediting its design and buying strategy for improvements in sell-through rates and margins.
New collections across lingerie, nightwear, swimwear and accessories helped drive customer engagement, with active customer numbers increasing by 6 per cent year on year.
Boux Avenue also reported a 13 per cent increase in sales to students, while sales among customers aged 35 and over rose by 9 per cent. The latter growth was attributed to campaigns including its Spring Icons Lingerie and Summer Swimwear collections.
Its third-party retail partnerships also delivered double-digit growth, with sales increasing across platforms including Next, Marks & Spencer, Very and ASOS.
Alongside its digital expansion, the retailer continued to invest in its UK store estate. This included relocating its northern flagship to a larger unit at Manchester’s Trafford Centre and moving to a new location within Liverpool ONE.
It also refurbished stores at Bluewater, Westfield White City, Guildford and Belfast.
Boux Avenue currently operates 27 stores across the UK and is exploring further locations in Edinburgh, Bristol, Nottingham and Leeds.
Chairman and owner Theo Paphitis said the results reflected the brand’s progress in recent years, adding that the business was looking to expand through existing channels and partnerships, as well as pursue further international collaborations.
Founded in 2011, Boux Avenue sells lingerie, nightwear and swimwear through its stores, website and retail partnerships, including John Lewis and TikTok Shop.
The latest performance follows a 6.9 per cent increase in sales in the year to March 2025, when EBITDA reached £6.4m.

items.title: SGF Annual Conference 2026 to celebrate the vital role of convenience retailers
items.summary: The Scottish Grocers’ Federation (SGF) Annual Conference 2026 will bring together leading industry figures, retailers and business partners to explore the future of convenience retailing, under the theme ‘Customer & Community: More Than a Store!’ Hosted by Scottish broadcaster Rona Dougall, the conference will feature… This story continues at SGF Annual Conference 2026 to celebrate the vital role of convenience retailers Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Hosted by Scottish broadcaster Rona Dougall, the conference will feature an outstanding line-up of speakers and contributors, including cabinet secretary for economy, tourism & transport Stephen Flynn MSP, alongside industry experts and prominent retailers.
The event will provide an important opportunity for the convenience retailing sector to come together, share insight, discuss the challenges and opportunities facing the industry, and celebrate the vital contribution independent and multiple convenience retailers make to communities across Scotland.
It takes place on 18 December at Doubletree by Hilton, 36 Cambridge St, Glasgow, 8:30am – 4pm.
A key highlight of this year’s conference will be the announcement of the appointment of Co-op operations director Kate McCrae as the next vice president of the trade association’s National Executive Board.
McCrae’s appointment marks a significant milestone for SGF, as she becomes the first female vice president in the Federation’s history.
Following two years in the role, she will go on to become SGF’s first female president, representing an important moment for the organisation and the wider convenience retailing industry.
The conference programme will combine business updates and sector insight with a series of interactive sessions featuring the UK Deposit Return Scheme DMO, Exchange for Change, Bobby’s Foods, The Knowledge Bank and Allwyn.
Pete Cheema, chief executive of the Scottish Grocers’ Federation, said: “The SGF Annual Conference is always a hugely important opportunity to bring our industry together, celebrate the contribution of convenience retailers and look ahead to the opportunities and challenges facing our sector.
“This year’s theme, ‘Customer & Community: More Than a Store!’, perfectly reflects the role that convenience stores play in communities across Scotland. Our retailers are much more than places to shop, they are at the heart of local communities, providing essential services, supporting local economies and responding every day to the changing needs of their customers.
“I’m particularly delighted to welcome Kate McCrae as our incoming vice president. Her appointment is a significant moment for SGF and I’m incredibly proud that she will become the first female president of the Federation in two years’ time.
“It is a fantastic milestone, and I look forward to working closely with Kate as she takes on this important leadership role.
“We have an excellent programme lined up for 2026, with a fantastic range of speakers, contributors and interactive sessions. I’m looking forward to welcoming colleagues from across the industry for what promises to be an engaging, informative and enjoyable day.”
The theme, ‘Customer & Community: More Than a Store!’, will run throughout the day, highlighting how convenience retailers continue to adapt, innovate and respond to changing customer expectations while playing an increasingly important role in the communities they serve.
Through these sessions, delegates will have the opportunity to hear directly from key industry organisations and business partners, gain valuable practical knowledge and explore developments that will shape the future of convenience retailing.

items.title: M&S investors get an early Christmas present as it doubles shareholder payout
items.summary: The retailer last week launched its Christmas campaign with James Norton and Amandaland star Lucy Punch after reporting a rebound in profits.
items.body:
M&S investors get an early Christmas present as it doubles shareholder payout
M&S investors are cheering an early Christmas as the retailer doubled its shareholder payouts after a bumper year.
The high street giant, which has hundreds of thousands of armchair investors, will raise its full year dividend from 4.2p to 8.4p.
It follows a surge in food sales to £5.1billion in the second half of the year, a 13.9 per cent increase from the previous year, with the retailer primed for an 'unforgettable' festive season.
The retailer last week launched its Christmas campaign with James Norton and Amandaland star Lucy Punch after reporting a rebound in profits.
The retailer has mostly recovered from last year's cyber attack, reporting half-year profits of £335.1million for the 26 weeks to September 26, from £3.4million a year earlier.
M&S launched its Christmas advert (pictured) after reporting a recovery in profits
It now plans 'mid-to-high single-digit sales growth' in the medium term, with ambitions for profit growth profits ahead of sales.
In an update ahead of a capital markets day for investors and analysts today, M&S said it aimed to double food sales, build its international footprint, and increase the online share of its fashion, home and beauty range to 50 per cent of its total sales.
Shares in M&S rose 3.45 per cent, bringing this year's gains to 37.9 per cent.
Boss Stuart Machin last week flagged a slower recovery for its clothing and beauty business, which had faced the 'long tail impact' of the hack with disruption to selected core lines.
He also admitted 'we felt we left money on the table' after some customers complained about there not being enough summer dresses with sleeves, while viral products sold out too quickly.
Figures published by Worldpanel by Numerator today showed M&S increased grocery sales by 14.6 per cent in the 12 weeks to November 1, the biggest increase of all major supermarkets.
It came as food inflation rose slightly to 2.6 per cent in the four weeks to November 1, after slowing over the summer.
Fraser McKevitt, head of retail and consumer insight at Worldpanel, said the 'direction of travel has changed.'
He added: 'Household budgets have already taken a hit after the latest increase to the energy price cap arrived with the cold weather in October, and shoppers will be keeping a close eye on prices at the tills this winter.'
That has not stopped consumers stocking up on essentials after the launch of the government's 'Be Ready' public awareness campaign, encouraging households to prepare for up to three days of disruption.
Hand sanitiser sales increased by 83 per cent compared to the previous year, while sales of bottled water and tinned and jarred goods rose 67 per cent and 37 per cent, respectively.

items.title: Brits are cutting back this Christmas and Black Friday will struggle to change their minds
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. Nearly one in three British shoppers (31%) are planning to cut back on spending this year as the cost-of-living crisis takes its toll on disposable income, according to new research from brand research agency Hall & Partners. Presents are the first thing consumers are looking to save money on, with 39% saying they can’t afford […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Nearly one in three British shoppers (31%) are planning to cut back on spending this year as the cost-of-living crisis takes its toll on disposable income, according to new research from brand research agency Hall & Partners.
Presents are the first thing consumers are looking to save money on, with 39% saying they can’t afford to spend as much on gifts this Christmas. Instead, nearly half of all shoppers, 46%, are going to prioritise experience over gifts as they look forward to catching up with friends and family over the festive season.
Traditionally, Black Friday deals are deployed by retailers to persuade cautious shoppers to loosen their purse strings but, this year, there’s a clear cynicism to promotions.
Among those spending less on Christmas this year, one in five now believe Black Friday sales do not represent good value. A mere 4% of cost cutting consumers believe Black Friday deals always offer good value.
Consumers are a little more trusting in general deals and promotions, but only just. Of those cutting back, only one in four think promotions can be good deals and 10% are convinced they do not represent good value.
When it comes to paying for Christmas this year, 37% will use disposable income while 29% tell us they will use savings. The cost of Christmas will be spread over several months by 12% of consumers relying on using credit cards and 10% by using Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL).
Farid Jeeawody, senior vice president at Hall & Partners believes the research reflects how people no longer see Black Friday as a novel, exciting discounting period.
“People still believe in the joy of Christmas, but the magic of Black Friday deals is starting to lose its sparkle,” he said.
“At a time when consumers are cutting back on gifting and prioritising experiences there is a huge opportunity to tap into the emotions that brand experiences can create.
“Experience led categories such as travel and entertainment, we believe, are the most resilient to cost-cutting because they bring consumers something to look forward to and offer shared joy. Brands can learn from this and double down on the physical and digital experiences that bring connection, joy and value to consumers such as an immersive product experience, combining food and drink for a themed meal or an online digital advent calendar.”

Following a competitive review process, The Brookfield Group… This story continues at Brookfield extends Co-op Wholesale contract Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
The extension reinforces the businesses’ existing 15-year relationship and supporting Brookfield Group’s continued growth ambitions across its six-store estate in Yorkshire and Lancashire.
Following a competitive review process, The Brookfield Group has chosen to extend its partnership with Co-op Wholesale, while gradually transitioning its store estate to the new Nisa fascia. The stores will also undergo internal refits to modernise their appearance and further enhance the shopping experience for customers.
The partnership will enable The Brookfield Group to continue offering customers competitive pricing, access to the Co-op brand range and a wider choice of products.
Alongside its investment in retail, The Brookfield Group said it remains committed to supporting local communities through Nisa’s Making a Difference Locally (MADL) charity initiative, which helps independent retailers make charitable donations and support worthwhile causes in the communities they serve.
Paul Webster, partnerships and sales director at Co-op Wholesale, said: “We’re delighted to be extending our partnership with Brookfield Group for a further five years.
“Over the course of our existing relationship, we’ve worked closely together to support the business as it has continued to grow, and this extension reflects the strength of that partnership.
“The decision to transition the estate to the new Nisa fascia demonstrates Brookfield Group’s confidence in the proposition we offer. We’re excited to continue working alongside Umar and his team as they build on their success over the coming years.”
Umar Patel, director at Brookfield Group, said: “We’ve been a Nisa customer for over 15 years – throughout that time we’ve built a strong working relationship based on trust, reliability and mutual support.
“As an independent retailer, we understand the pressures facing households in the current economic climate. Our priority has always been to offer our customers quality products at competitive prices, without compromising on service or convenience.
“By continuing our partnership with Co-op Wholesale, we believe we’re well placed to deliver on that commitment, benefiting from its competitive wholesale proposition, extensive product range and the strength of the Co-op brand. The convenience retail market is extremely competitive, and we took the opportunity to review all our options.
“Ultimately, we felt that continuing with a company we’ve worked alongside for over 15 years was the right decision. Good business relationships are built over time, and we value the support and understanding Nisa has shown our business throughout that period.
“We’re pleased to commit to a further five years with Co-op Wholesale. This partnership gives us the confidence to continue investing in our business, keeping our prices competitive and delivering the value and service our customers expect, particularly during these challenging economic times.”

items.title: Shoppers stock up following government advice, but no panic buying
items.summary: Take-home sales at the grocers increased by 2.2% in the four weeks to 1 November 2026 compared with a year ago, according to the latest data from Worldpanel by Numerator. Like-for-like grocery price inflation remains relatively subdued but rose slightly to 2.6%, up from 2.5%… This story continues at Shoppers stock up following government advice, but no panic buying Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Like-for-like grocery price inflation remains relatively subdued but rose slightly to 2.6%, up from 2.5% in the previous four weeks.
Fraser McKevitt, head of retail and consumer insight at Worldpanel by Numerator, said: “Grocery price inflation continued to increase after slowing over the summer. While prices are rising at a slower rate than at the beginning of the year, the direction of travel has changed.
“Household budgets have already taken a hit after the latest increase to the energy price cap arrived with the cold weather in October, and shoppers will be keeping a close eye on prices at the tills this winter.”
Sales of essential supplies jumped in the ten days from 22 October after the launch of the government’s ‘Be Ready’ public awareness campaign, which encourages households to prepare for up to three days in the event of disruption to essential services.
In the ten days after the campaign was launched, sales of hand sanitiser increased by 83% compared to the corresponding period last year, with sales of bottled water (+67%) and tinned and jarred goods (+37%) also rising.
The number of people buying tinned meat each day after the launch of the campaign rose by 43%, equivalent to an extra 400,000 shoppers a day, yet the typical amount bought remained at around 500g in terms of pack size.
McKevitt added: “Shoppers clearly took notice of the ‘Be Ready’ campaign, but this wasn’t panic buying, with less than a third of households buying bottled water in October.
“Growth came from more people adding the recommended items on the government’s checklist to their weekly shop, not from shoppers piling their trolleys high, which is very much in line with what the government wanted households to do.”
Over the month of October, 3.3 million households purchased a pumpkin, with the number sold up 10% year on year.
The average price paid for a pumpkin stood at £1.20, 12% lower than last year, providing some small but welcome relief for shoppers looking to celebrate Halloween.
Tubs of sugar confectionery were the standout ‘trick or treat’ performer, with sales up by 28% compared to last year.
