items.title: The 78 must-have toys this Christmas for every age group and budget - as picked by John Lewis, Amazon and children's gift experts
items.summary: What do you get children, grandchildren, nieces, nephews and kids of friends that they don't already have?
items.body:
The 78 must-have toys this Christmas for every age group and budget - as picked by John Lewis, Amazon and children's gift experts
Daily Mail journalists select and curate the products that feature on our site. If you make a purchase via links on this page we will earn commission - learn more
Christmas is fast approaching – and with it the panic of buying presents, especially for the little ones in your life.
What do you get children, grandchildren, nieces, nephews and kids of friends that seemingly already have it all? Well, we've got the answer with our comprehensive, curated gift guide.
We've asked the best retail minds at Hamleys, John Lewis, Amazon, Argos, The Entertainer and an expert panel at industry body CIJ to tell us the hottest presents and trends for this festive season.
They have each picked out toys they believe will be big sellers this Christmas – and we have categorised them into age groups, making it easy for you to pick out the perfect gift. All price points are catered for – with gifts from just a few pounds to more than £400.
We have also highlighted toys picked by more than one of the retail experts – making them a star buy.
Alongside that, as a parent of two daughters who heavily encourages playtime away from screens, I've put in a few personal picks too.
We also unboxed many of the toys to see the quality and show you what they look like outside of the packaging.
Whether you want to blow the budget or buy something small – but guaranteed to produce a smile on Christmas morning regardless – we have you covered.
Christmas sorted: We've curated a list of star buys from a range of top retailers
Unboxed: Some of the recommended toys our team took a closer look at for the guide
What are the trends this Christmas?
The hot trend this year, according to John Lewis, is families swapping screen time for play time.
This means collaborative building, role play, imaginative storytelling and outdoor adventures are the key themes this year. Think premium toys made to last.
Meanwhile, Argos predicts a shift towards retro-inspired toys but also favourites from the big screen – think KPop Demon Hunters, Paw Patrol and Toy Story 5.
The Entertainer too has highlighted nostalgic comebacks as a strong theme, alongside interactive toys, viral sensations and toys that stand the test of time.
Hamleys says there is a growing trend for 'persona play', where toys aren't defined by what they do, but by the figure at their centre – essentially, inviting children in, handing them a persona and letting them build their own stories and adventures…
Perfect toys for toddlers
1. STAR BUY: Peppa Pig Ready Pedal Peppa
Picked by three of the experts, this interactive figure reacts with 75 sounds and phrases, depending on how she's used. Suitable for toddlers over three.
Picked by: Argos, The Entertainer and Hamleys
Oink: This activity toy comes with a range of accessories including a detatachable stick handle, helmet and a sheet of stickers to personalise Peppa's bike
2. Wooden Breakfast in Bed Set by John Lewis
John Lewis says this will spark 'imaginative family role play' tapping into a growing desire for 'slow morning'. Suitable from the age of two.
Picked by: John Lewis
Exclusively at John Lewis, it says these plush toys reflect a wider shift towards choosing value over volume and make a perfect 'heirloom nursery piece'. Suitable from birth.
Picked by: John Lewis
4. Chad Valley Alfie and Jo Wooden Train Set
This train set brings Alfie & Joe (two Argos hedgehog mascots) into the world of play with easy connect tracks and smooth-rolling carriages. Suitable from the age of two.
Picked by: Argos
5. Chad Valley Wooden Classic Kitchen
A wooden kitchen has been a staple in the Boyce household for many years – and this one from Argos is a great choice to spark imaginative play. Suitable for over the age of three.
Picked by: Argos
6. Early Learning Centre Wooden Kitchen
Another wooden kitchen makes a list – but this one is double the price. It comes with a little pretend microwave and gold taps. Suitable for over the age of three.
Picked by: The Entertainer
7. Paw Patrol The Dino Movie Megasaurus Dino Vehicle
This vehicle features sounds from the film and a 76.2cm dinosaur that automatically inflates at the press of a button. Suitable for over the age of three.
Picked by: Argos
8. Goodnight You, Goodnight Everyone Book
This personalised book makes the child the star – you can add up to seven names to the book so they can say goodnight to the special people in their life. Suitable from birth.
Picked by: CIJ
This wooden lighthouse comes complete with a wooden lighthouse keeper, seagull, seal, dolphin, fish, crab, stone and seaweed – to let imaginations run wild. Suitable for over the age of three.
Picked by: CIJ
10. Movers and Shakers Soft Toy
These interactive soft toys are the perfect faux pet. They come in the form of a West Highland Terrier, Golden Retriever, Husky and a black and white cat. Suitable from 18 months old.
Picked by: Hamleys
Adorable: These plushies are interactive; they walk, sit and beg while making cat or dog noises noises triggered by movement
11. Hamleys Wooden London Taxi
Bring a piece of London charm into your home with this taxi – perfect for little hands to push and pull. Suitable for ages over 12 months.
Picked by: Hamleys
Quintessential London: The iconic black cab comes in play form in this adorable wooden taxi with a removeable roof that reveals four cute passengers
12. Maped Jumbo Infinity Coloured Pencils 12 Colours
We discovered these on a holiday in France and bought them upon our return. They are so much better than crayons and regular pencils for toddlers – my two-year-old uses them every day. A bargain. Suitable for toddlers.
Picked by: Lee
13. Disney Darlings Minnie Mouse Feature Doll
This interactive doll makes sounds and responds to a magic wand. Each character comes with a character-themed outfit, headband and sparkly eyes. Suitable for ages over two years.
Picked by: Amazon
Each inspired by a classic Disney character, these baby dolls come with their own themed accessories, including a birth certificate and magic wand
Perfect toys for ages 3-5
14. Le Toy Van Paddington Doll's House
We have had a wooden Le Toy Van doll's house for many years in our home – they stand the test of time (and toddlers). This Paddington special comes as classic dollshouses make a comeback.
Picked by: John Lewis
15. Micro Scooter Gruffalo Scooter and accessories
Micro Scooters have also been a staple in our household – and this new themed one comes to ride the wave of Gruffalo mania, after the launch of the new book Gruffalo Granny in September.
Picked by: John Lewis
16. Hot Wheels City Ultimate T-Rex Garage
Hot Wheels are always hot with kids – and this mega playset packs storage for 50 cars in a showdown against a car-hungry dino, complete with two 1:64 scale vehicles.
Picked by: Argos
17. LLP My Magical Dragon Skye
This new interactive dragon from Little Live Pets features 60 interactive reactions and an integrated LCD screen that rewards caring for the little creature.
Picked by: Argos
18. Vtech Kidi 12-in-1 Guitar Superstar
Complete with dazzling light-up frets, touch-sensitive strings, Bluetooth music streaming and rhythm challenges, this could be the gateway toy to turning your child into the next Jimi Hendrix or Slash.
Picked by: Argos
19. Jupiter Workshops Four Storey Wooden Doll House
Another wooden doll house makes this list, but at half the price of the John Lewis one above. This one is four-storey and comes with sounds and lights.
Picked by: Argos
20. Flutter Monster 40cm Soft Toy
This toy is a gentle way for children to talk about their emotions, according to Argos. It has four butterflies tucked into its tummy – each with a pocket for a feeling note card to write or draw emotions.
Picked by: Argos
21. Toy Story 5 Bullseye Jumbo Plush
This giant plush is a must-have for any Toy Story fan – and could make the perfect companion for snuggling up to in bed.
Picked by: Argos
22. Minions & Monsters Fart Blaster Pro
Armed with eight stink settings and two scented formulas, this movie tie-in with Minions & Monsters might drive you a bit mad, launching real floating scent rings up to 6ft away. One to gift to a relative, maybe!
Picked by: Argos
23. FurReal Gabby The Grow and Roar Tiger Interactive Pet
This has been a frequent sell-out since launching this year, the toy responds to love and care with more than 100 combinations of sounds and movements. The Entertainer says she feels more like a real furry friend than a traditional toy.
Picked by: The Entertainer
24. Bluey Muffin's Home Playset
This two-level playset encourages imaginative storytelling – and if the children in your life are anything like mine, they love this little Australian family of dogs!
Picked by: The Entertainer (exclusive)
This toy has been earmarked as the number one pick by a panel at CIJ. Young children can build and explore basic structures through the magnatiles, while also learning numbers and letter recognition.
Picked by: CIJ
26. Playmobil Space ESA Mars Research Rocket
This modular rocket with launch pad and two astronauts is perfect for any little space lover in your life. Comes with 71 pieces.
Picked by: Amazon
27. A Playful Day with Bluey: Tonieplay
This turns eight favourite Bluey episodes into screen-free, interactive audio adventures for children and also includes mini games. You'll need a Toniebox 2 (£100) to use it.
Picked by: CIJ
28. Pikachu Pokémon Holiday Plush – 10 ½ inches
Kids are Pokémon mad again, with trading cards selling for big bucks. This plush is perfect for any fan of the Japanese franchise.
Picked by: CIJ
29. Thunder Unicorn
This remote-controlled toy struts, glows and gallops with special effects – an exciting gift for any horse or unicorn-obsessed child you know.
Picked by: Hamleys
Magic: The unicorn itself was made of a foam but its 0.1g weight means it has no trouble getting - and staying - off the ground
30. Play-Doh Stamp and Spin Pizza Playset
Play-Doh is another staple in our home (even I'm often picking it out of my fingernails for hours after!) This version comes with five tubs of modelling dough and a pretend pizza oven that twirls out a pretend crust. Comes with eight tools for cutting, rolling and shaping.
Picked by: Hamleys
Easy assembly: The Play-Doh was ready to play with moments after unboxing. It has a bunch of stamps and stencils to make pizzas and a cute box to 'serve' them in
31. Numberblocks Sing and Record Music Player
This device has 15 sounds and songs and blends learning with fun. A built-in microphone records up to 90 seconds of singing for playback, and five character buttons teach counting, colours and shapes.
Picked by: Hamleys
Inspired by the maths learning TV show, Numberblocks, this colourful little gadget already comes with bartteries so it can be enjoyed the moment it's unwrapped
With 171 pieces of electronic 3D track including colourful track cubes, traffic accessories and a USB-chargeable train, it encourages creativity and logical thinking.
Picked by: Hamleys
We're big fans of board games – my eldest daughter and I are often busting out the Monopoly, Junior Cluedo and Family Trivial Pursuit. This game, however, is a great first board game for five and up, with the rules simple but the jeopardy providing plenty of fun and replay.
Picked by: Lee
34. Disney Yuyus Wave 3 Winnie The Pooh Blind Box Vinyl Plush
Blind boxes are big business, and these ones are expected to sell like hotcakes according to Amazon. There are nine plush keyrings to collect – they are around 10cm and you don’t know which character you will get.
Picked by: Amazon
Perfect toys for ages 6-8
35. STAR BUY: Primal Hatch Megalodon Hatching Egg Shark Toy
Drop the oversized egg into its tank, pour in water and await a 40cm Megalodon shark smash through – it's the follow-up to the big seller last year, the hatching dino.
Picked by: Argos, The Entertainer and Hamleys
36. STAR BUY: KPop Demon Hunters Golden Singing Dolls (Rumi, Mira, Zoey)
Bringing the Netflix phenomenon to life, these dolls from the film sing smash-hit Golden. Buy all three and they sync up for a full group harmony.
Picked by: Argos and John Lewis
37. Marvin's Magic Treasured Tricks Wooden Set
My eldest is magic obsessed (a local magician invited us to the Magic Circle to watch a show last year). Her gateway was a Marvin's Magic set, and this wooden version can help build confidence through imaginative role play.
Picked by: John Lewis
38. Pokémon TCG: Mega Moonlit Tin
These vastly popular sets sell out quick, so if they come in stock, you’ll have to act quickly. The tin includes one foil promo card featuring Mega Gengar ex.
Picked by: Amazon
39. Plus-Plus Learn To Build Space Superset
This set lets children (and adults) build an entire universe, from simple 2D shapes to advanced 3D models like rockets, planets, astronauts and aliens. It comes with 1,000 pieces, baseplates, wheels and hubs.
Picked by: John Lewis
40. Connetix Ball Run Launcher
We love a marble run in our home – and this version adds a kinetic twist to construction, perfect for experimenting with gravity and design.
Picked by: John Lewis
41. Toniebox Lite
This screen-free storytelling device comes in a smaller, portable edition, with six hours of audio stories and music.
Picked by: Argos
42. Lego Pokemon Smart Play: Sprigatito, Fuecoco and Quaxly Battle
Another Pokemon product in the list, this starter kit features buildable figures with movable parts and smart tags, which trigger responsive lights and sound effects.
Picked by: Argos
43. Star Wars Action Buddy Grogu 25-cm Animatronic, Interactive Plush
Star Wars is still an incredibly popular franchise, as parents spread their love for the fictional universe. This 25cm plush has 50 sound and action combinations.
Picked by: Amazon
Star toys: This buddy Grogu was unexpectedly endearing. Press its head to trigger movements, sounds and play modes or lay him for a nap complete with snoozing sounds
44. Pokémon Battle Action Pikachu
Oh look, Pokemon again. This figure has touch sensors, a light-up tail alongside unique sounds and movements.
Picked by: The Entertainer
45. Armosaurs Armor-Up Dinosaur T-Rex, Ajax
This figure comes with seven interchangeable armour pieces and is sure to be a hit for any dino-loving child.
Picked by: Argos
My girls love crafting, and my eldest has asked for a badge maker for years (we're yet to buckle). This version comes with an app to customise templates and turn personal photos into custom pins.
Picked by: Argos
47. Starbox Nook Nooks Series 1 Blind Box Collectible
Another blind box. Each Nook Nook includes a unique miniature home that lights up. Designs range from retro TVs and washing machines to clocks and computers.
Picked by: Amazon
48. Clickeez Bubble Pops Keyboard Mega Mystery Figure Pack
My daughter has mucked around with these Clickeez sensory things for a while. They click and clack like a real keyboard (or typewriter if you prefer). They are a social media sensation and the sort of toy you get pestered for but will never understand why.
Picked by: The Entertainer
49. Santa's Express Train Set by Hornby
Mention Hornby, and dad or grandad might get a little misty-eyed. This lovely set can go underneath your Christmas tree and is sure to keep any train buff satisfied.
Picked by: CIJ
50. Kitsound HD Digital Camera, BM Stores
At the bargain price of £20, this camera offers 4K Ultra HD with a flip screen to take selfies with an 8x digital zoom. This little camera packs a punch and comes with a 256MB memory card.
Picked by: CIJ
51. Barbie in the Nutcracker Clara Doll and Sugar Plum Doll
This Barbie comes in a shimmering tutu and glittering tiara – perfect for any dance lovers in your family.
Picked by: Hamleys
From Barbies to Dr Doom. This 15cm Marvel figure comes with 20 movable joints and is the perfect collector's item.
Picked by: Hamleys
Marvellous: This Doctor Doom action figure features a cape that fans out, light up chest and face as well as a projectile launcher from his hand
53. Scorpix RC Transforming Car
This sports car comes with LED head and tail lights, and compact wheels for precision turning. It transforms into a scorpion at the touch of a button and smoke is released from underneath. It can be driven in car or scorpion mode with a remote control distance of 25 meters.
Picked by: Hamleys
54. Hatsune Miku T-Most PVC Figure
This virtual superstar is a 'vocaloid'. Yep, you can catch her in concert next month in London – but she doesn't actually exist. This model captures her signature look.
Picked by: Hamleys
Hamleys says this is the season's hottest trend – these small squeezy toys come in dozens of shapes. Duck, Fortune Cookie, Ghost, Croissant and Pig, just to name a few.
Picked by: Hamleys
Hot and squishy trend: These sensory toys were a bit bigger than we expected at around 22cm but are great fun squeeze and play with
My daughter picked up the rules of Uno at five, but doesn't realise it's a fun way of learning maths and numbers (sssh!). Our Mario version of Uno has travelled the world. We've now gone onto a harder number-based game as she is seven – Skip Bo – and we're loving it! Perfect stocking filler.
Picked by: Lee
Uno is incredibly popular in the Boyce household, and this spin on it is for those who have mastered the regular version and want to mix it up.
Picked by: Amazon
58. Schleich Horse Club – 110Pc Horse Camping Playset with car
Ideal for any horse lovers in your life, this set Includes fully poseable Hannah and her dad, Quarter Horse figure Cayenne, SUV, trailer, tent, fencing and fun accessories for horse-powered adventures.
Picked by: Amazon
Perfect toys for ages 9-11
59. STAR BUY: Mini Brands Really Works Vinyl Playset
These have been out for a few months; this mini record player can play tiny vinyls sold separately in 'surprise' mini vinyl capsules. Fun to collect, delightful, and they actually play music.
Picked by: Argos and The Entertainer
60. Lego Icons 10361 Winter Village Collection Holiday Express Train
Exclusive to John Lewis, this Lego set could be a fun build for old and young alike over the Christmas period.
Picked by: John Lewis
Listen, we're big karaoke fans in our household and have a Vtech karaoke machine which, to be honest, is great. You can cast your favourite music apps directly onto walls while singing. One of those – 'yeah, I bought it for the kids, but bust it out once they're in bed with a couple of wines' type presents.
Picked by: Argos
62. Lexibook, ELO-StarCAM, AI Digital Camera
This is a camera with an extra feature. Users can take a picture and choose an expert guide to explain discoveries through Artificial Intelligence object recognition.
Picked by: Amazon
63. Lego Botanicals Rocking Plants Construction Set
More Lego. This time, a buildable plant that doubles up as home decor. These two are pastel-coloured plants – a delosperma named Lumi and an echeveria named Ellie. It's a surefire way to keep a child busy for a few hours during a build.
Picked by: The Entertainer and Amazon
Keeping it classic: These cute botanical Lego sets had a manageable number of pieces and the instructions seemed easy to follow, too
64. 3D Puzzle Vase by Ravensburger
Picked out as a must-buy by the CIJ expert panel, this jigsaw has a practical use – it can really be used as a vase, meaning it's labelled as very 'good value'.
Picked by: CIJ
65. KPop Demon Hunters Derpy Glow Cosplay Crossbody Bagbu Loungefly
Another KPop Demon Hunters entry. This bag is pricey and a little freaky, but could be the perfect 'wow' gift for a superfan.
Picked by: CIJ
66. The Best of Christmas Game by Tomy
This festive family trivia board game sees two teams race to decorate their Christmas trees by answering holiday-themed questions.
Picked by: CIJ
Another numbers card game on the list, although for this one you need a minimum of three players. Again, perfect for those who have mastered Uno and Skip Bo! This is a spin-off version from its main base game.
Picked by: Amazon
68. Asteroid Electric Go Kart by Wilton Bradley Ltd
This battery-powered Go Kart could be the gadget to inspire your new child to become the new Lewis Hamilton or Jackie Stewart.
Picked by: CIJ
69. Articulate Under Pressure
This new twist on the classic party game could be perfect light relief after that heavy Christmas dinner – you have to describe words as quickly as you can.
Picked by: Hamleys
Christmas games sorted: A new take on a beloved boardgame ups the stakes. This version has new twists, turns and rewards with three different game modes
70. Flashforge AD5X 3D Printer
My nephew, 11, begged my brother-in-law for a 3D printer for his birthday earlier in the summer. He got this model and has had it for a few months. They both say it's great. You'll need to buy filaments to print with separately – and often have to pay to download designs.
Picked by: Lee
Perfect toys for over 12s
71. Mattel Brick Shop Hot Wheels Lamborghini Miura P400 SV Building Toy Kit
Picked by: Amazon
Build a luxury supercar – it's a 1:12 scale Lamborghini Miura P400 SV loaded with realistic details and including metal parts. It has 1,523 pieces, so will take some patience.
On your marks: There were almost 30 bags of pieces in this Hot Wheels car-builder set - plus mini headlights, a steering wheel and real rubber tyres. Hours (or even days) of amusement
72. STAR BUY: Meccano Pro Limited Edition Aston Martin Aramco Formula 1 Construction Set
This new 1:8 scale Aston Martin F1 set combines the classic appeal of Meccano with the huge newfound popularity of motor racing. Featuring 1,203 real metal parts, two tools and 15 hours building time, it could be a great Christmas project.
Picked by: The Entertainer (exclusive) and CIJ
73. Momiji's Sugar Plum Wood Message Dolls
Children can hide personalised messages inside and swap between siblings and friends – John Lewis says these will be popular, thanks to the trend of blind-box collectables. You don't know what design you're going to get.
Picked by: John Lewis
74. Lego Donkey Kong Arcade Building Set
You can create a Donkey Kong arcade level featuring Jumpman (later to be Super Mario), Donkey Kong figure and Lady (later to be Princess Peach). Pull the lever to release one of the 21 barrels at a time and you can make Jumpman jump over the barrels with a joystick. This one might go on my own personal Christmas list (I'm 39).
Picked by: Argos
75. Star Wars Sith Lightsaber Umbrella by Menkind
Look, an umbrella isn't exactly a toy or the most exciting Christmas gift, but sometimes, a practical but fun present is what a sulky teenager needs – and this Star Wars one fits the bill.
Picked by: CIJ
76. Miko: Self-Moving AI Chess Set by Menkind
The priciest gift on the list, I'd say check reviews and watch YouTube videos to ensure you know exactly what you're getting with this. Could be the perfect way to train up a new chess Grand Master though.
Picked by: CIJ
Doctor Doom gets a second showing here – and again, picked by Hamleys. It says the Christmas 'kidult' trend continues and this Lego version allows you to assemble a display piece.
Picked by: Hamleys
78. Switch 2 + The Legend of Zelda
While screentime is kept to a minimum in Casa Boyce, my eldest and I often have a little Switch time at the weekends. Currently, we love playing Super Mario Party Jamboree (perfect for Christmas family multi-player fun, £37.95), Mario Kart 8 (£37.99) and an old favourite of mine growing up... Rollercoaster Tycoon (£18.99), where you build and run virtual theme parks. This newest Switch is an upgrade on the original – and with a new Zelda game, the perfect combo.
Picked by: Lee

items.title: Pip & Nut partners with Bio&Me to launch Peanut Butter Granola
items.summary: Pip & Nut has partnered with gut health brand Bio&Me to launch a Peanut Butter Granola, which is set to exclusively launch across 803 Tesco stores from 16 November 2026.…
items.body:
Pip & Nut partners with Bio&Me to launch Peanut Butter Granola
Pip & Nut has partnered with gut health brand Bio&Me to launch a Peanut Butter Granola, which is set to exclusively launch across 803 Tesco stores from 16 November 2026.
This move aims to add more variety to the breakfast aisle and was designed to make it easier for shoppers to add more plant diversity to their diets.
The new product is vegan-friendly and contains nine plant-based foods, including wholegrain oats, dates, linseeds, sunflower seeds, carrots and extra virgin olive oil.
According to the business, each serving offers 9g of fibre and 13g of protein as the brands aim to cater to changing consumer preferences.
Pip Murray, Pip & Nut founder, said: Peanut Butter & Granola have always been a good match, a bit like Bio&Me and Pip & Nut. We both believe in using real ingredients for real flavour, and that tasty food shouldn’t come at a compromise.
Subscribe to Grocery Gazette for free
Sign up here to get the latest grocery and food news each morning
“Together we’ve made a proper Peanut Butter Granola that will fill your bowl with good stuff like fibre and protein. No big secrets or hidden nasties, just a breakfast worth getting up for.”
Additionally, the product uses only natural ingredients and contains no palm oil, emulsifiers or added sugars in line with the brand’s mission.
In an interview with Grocery Gazette, Pip & Nut founder Pip Murray stated her product-development rule is to keep ingredients lists short and use ingredients people will recognise from their own kitchens.
Jon Walsh, Bio&Me co-founder and CEO added: “We’re excited to be working with Pip & Nut on this dream collaboration, bringing together two brands with a shared passion for giving consumers healthier choices.
“With fibre and protein firmly on consumers’ radars, we see a real opportunity to bring something distinctive to the breakfast aisle with this seriously nutty granola. We’re excited to bring this proposition to shoppers and grateful to the Tesco team for supporting the launch.”
This comes after Pip & Nut posted its first-ever annual profit in late September, marking a major milestone for the independent brand.

items.title: Monsoon Accessorize upgrades store systems as expansion continues
items.summary: Monsoon Accessorize has upgraded its in-store technology to reduce disruption at its shops, as it continues to expand its high street and travel retail presence. The fashion and accessories retailer is addressing problems with ageing hardware and software that had made it harder to keep store systems running and introduce updates across its estate. The...
items.body:
Monsoon Accessorize has upgraded its in-store technology to reduce disruption at its shops, as it continues to expand its high street and travel retail presence.
The fashion and accessories retailer is addressing problems with ageing hardware and software that had made it harder to keep store systems running and introduce updates across its estate.
The investment follows its return to profitability, announced last year, when it reported a 3.7 per cent rise in sales to £212m. Growth was driven by its core Accessorize business, alongside gains in Monsoon’s ecommerce and marketplace operations.
Monsoon Accessorize is continuing to open and refurbish stores across both high street and travel retail locations, putting further emphasis on the reliability of its tills and other store systems.
Working with technology services provider PMC, the retailer has introduced remote monitoring to identify potential faults before they interrupt trading and resolve some issues automatically.
The supplier says the system prevents more than 2,000 technical incidents a year and now carries out over 20 million automated procedures annually. The work also supports the retailer’s existing point-of-sale systems and the rollout of software updates.
Monsoon Accessorize chief technology officer David West said the monitoring and automation had helped “prevent incidents and reduce the operational impact of technical issues on our stores”.
West said maintaining stable store operations remained important as “some of our underlying hardware and software has aged”.

items.title: New Asda CEO pledges more full-service checkouts and more products on shelves
items.summary: “The shopping trip is everything”, according to the newly appointed Asda CEO David Potts. He has used his first official day to call on the supermarket’s 1,100 Store Managers to…
items.body:
New Asda CEO pledges more full-service checkouts and more products on shelves
“The shopping trip is everything”, according to the newly appointed Asda CEO David Potts. He has used his first official day to call on the supermarket’s 1,100 Store Managers to focus on fixing the things that matter most to customers shopping in its stores.
In a message to store managers across the country, Potts asked them to focus on three fundamental areas that will make the biggest difference to the shopping trip:
- Open more full-service checkouts so customers, especially those doing bigger shops can get help from a colleague when they need it.
- Spend more time on the shop floor supporting colleagues, and making sure the store is in good shape for customers throughout the day.
- Get more product on shelves and presented well so the things customers come in for are easy to see and pick-up.
Subscribe to Grocery Gazette for free
Sign up here to get the latest grocery and food news each morning
“We’re making it harder than it should be for customers to get what they want, move around the store and pay for their shopping,” stressed Potts.
“We need to change that, starting now, which is why I’ve instructed all our General Store Managers to open more full-service checkouts, spend more time on the shopfloor and get more product on shelves and well-presented throughout the day.
“The shopping trip is everything and by making Asda easier to shop so customers can find what they came for and get through the checkouts easily, they’ll come back and shop more with us.
“I’ll be out in stores again this week and over the weekend listening to customers to see how we’re doing, and making sure our colleagues have what they need to deliver the improvements our customers expect.”

items.title: M&S announces target to double Food sales
items.summary: M&S has announced plans to double food sales as part of its long-term ambitions for the next phase of the retailer’s growth. The supermarket retailer has a goal of reaching…
items.body:
M&S announces target to double Food sales
M&S has announced plans to double food sales as part of its long-term ambitions for the next phase of the retailer’s growth.
The supermarket retailer has a goal of reaching mid-to-high single-digit sales growth over the medium-term, with a priority of a profit increase ahead of sales.
M&S plans to double the Food sales, building on the current momentum in the segment, having increased annual sales by over 50 per cent since FY22.
According to the business, the food segment has continued to gain market share and delivered an operating margin of approximately 5 per cent.
The supermarket retailer has made ongoing investments across its own-label food lines and worked on expanding its grocery store estate.
M&S plans to achieve its financial goals by maintaining a focus on developing strong margins which will be backed by increased cost reduction.
Subscribe to Grocery Gazette for free
Sign up here to get the latest grocery and food news each morning
The supermarket retailer has a cost reduction target of £600m by FY28, and the investments will be used to fund the next stage of savings.
Additionally, M&S announced plans to increase online activity in the Fashion, Home & Beauty department to 50 per cent with 180 stores.
The supermarket retailer also plans to expand its global presence and increase its international footprint across markets.
This announcement comes after the business posted strong first half results, crediting a surge in food sales.
Stuart Machin, CEO of M&S said in a statement at the time: “Our Food business is ahead, delivering double-digit volume growth in a flat market, and we have momentum as the UK’s fastest-growing grocer.
“One and a half million more customers are shopping with us, and our continued focus on quality, innovation and value is appealing to more families, as we become more of a shopping list retailer.”

items.title: Marks & Spencer targets doubling food sales as it steps up growth ambitions
items.summary: Marks & Spencer has reaffirmed its ambition to double food sales over time as it outlined plans to grow profits faster than sales. It used its capital markets day on November 10 to set out the next phase of its transformation, targeting annual sales growth in the mid-to-high single digits over the medium term. Food...
items.body:
Marks & Spencer has reaffirmed its ambition to double food sales over time as it outlined plans to grow profits faster than sales.
It used its capital markets day on November 10 to set out the next phase of its transformation, targeting annual sales growth in the mid-to-high single digits over the medium term.
Food remains central to those ambitions. The division has increased annual sales by more than 50 per cent since 2021/22 and is targeting further market share gains alongside an operating margin of around five per cent.
M&S said continued investment in its customer offer and operating model would support growth, improve productivity and help control costs. It remained on track to deliver £600 million of structural savings by 2027/28.
M&S has seen a strong first half for its food business, with sales rising 13.9 per cent to £5.2 billion in the six months to September 26.
Food volumes increased 11.9 per cent, while adjusted operating profit reached £288.6 million, delivering a margin of 5.6 per cent. M&S said it had attracted 1.5 million additional food customers over the past two years as it sought to capture more of families’ regular grocery spending.
Speaking alongside last week’s results, chief executive Stuart Machin said: “Our Food business is ahead, delivering double-digit volume growth in a flat market.”
Online grocery also contributed to the momentum. Sales of M&S food through Ocado Retail rose 22.8 per cent, with its products accounting for 30.9 per cent of the average basket.
The ambition to become a bigger destination for the weekly shop is being supported by substantial investment in distribution capacity.
As previously reported by Retail Gazette, M&S began construction on a £340 million automated food distribution centre in Northamptonshire in May.
The 1.3 million sq ft facility is scheduled to open in 2029 and serve more than 200 M&S Food stores. The retailer’s largest-ever supply chain investment is designed to increase capacity, improve availability and reduce long-term costs.
Automation will include pallet cranes, high-speed shuttles and hands-free picking, while changes to deliveries and replenishment are intended to free store colleagues to spend more time serving customers.
M&S has also deployed forecasting and replenishment technology from RELEX across its food operations, covering 1050 stores and 13 distribution centres in the UK and Ireland.
The system draws on sales history, weather, promotions and pricing to help predict demand and manage stock, particularly in fresh and chilled categories.
However, the wider group’s recovery remains uneven. Retail Gazette reported last week that fashion and home profits remained below pre-cyberattack levels, despite a rebound in sales.
Group adjusted pre-tax profit more than doubled year on year to £403.2 million, but the fashion, home and beauty division continued to face availability constraints and higher fulfilment costs.
Alongside its growth targets, M&S announced plans to double its full-year dividend for 2026/27 to 8.4p a share from 4.2p. It said maintaining a strong balance sheet and investment-grade credit rating remained priorities as it balanced investment with increased shareholder returns.

items.body:
Go Local Wholesale grows retailer support team
Go Local Wholesale has expanded its retail support team from 55 to 75, as it prepares for the next phase of growth across its estate in the UK.
According to the wholesaler, this move aims to provide support to the current 2,000 operating stores while helping the business expand with around 500 new stores each year.
This is part of Go Local’s wider business growth strategy, recently launching a major rebrand as it pushes toward a turnover of £1bn within three years.
Go Local Wholesale has announced a target of 3,000 symbol stores within the next two years, which has strengthened its team as it plans to expand the overall retail footprint.
Guy Swindell, joint managing director of Go Local Wholesale, said: “As we grow, it is important that we keep the close relationship we have with our retailers.
Subscribe to Grocery Gazette for free
Sign up here to get the latest grocery and food news each morning
“Expanding the retail team means we can spend more time in stores, helping retailers to maximise the potential of their store space, product ranges and promotional activity.
“Our ambition to become a £1bn business depends on our retailers succeeding. Employee ownership allows us to keep investing in the people, technology, depots and services that help them build stronger businesses.”
The company’s estate includes Go Local Extra, Go Local, The Local, Local 4 U and forecourt-focused Shop & Go.
The wholesaler currently runs nine depots nationwide and has over 2,000 symbol stores with plans for further expansion in development.
The business has been growing beyond its main headquarters over the recent years, which includes the opening of an 113,000 sq ft depot in Southampton.

items.title: France blames Iran for cyberattacks on 700 supermarket sites
items.summary: France accused Iran’s Revolutionary Guards of carrying out cyberattacks on supermarket refrigeration systems that forced retailers to discard perishable food. French foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot said the October 11 and…
items.body:
France blames Iran for cyberattacks on 700 supermarket sites
France accused Iran’s Revolutionary Guards of carrying out cyberattacks on supermarket refrigeration systems that forced retailers to discard perishable food.
French foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot said the October 11 and 12 attacks targeted 700 sites across the country.
Hackers remotely raised fridge temperatures, with some supermarkets forced to dispose of their entire stocks of perishable goods.
Intermarché reported losses running into tens of millions of euros in a single day, according to the Associated Press.
Speaking on November 9, Barrot described the attack as “unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression”.
France summoned Iran’s ambassador and said it would pursue European sanctions against those responsible.
Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau said a judicial investigation had been opened into the head of Shahid Kaveh and two deputies. French authorities described the group as a cyber unit affiliated with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
According to prosecutors, attackers triggered prolonged defrost cycles while disabling alerts intended to warn staff when temperatures exceeded safe thresholds.
Iran has routinely denied carrying out malicious cyber operations.
The attribution followed further suspected attacks on refrigeration systems elsewhere in Europe, including supermarkets in Sweden, Belgium, Luxembourg, Ireland and Estonia. Some stores were forced to dispose of spoiled food.
French officials did not establish whether the subsequent incidents were connected to the October attacks.

items.title: Hovis launches Just…3 sourdough range in Tesco
items.summary: Hovis launched a new sliced sourdough range in Tesco, targeting shoppers seeking bread made with simpler, more recognisable ingredients. The Just…3 range launched on November 9 in white and seeded…
items.body:
Hovis launches Just…3 sourdough range in Tesco
Hovis launched a new sliced sourdough range in Tesco, targeting shoppers seeking bread made with simpler, more recognisable ingredients.
The Just…3 range launched on November 9 in white and seeded varieties, priced at £2 for a 650g loaf. Tesco has initial exclusivity.
Both products use a base recipe of wheat flour, water and sea salt. The seeded version also contains a nine per cent blend of pumpkin seeds, sunflower seeds, millet, brown linseed, golden linseed and poppy seeds.
The flour is fortified with calcium, folic acid, iron, niacin and thiamin, according to Tesco’s product information.
Hovis developed the loaves with a milder flavour and softer texture for everyday uses such as sandwiches and toast.
The brand said shoppers wanted shorter ingredient lists, but traditional sourdough’s tang, crust and texture did not suit every occasion or household.
Hovis Bakeries chief marketing officer Mark Brown said: “Just…3 is all about giving people choice.”
He said the launch aimed to make simpler recipes more widely available while maintaining taste and convenience.
The range marks Hovis’ first product launch since its acquisition by Allied Bakeries in July.
It follows a £4 million investment in the brand, with advertising running across TV, video on demand, YouTube, outdoor, radio and social media from September to December.

items.title: El Rayo secures Tesco listing across 525 stores
items.summary: El Rayo secured a nationwide listing for its Plata tequila in 525 Tesco stores, expanding its presence across the UK grocery market. The deal adds Tesco to the independent spirits…
items.body:
El Rayo secures Tesco listing across 525 stores
El Rayo secured a nationwide listing for its Plata tequila in 525 Tesco stores, expanding its presence across the UK grocery market.
The deal adds Tesco to the independent spirits brand’s supermarket stockists, which already include Sainsbury’s and Waitrose.
The 100 per cent agave tequila is listed on Tesco’s website at £35 for a 70cl bottle, with an ABV of 40 per cent.
El Rayo founder and chief executive Tom Bishop said: “Tesco is a major milestone for us.”
He said the listing would help the brand reach more shoppers as it seeks to broaden tequila’s appeal beyond shots into longer drinks and cocktails.
Tesco spirits buyer Antonia Karkides said the retailer was seeing growing interest in tequila across different occasions and serves, alongside demand for brands offering something different.
Founded in 2019, El Rayo has built its proposition around serves such as tequila and tonic. Its range also includes ready-to-drink Tequila Tonic & Grapefruit and Tequila Lime & Soda.
Alongside its retail distribution, the brand is served in more than 1000 hospitality venues nationwide, including Sushi Samba, Forza Wine and Cubitt House.

items.title: The Entertainer owner’s losses widen despite record £315m sales
items.summary: The Entertainer owner Teal Group posted record annual sales of £315 million, but pre-tax losses widened to £19 million as costs mounted. Sales rose 10 per cent from £286.6 million in the year to January 31, 2026. Pre-tax losses increased from £10.1 million, while operating losses doubled to £16.8 million. Adjusted EBITDA stood at £2.9...
items.body:
The Entertainer owner Teal Group posted record annual sales of £315 million, but pre-tax losses widened to £19 million as costs mounted.
Sales rose 10 per cent from £286.6 million in the year to January 31, 2026. Pre-tax losses increased from £10.1 million, while operating losses doubled to £16.8 million. Adjusted EBITDA stood at £2.9 million.
The group blamed higher employment costs, business rates, depreciation and exceptional charges, including its move to employee ownership.
It also incurred £5.4 million in one-off costs establishing its largest retail partnership.
Trading strengthened after the year end, with like-for-like sales at The Entertainer’s own stores rising 22 per cent in the first half and sales across all channels increasing 13 per cent.
The improvement followed the Grant family’s transfer of ownership to an employee ownership trust in September 2025, enabling Sunday opening and broader product ranges.
Teal also invested £5 million in lower prices and restructured to remove £10 million from operating costs from 2027/28.
The board expected profitability to improve significantly this year. Several store openings are planned for 2027, including at least three in the UK’s top 20 retail locations.

items.title: Retail spending stalls as shoppers hold out for Black Friday deals
items.summary: UK retail sales rose 1.5 per cent in October, but shoppers held back on big-ticket purchases ahead of Black Friday and Christmas. The latest BRC-KPMG figures, covering the four weeks to October 31, showed growth was slightly below the 1.6 per cent recorded a year earlier but above the three-month average of 1.2 per cent....
items.body:
UK retail sales rose 1.5 per cent in October, but shoppers held back on big-ticket purchases ahead of Black Friday and Christmas.
The latest BRC-KPMG figures, covering the four weeks to October 31, showed growth was slightly below the 1.6 per cent recorded a year earlier but above the three-month average of 1.2 per cent.
Food sales increased 3.2 per cent, while non-food sales were flat as customers delayed purchases of furniture and white goods.
In-store non-food sales fell 1.1 per cent, compared with growth of 0.1 per cent last October. Online non-food sales rose 1.8 per cent, taking online penetration to 38.6 per cent from 38.2 per cent a year earlier.
British Retail Consortium chief executive Helen Dickinson said: “October was subdued for retailers, as shoppers delayed spending ahead of Black Friday and Christmas. Big ticket categories, such as furniture and white goods, performed badly as customers waited for November deals.”
Dickinson said wet weather helped online sales, while Halloween falling on a Saturday boosted spending on snacks, costumes and decorations.
She added: “Retailers are hoping pent-up demand translates into stronger spending through November and December, as they work hard to deliver great choice and value for households this Christmas.”
KPMG UK head of consumer, retail and leisure Linda Ellett said clothing, footwear and duvets benefited from falling temperatures, but higher household costs and uncertainty ahead of the Budget limited overall growth.
“Nonetheless, growth will be welcomed by a retail sector that desperately needs to offset cost increases with some strong sales as the promotional and festive season gets into full swing,” she said.
IGD chief executive Sarah Bradbury said half term and Halloween supported grocery spending, potentially alongside households stocking up following the government’s Be Ready campaign.
However, she warned shoppers remained pessimistic about their finances.
“Food and grocery promotions should help keep shoppers spending during the festive period, but we expect January to be a difficult month for many households,” Bradbury said.

items.title: Cadbury connects with THG Ingenuity for new direct-to-consumer gifting platform
items.summary: Cadbury has appointed THG Ingenuity to power its new direct-to-consumer Cadbury Shop.This will see THG Commerce deliver a cloud native digital storefront and interactive customisation software, THG Studios produce end-to-end e-commerce creative assets and visual digital merchandising,
items.body:
Cadbury has appointed THG Ingenuity to power its new direct-to-consumer Cadbury Shop.
This will see THG Commerce deliver a cloud native digital storefront and interactive customisation software, THG Studios produce end-to-end e-commerce creative assets and visual digital merchandising, while THG Fulfil will provide warehousing, pick-and-pack, temperature controlled confectionery handling, courier management and customer service solutions.
Central to the launch is an interactive product customisation engine developed to power the flagship Cadbury Heroes Pick & Mix, which allows shoppers to hand-pick a combination of miniature favourites.
The platform also introduces on-demand personalisation across giftboxes, including the dedicated Cadbury Build Your Own Letterbox Gift service, where shoppers can pick any six Cadbury tablets to be packaged and delivered straight to someone's doorstep.
Darren Rajanah, Chief Revenue Officer, THG Ingenuity, says: “We are proud to power the next phase of Cadbury’s commerce journey. Delivering exceptional direct-to-consumer experiences requires more than just a storefront; it demands an integrated operating environment where engaging creative content and intelligent digital technology connect seamlessly with automated fulfilment."
"By uniting THG Commerce’s e-commerce capabilities with THG Studios’ creative production and THG Fulfil’s operational scale, we are equipping Cadbury with the infrastructure needed to scale their direct-to-consumer personalised gifting business with confidence.”
Philip Warfield, Marketing Director, Cadbury - Mondelēz International, says: “Cadbury has always been about generosity and bringing people closer together. Appointing THG Ingenuity and launching the new Cadbury Shop gives us an exciting way to do exactly that ahead of Christmas, combining the chocolate the nation loves with beautifully personal gifting experiences, from the moment you choose it to the moment it's opened."
"It's a unified end-to-end solution that pairs personalisation, visual storytelling and fulfilment, helping us turn every gift into something truly special and serve our customers better than ever before.”
2026 RTIH Innovation Awards
E-commerce was a key focus area at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards.
The awards celebrate global retail technology innovation in a fast moving omnichannel world. Our winners were revealed at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London on Wednesday, 4th November.
The event consisted of a drinks reception, three course meal, awards ceremony presided over by award winning stand-up comedian, presenter, actor and broadcaster, Aurie Styla, and after party until 1am.

items.title: Waitrose reunites Keira Knightley and Joe Wilkinson for Christmas ad sequel
items.summary: Waitrose has reunited Keira Knightley and Joe Wilkinson for its 2026 Christmas campaign, launching a six-minute sequel to last year’s festive romantic comedy. ‘The Perfect Gift 2’, which premiered on YouTube and Waitrose.com on November 10, also stars Alex Hassell as Hugo Bunty-Griffin, a new love rival for Wilkinson’s character Phil. Waitrose said the film...
items.body:
Waitrose has reunited Keira Knightley and Joe Wilkinson for its 2026 Christmas campaign, launching a six-minute sequel to last year’s festive romantic comedy. ‘The Perfect Gift 2’, which premiered on YouTube and Waitrose.com on November 10, also stars Alex Hassell as Hugo Bunty-Griffin, a new love rival for Wilkinson’s character Phil. Waitrose said the film was the longest advert produced by a UK supermarket, running two minutes longer than last year’s instalment. Created with Wonderhood Studios and directed by Molly Manners through Biscuit Filmworks, the sequel follows Phil’s attempt to win back Knightley with a homemade beef Wellington. Waitrose’s festive range features throughout, including its No.1 Handmade Polar Bear Bao Buns, to build on its ‘Home of food lovers’ positioning.
Waitrose chief customer officer Nathan Ansell said: “Last year demonstrated that emotional, entertainment-first storytelling effectively cuts through the festive noise, builds strong brand affinity, and creates genuine cultural momentum.” He added: “With this ambitious sequel, our goal is to build on that connection, bring our story full circle, and give audiences a compelling reason to return.” MG OMD led the media strategy, planning and buying for the wider campaign, which takes inspiration from a film release with trailers, cinema advertising and romcom-style posters. Activity will run across TV, video on demand, cinema, print, outdoor, audio, social and online channels, alongside PR and in-store marketing. The full film will sit on Waitrose’s owned channels, supported by 60-second and 30-second trailers. Separate product adverts will feature the cast alongside items from the Christmas range, including No.1 Ham & Cheese Croissant Stacks and No.1 Pistachio & Sour Cherry Frangipane Mince Pies. The launch will also be supported by a press junket, behind-the-scenes footage, bloopers, cooking content with @whatwillycook and a partnership with Meet Cutes London. items.title: What are Britons buying on Whatnot? Auction site reveals top items from darts trading cards to old M&S clothes
items.summary: Online selling platform Whatnot has exploded in popularity this year, as Britons bid on everything from trading cards to the latest toys and sold-out trainers.
items.body:
What are Britons buying on Whatnot? Auction site reveals top items from darts trading cards to old M&S clothes
The online selling platform Whatnot has exploded in popularity this year, as Britons bid on everything from trading cards to the latest toys and sold-out trainers.
Whatnot's most popular feature is its live auctions, where sellers can flog their wares on video in real-time and buyers swipe to make bids.
The website has become known as the place to go if you are looking to buy into the latest internet craze or viral sensation.
In 2026 it has been a hub for people selling Labubus, Pokémon cards and vintage clothing from the early 2000s.
But what will be the hot items for sellers in 2027? Whatnot has trawled through its search and purchase data to reveal what buyers want right now, and what will be popular next year.
Hot item: Small stress toys called Squishies were one of the biggest selling products on the auction website Whatnot this year, with searches rising 100-fold
Toys
Toys are big business, as the number of adult collectors looking to relive their childhoods grows.
The next wave of nostalgia centres on the 1990s and 2000s, according to Whatnot.
In particular, it predicts a boom for Shrek Lego collections as fans combine their love of nostalgic toys with revived interest in the popular 2001 film.
Orders for Shrek Lego figures recently spiked 30-fold in a month after a new edition was released.
Jellycats, the popular cuddly toys with smiley faces, are still very popular, with orders up 13-fold in 2026.
Rare characters like the Luxe Bunny fetch 77 per cent more than a typical Jellycat. This year, the highest-selling Jellycat went for £850.
And it's vital to keep them in mint condition if you want to make a big profit.
Daniel Fisher, head of categories & expansion, Europe at Whatnot, said: 'Condition, completeness and rarity make the biggest difference when reselling.
'On Whatnot, a Jellycat with its tags still on sells for 37 per cent more than one without.'
Squishies, the squeezable polyurethane toys in the shape of animals or food items, have replaced Labubus as Britain's breakout toy according to Whatnot.
Searches for squishies went up 100-fold this year while Labubu searches fell 89 per cent.
PS3 consoles and games are also set to boom as the console turns 20 in March 2027. Searches increased by 360 per cent on Whatnot in 2026.
Trading cards
Pokémon's popularity has risen seismically over the years, with some trading cards originally worth just a few pence now selling for close to £2,000.
Originally named Pocket Monsters, Pokémon started out as a game released for the Nintendo Gameboy in Japan in 1996.
It's 30th anniversary in September brought in hundreds of thousands of first-time buyers to Whatnot. Many were original fans who grew up in the late 1990s and early 2000s.
Searches for Vintage Pokémon cards went up 164 per cent last year, while the Charizards and Eevees were the most-searched Pokémon.
Whatnot said buyers are building collections around favourite characters and the cards that mean something to them.
In the UK, football is still the backbone of card collecting. Arsenal cards have led the way in 2026 with orders up 490 per cent after the club's Premier League-winning season.
But Liverpool cards are Whatnot's hot tip for 2027. The club has inched ahead since the new season kicked off with Florian Wirtz and Virgil van Dijk among the most-bought players.
And with the Women's World Cup arriving in 2027, women's football is set to have its collecting moment too.
The number of sellers going live with darts cards has also more than tripled, with orders up more than 30-fold in 2026.
This could be a sweet spot for sellers, as darts auctions on Whatnot sell 2.6 times as many cards as typical sports card shows.

Arsenal card orders are up 490% after the club's Premier League-winning season
Fashion
Whatnot shoppers are looking for quality over quantity, the platform says, as British shoppers gravitate towards timeless fashion items over fleeting trends.
Searches for Mulberry, the quintessentially British luxury fashion and leather goods brand known for its iconic handbag styles like the Bayswater and Alexa, jumped by 500 per cent this year.
Buyers can still find bargains, though. In October, a Vintage Mulberry Daria Hobo bag sold for £285. On Mulberry's official resale site, they can sell for around £500.
Coach, another popular handbag brand, saw its searches rise by 600 per cent.
Marks & Spencer resale clothing is also popular with searches up 26 per cent.
Whatnot's Fisher said: 'Check your loft for childhood favourites and well-kept vintage pieces from the likes of M&S, Coach or Mulberry, and hold on to any tags, boxes and dust bags, as they all help increase item's value.'
Classic accessories are also being restyled in new ways. Searches for floral brooches have increased by 202 per cent, big sunglasses by 68 per cent, and silk scarves by 78 per cent.
On the whole, fashion generates more orders than any other category on the platform, with order volume more than doubling since last year.
The number of fashion buyers and sellers has also doubled year on year. This could be down to two reasons.
One, a lack of graduate jobs prompting a surge in side hustles. And two, a generation of 'doom spenders' splurging on luxuries instead of saving for a property or other milestones they feel they might never afford.
Now could be a great time to start selling clothes on the side as the tax-free trading allowance is set to treble from April 2027.
Mulberry: Bags from the iconic brand are selling well on Whatnot, as a cheaper alternative to new pieces such as this Vintage Oak Suede Bayswater bag which costs £1,245 brand new
Beauty
Korean beauty will continue to be a staple of skincare routines in 2027, Whatnot predicts.
In 2024, the Korean beauty market was worth about £9.75billion. By 2030, this could be £14.3billion according to forecasts.
K-beauty brands accounted for more than 80 per cent of skincare orders on Whatnot's platform, and Korean and Japanese brands' share of UK beauty orders rose 860 per cent over the last year.
Medicube, a popular Korean brand appears to be taking centre stage, with UK searches up 60-fold in 2026.
Whatnot says fragrance is a big trend for 2027, and this is being driven by British men with searches for men's aftershave soaring 400 per cent.
Dior Sauvage, Parfums de Marly Layton and Creed Aventus are among the fragrances proving particularly popular.
The number of men buying beauty in Whatnot's auctions grew by 630 per cent this year meaning there are roughly around 7.3 times as many male beauty buyers compared to last year.
On top of this, the amount of money men spent on beauty grew by 800 per cent, making the total spend roughly 9x higher.
Medicube is a popular Korean derma-cosmetic brand booming on TikTok

items.summary: Morrisons has gone live in its first store with Emerald, the UK grocery retailer's new checkout software. It is working with NCR Voyix on the project.In a LinkedIn post, Laura Critchley, Support Office Specialist- Front End Operations, said: "This is a project that I, alongside so many fantastic col
items.body:
Morrisons has gone live in its first store with Emerald, the UK grocery retailer's new checkout software. It is working with NCR Voyix on the project.
In a LinkedIn post, Laura Critchley, Support Office Specialist- Front End Operations, said: "This is a project that I, alongside so many fantastic colleagues across the business, have been working on for the last two years, so seeing it finally come to life in store is a brilliant feeling."
She added: "Emerald will replace our existing Storeline software across checkouts and cash offices, bringing a more streamlined, modern and user-friendly experience for colleagues, while helping to make everyday processes easier and improve the customer experience."
"It’s been a huge collaborative effort to get us to this point, and it’s fantastic to see all the hard work starting to pay off. A brilliant step forward for our Front End teams, and we can’t wait to see Emerald rolled out across our stores from next year."
2026 RTIH Innovation Awards
Morrisons was named Overall Winner at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, which took place in Central London last week. And it also emerged victorious in the RTIH Editor's Choice category for its partnership with Gatekeeper Systems.
In a LinkedIn post, the retailer said: "We’re delighted to have been named Overall Winner, selected by the judging panel as the standout entry from across all of the event's 23 categories. Great recognition for some of the brilliant and innovative cross functional projects that have been delivered over the last few months!"
It added: "We were also recognised in the Editor’s Choice Award, alongside Gatekeeper Systems for our Cart Control programme across five Morrisons stores. The programme has delivered some fantastic results: An estimated 82.1 tonnes of CO₂e saved each year; 1,170 fewer replacement trolleys needed; 7,696 fewer trolleys ending up in local communities and waterways. Congratulations to everyone involved in making this possible!"
Scott Thompson, Editor and Founder at RTIH, said: "Congratulations to Morrisons. We received a record number of entries this year, showcasing truly impressive innovation across both traditional and digital retail spaces."
"To quote a member of our judging panel: Reviewing such inventive, high impact solutions has been a truly rewarding experience. The depth of engineering, scalable architecture, and strategic vision displayed throughout the submissions underscores the rapid transformation happening across modern retail technology."
"A number of companies were in the running for Overall Winner but ultimately the judges picked Morrisons for launching several innovative initiatives encompassing major technological upgrades to enhance its customers’ shopping experience."

items.title: US retailer DeCicco & Sons expands Simbe Store Intelligence technology roll-out following pilot
items.summary: US grocery retailer DeCicco & Sons has expanded Simbe’s Store Intelligence platform chainwide following a 35% reduction in out-of-stocks within the first 60 days at its pilot locations. Simbe’s autonomous shelf scanning robot, Tally, captures detailed shelf conditions multiple times daily. That
items.body:
US grocery retailer DeCicco & Sons has expanded Simbe’s Store Intelligence platform chainwide following a 35% reduction in out-of-stocks within the first 60 days at its pilot locations.
Simbe’s autonomous shelf scanning robot, Tally, captures detailed shelf conditions multiple times daily. That intelligence flows into the retailer’s existing systems, helping teams identify and resolve issues faster while supporting applications spanning store operations, e-commerce, and business intelligence.
“Our customers count on us to have the products they love and a team ready to help,” says John DeCicco Jr., CEO, DeCicco & Sons. “Simbe helps us deliver on both. Digitising our shelves is foundational to our broader technology strategy, because it gives every system we run an accurate picture of what’s happening in our stores. With real-time visibility into stores, our teams can address corrective fixes sooner and spend more time providing the personal service that brings people back to DeCiccos.”
A critical element of DeCicco & Sons’ success has been integrating physical intelligence directly into existing workflows. Rather than requiring store teams to adopt another standalone tool, Simbe connects shelf-level data to the systems and routines they already use. This approach enables associates to stop searching for issues and focus on resolving them instead, while giving business teams access to a consistent, accurate understanding of store conditions.
“Having better information about our shelves helps us take better care of our customers and our team,” says Chris Dapolito, Manager at DeCicco & Sons, Sleepy Hollow. “I’m spending more of my day out in the store, talking with shoppers and supporting our department managers. Those relationships are a big part of what makes DeCiccos special, and Tally helps us build on them.”
“DeCicco & Sons recognised early that the future of retail operations depends on continuous understanding of what’s happening inside physical stores,” says Caitlin Allen, SVP, Market at Simbe. “By connecting that intelligence to the systems and people running its business, DeCiccos is demonstrating how physical AI can elevate shopper experience, empower associates, and lay the foundation for increasingly autonomous retail.”
2026 RTIH Innovation Awards
Automation was a key focus area at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards.
The awards celebrate global retail technology innovation in a fast moving omnichannel world. Our winners were revealed at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London on Wednesday, 4th November.
The event consisted of a drinks reception, three course meal, awards ceremony presided over by award winning stand-up comedian, presenter, actor and broadcaster, Aurie Styla, and after party until 1am.

items.title: How to get the buzz back on Britain’s high streets | Letters
items.summary: Readers respond to an article about the decline of town centres Sammy Gecsoyler’s report from Rotherham ( ‘It’s just vape shops, nail shops, charity shops’: can anything save the British high street?, 4 November ) tells the story in its dates. One out-of-town retail park in Britain in 1981; 385 by 1996. Parkgate opened in 1987 and MPs warned that it would disembowel towns and villages. It did. Rotherham town centre is now 24% vacant, while retail park vacancy nationally sits at 4.8%. That is not a mystery. It is 40 years of planning policy. We have since gone one step further by making home delivery cheaper than retail parks. Up to 3bn parcels a year now land on British doorsteps and not one of them passes through a town centre. Continue reading...
items.body:
Sammy Gecsoyler’s report from Rotherham (‘It’s just vape shops, nail shops, charity shops’: can anything save the British high street?, 4 November) tells the story in its dates. One out-of-town retail park in Britain in 1981; 385 by 1996. Parkgate opened in 1987 and MPs warned that it would disembowel towns and villages. It did. Rotherham town centre is now 24% vacant, while retail park vacancy nationally sits at 4.8%. That is not a mystery. It is 40 years of planning policy.
We have since gone one step further by making home delivery cheaper than retail parks. Up to 3bn parcels a year now land on British doorsteps and not one of them passes through a town centre.
Andy Burnham’s £210m for high streets is welcome, but is a one-off against a structural problem. What a town centre needs is a reason for people to walk into it again, every week, without being told to.
So here is a proposal, given in written evidence to an inquiry by the Commons housing, communities and local government committee into revitalising high streets. Put £1 on every parcel delivered to a residential address. Charge nothing if it is collected from a shop, locker or pickup point in town. Ringfence the money by law and return it to the council area that the parcel landed in – 60% to transport and 40% to markets and high streets.
The pound is not the point; the exemption is. The cheapest way to receive a parcel would involve walking into a town centre. That would do more for Rotherham than any grant.
 
Dan Johnson
 
Co-founder, Crafty Vintage, Whalley, Lancashire
I run the Grumpy Cook, a community-focused cafe in Hastings. I’ve seen first-hand how difficult it is for independent businesses to survive, particularly in communities where disposable income is already stretched. That’s why I recently launched My Local First, a loyalty and rewards platform to bring independent businesses together. Customers earn rewards for spending locally, discover other independent businesses and have a reason to return. Businesses can participate for just £10 a month, without paying commission on their sales to the platform.
But high streets cannot thrive if the people living around them cannot afford to participate in their local economy. That’s why we’re also developing ways to connect affordable food and discreet community support.
We cannot expect councils or government grants alone to regenerate town centres. Nor can we expect individual businesses to compete with multinational corporations on their own. We need to start working collectively. My Local First won’t solve every problem facing Britain’s high streets. But it represents something I believe we’ve lost sight of: communities taking responsibility for their own local economies. Perhaps the answer isn’t simply saving our high streets. Perhaps it’s giving people a reason to believe in them again.
 
Barry Ashley
 
Hastings, East Sussex
As someone who grew up locally, I recognise the challenges in Rotherham. The new government strategy, Hope on the High Street, has some ideas – including a number of community-led schemes that we helped support at the Architectural Heritage Fund. Projects like High Street West in Sunderland – a mixed-use approach to derelict shops that delivered a cafe, music venue and workspaces. Or Valley Heritage’s development in Bacup, Lancashire, where a Grade II former bank has been split into co-working space and affordable housing.
Equally importantly, it’s about empowering these communities as they are passionate about their environment. Although there are many challenging town centres, a growing number offer a more positive future and could be replicated elsewhere.
 
Matthew Mckeague
 
CEO, Architectural Heritage Fund
Saving the British high street means accepting that retail can no longer be its primary purpose. Councils should acquire vacant or persistently underused sites and, where appropriate, replace poor-quality empty buildings with well-insulated, low-rise homes for renters and young professionals. New developments could be designed from the outset so that extra floors or modular homes can be added later as demand grows. That would cost more initially, but could reduce the disruption and expense of future expansion.
Housing alone, however, will not make a thriving neighbourhood. It should be interspersed with services and spaces that people genuinely need: walk-in health and mental health support, childcare, community and arts spaces, and other local amenities. There is a strong case for locating services closer to the communities they serve, rather than expecting people to travel elsewhere to find support. High streets should also include more and better green spaces, with trees, planting and small parks that give people somewhere pleasant to spend time, while at the same time responding to the challenge of climate change and air pollution.
Bring people back to the high street and businesses will have a reason to return too: cafes, hairdressers, independent shops and other everyday services. Councils should use planning and licensing powers carefully to encourage a balanced mix of businesses and avoid excessive concentrations of premises that can undermine the health and character of an area. The high street will not be saved by restoring the past. Its future could lie in becoming a place to live, meet, access services and build community, with retail as one part of a much broader purpose.
 
Helen Roberts
 
Sheffield

items.title: Poundland unable to buy new stock as fears over collapse grow
items.summary: The discount chain is continuing to edge towards collapse and is said to be "running on fumes", according to one insider.
items.body:
Poundland unable to buy new stock as fears over collapse grow
- Published
Poundland is unable to buy new stock to fill its shelves after being blocked by its owners from accessing cash in its bank accounts.
The discount chain is on the brink of collapse with one insider describing it as "running on fumes". It has until Thursday to secure a rescue deal.
About Â£50m has been frozen by its American owner Gordon Brothers, the BBC understands, meaning its 600 shops are running out of stock.
Pressure is building on Gordon Brothers, which bought Poundland for Â£1 last June, after the owner rejected a takeover bid that could have saved the thousands of jobs currently at risk. Gordon Brothers has been approached for comment.
Poundland has filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators, which protects it from its creditors until Thursday.
Access to funds was limited because of a tension between Gordon Brothers' dual role as both creditor and shareholder, a source said, but added they expected a relaxation of funds in the next two days.
Last week, Poundland boss Barry Williams told staff like-for-like sales, which exclude new store openings, were up 11.4% last week, which included Halloween, but said this was Â£1.5m ahead of budget.
He said the business made a profit of Â£18.1m in the year to September, which was a "strong recovery" from the previous year where the business made losses of Â£68m.
The latest annual accounts have yet to be audited.
- Burnham 'ready to support' Poundland staff as retailer faces collapse 
  - Published29 October
- Poundland staff protest after chain approach administrators 
  - Published29 October
However, Gordon Brothers has painted a different picture of the business, saying the chain remains "challenged and vulnerable to any potential downturn in future trading".
It said it had provided significant funding to support the company's ability to trade since it acquired the business.
It has also made Â£18m, from a combination of debt interest payments and other fees and charges.
On Wednesday, executives from Gordon Brothers will appear before the Business Select Committee with MPs probing whether they are genuinely pursuing a solvent rescue of the business, which has 11,000 employees, and whether every realistic step is being taken to protect jobs and stores.
The session is being held in private given commercially sensitive discussions are still under way with bidders.
Uncertain future
On Thursday, the 10-day moratorium to protect Poundland from its creditors expires, but if there is a prospect of a solvent deal, the deadline could be extended.
If not, Poundland is set to collapse into administration and could be broken up.
A source familiar with the sales process said London-based Xyra Group was making "significant progress" in its last minute bid to buy Poundland and could now be the front runner.
An extension of Thursday's deadline now seems an increasingly likely scenario. But such a case would be difficult to put forward if Gordon Brothers continues to block funding.
One observer remarked "if Gordon Brothers is going in front of that committee, you don't want to be giving the message we're pulling up the drawbridge".
Even if a deal is agreed to sell the business as a whole, there is no guarantee a new owner would not reduce the number of stores, but suppliers to Poundland would prefer that outcome to hundreds of sites being sold off to other retailers.
There has been interest from the likes of Poundstretcher, Tesco and B&M in picking up stores which could mean continuing employment for many workers.
The central issue is whether a piecemeal sale would protect more jobs than a buyer willing to keep Poundland trading as a national chain.

items.title: The hottest product in Britain this year? A 2kg bag of ice
items.summary: As the UK endured record-breaking temperatures this summer, nothing grew in popularity on Deliveroo like sacks of sweet relief from the supermarket Iceland Name: Iceland’s 2kg bag of ice. Age: The first patents for commercial mechanical production date to the 1850s. Continue reading...
items.body:
Name: Iceland’s 2kg bag of ice.
Age: The first patents for commercial mechanical production date to the 1850s.
Appearance: Clear, cold.
Just normal ice, then. Ice in its most desirable form.
Cubes, you mean. A bag containing 2kg of ice cubes, as sold by the British supermarket Iceland.
What’s so desirable about that? “These ice cubes are better than anyone else’s and are great value for money,” according to a five-star review on Iceland’s website from Trevor P.
So Trevor likes ice. Not just Trevor. According to Deliveroo, Iceland’s 2kg ice bag was the “top trending” UK delivery order – a metric that marries year-on-year growth in orders, relative order volume in the local area and customer ratings – of 2026 so far.
Really? What came second? The diavola pizza from Monte Forte Neapolitan Pizza in Horsham, West Sussex.
How specific. But ice bag deliveries from Iceland were so popular in London that they came second in Deliveroo’s global ranking.
I guess it was a pretty hot summer. The hottest since records began.
How much would a 2kg bag of ice set me back on a scorching July afternoon? You can get one for £1 in the store.
That’s not bad, actually. But when you add in the Deliveroo surcharge, its small-order fee, the delivery fee, the bag charge and the service charge, it could cost as much as £8.
That’s ridiculous! As I’ve pointed out, you could get the same bag from the shop for a quid.
Yeah, but the shops are, like, hundreds of metres away. You could even make your own ice, in your own freezer, for a fraction of the cost.
But then I’d have to realise I’ll want a margarita hours before I do. I prefer to be spontaneous. Do you not see the irony of paying over the odds to have someone bring you a single bag of ice amid a climate crisis?
The climate crisis is why I want the ice. A climate crisis brought about in no small part by the rapacious demands of western consumerism, all because you can’t be bothered to fill your own ice trays?
OK, I do see the irony, but my hands are tied. No they aren’t! You can make better choices!
Anyway, it’s November now. I’m cold and I want soup. Well, the good news is you can probably make a lovely soup from things you already have in your kitchen.
I don’t like that kind of soup. What kind of soup do you like?
Soup from a man in a motorbike helmet. I despair.
Do say: “When we’re having ice delivered while the world burns, something is seriously wrong with our priorities.”
Don’t say: “This pizza from Horsham – can I get it delivered to Peterborough?”
