items.title: Shopping or social? What an under-16 ban could mean for resale
items.summary: As ministers consider bringing online marketplaces into the proposed social media ban, eBay, Vinted and Depop face a question that cuts to the heart of social commerce: where does shopping end and social networking begin? Follow a seller, scroll through a personalised feed, message about a jacket and make an offer. On peer-to-peer marketplaces, shopping...
items.body:
As ministers consider bringing online marketplaces into the proposed social media ban, eBay, Vinted and Depop face a question that cuts to the heart of social commerce: where does shopping end and social networking begin?
Follow a seller, scroll through a personalised feed, message about a jacket and make an offer. On peer-to-peer marketplaces, shopping and social interaction are often part of the same journey.
That overlap could become a regulatory headache for the resale sector as the UK government considers whether its proposed ban on social media for under-16s should extend to online marketplaces.
For eBay, Vinted and Depop, the stakes go beyond losing access to younger shoppers. Restrictions could affect how buyers discover products, how sellers build a following and how the two sides communicate before a sale.
Yet their inclusion is not confirmed. The central question is whether ministers will regulate platforms according to their primary purpose — buying and selling — or the risks created by the social features built around transactions.
Why marketplaces are in the frame
The prospect moved beyond a theoretical debate on 8 November, when Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy said the government was seriously considering extending the proposed ban to online marketplaces.
Speaking on the BBC’s Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Nandy said ministers were examining the move as part of efforts to protect children from online harm.
The concern is not simply what children can buy. It is who can contact them while they browse and trade.
The Children’s Society has warned that some young people are being approached through resale platforms and asked for indecent photographs in exchange for money or gifts.
These services also have a young audience. Ofcom research found that 19 per cent of children aged eight to 14 use eBay at least monthly, while 15 per cent use Vinted.
That puts marketplaces at the intersection of two competing considerations: protecting children from harmful contact and preserving access to services whose main function is commerce rather than social networking.
When a shop becomes a social network
On paper, the distinction looks straightforward. eBay, Vinted and Depop connect people who want to buy and sell goods. But profiles, private messages, following, recommendations and personalised feeds make the experience more social than a conventional online checkout.
Depop illustrates the blurred boundary particularly clearly. Its social-commerce model lets users follow sellers, discover products through feeds and interact with other members. The community and the shop are closely connected.
This creates a difficult choice for policymakers. Treat every marketplace with social functions as a social network and the restrictions could reach well beyond their original target. Focus only on a platform’s commercial purpose and the risks associated with private contact could remain.
More than a loss of young shoppers
If marketplaces fall within a blanket ban, the most immediate consequence would be the exclusion of under-16 users. For resale businesses, however, those users can sit on both sides of the transaction.
A younger participant may be buying affordable second-hand clothing one day and selling unwanted items the next. Removing that access could therefore affect both demand and the supply of goods, rather than simply reducing a platform’s audience.
The implications would vary. Depop’s fashion-led community makes its appeal to younger consumers particularly relevant. Vinted could face disruption to younger users’ clothing resale activity, while eBay’s exposure would span a broader range of product categories.
The wider question for second-hand retail is whether restrictions would narrow young people’s opportunities to earn money from unwanted possessions and take part in circular shopping. The size of any commercial impact would depend on the final rules and the users they cover.
Keeping under-16s off affected services would also raise a practical challenge: establishing who is old enough to use them.
More robust age verification could introduce additional compliance costs and extra steps at registration. Marketplaces face a potential tension between demonstrating effective safeguards and keeping the buying and selling journey straightforward.
Ofcom has identified photo ID matching, digital ID, banking checks and facial age estimation as methods capable of providing highly effective age assurance at 16. Which approach affected marketplaces might adopt, and how it would fit into their services, remains an open question.
Could messaging be the dividing line?
An alternative to excluding younger users entirely would be to target the features that expose them to harmful contact.
That could mean tighter restrictions on communication between strangers. But messaging is not merely a social extra on a resale platform: it allows buyers to ask about an item’s condition, negotiate a price or arrange a collection.
Restricting those exchanges could leave younger users able to browse while limiting their ability to complete the interactions that support a purchase. The challenge would be to separate necessary trading conversations from unsafe contact without undermining the marketplace itself.
A defining test for social commerce
The government has said the first regulations for its proposed under-16 social media ban will be laid before Parliament by the end of 2026, with initial restrictions expected in spring 2027. Whether eBay, Vinted and Depop will be included remains unresolved.
A platform-wide age restriction could affect customer acquisition, transactions and stock coming onto services. Feature-specific safeguards could leave younger users able to participate, but change how they discover sellers and communicate with them.
The debate exposes a tension at the centre of social commerce. Features that make online shopping feel personal and community-driven can also create channels for harmful contact.
The question is no longer simply whether they are shops or social networks. It is whether the rules can address the risks of being both without removing the interactions that help them function.

items.title: AI joins the Christmas ecommerce rush — but will recommendations turn into sales?
items.summary: With UK festive online spending forecast to hit £28.52bn, retailers face a new contest for visibility, trust and conversion as shoppers turn to AI for gift inspiration and better deals. The battle for Christmas spending may begin before a shopper reaches a search engine, let alone a website. A request for a gift within a...
items.body:
With UK festive online spending forecast to hit £28.52bn, retailers face a new contest for visibility, trust and conversion as shoppers turn to AI for gift inspiration and better deals.
The battle for Christmas spending may begin before a shopper reaches a search engine, let alone a website. A request for a gift within a particular budget can now produce an AI-generated shortlist, this leaves brands with a new challenge – making sure they are on it.
The opportunity comes against a backdrop of forecast growth. Research from Adobe predicts UK shoppers will spend a record £28.52bn online between 1 November and 31 December, up 6.2 per cent year-on-year. Fourth-quarter ecommerce sales are expected to climb 6.4 per cent to £40bn.
AI is expected to play a bigger role in how that spending is directed. Adobe forecasts that traffic to retail websites from AI platforms will rise 214 per cent year-on-year during November and December, compared with a 111 per cent increase in September.
That does not mean AI is responsible for the overall increase in sales, or that shoppers are ready to hand over their wallets to autonomous assistants. The research and industry commentary point to a more nuanced shift. AI is helping consumers decide what to buy, while retailers work out how to be recommended, and how to turn that recommendation into a completed order.
A new route to the Christmas shortlist
PayPal research finds that 35 per cent of UK consumers are already using, or planning to use, AI to help with their Christmas shopping. Finding deals or comparing prices is cited by 52 per cent, while 51 per cent point to product research. Personalised gift recommendations and identifying this year’s must-have presents each attract 39 per cent.
Dave Jones, head of UK consumer at PayPal, describes shoppers as “embracing new ways to make their lives easier”, including “using AI to compare deals and take some of the stress out of Christmas and gift buying”.
These more detailed requests could reveal needs that a conventional search leaves unclear. Simon James, managing director of AI & data strategy at Publicis Sapient, says: “The average Google search is four or five words. The average AI prompt is around twenty. That gives retailers a much richer picture of intent, because you start to understand the ask behind the ask.”
He points to B&Q’s assistant as an example of helping customers work out what they need for a project, rather than simply directing them to an individual product. The potential commercial benefit is a fuller basket, although that remains an opportunity rather than a guaranteed outcome.
Winning a recommendation, not just a click
The shift creates a different kind of competition for visibility. Tom Bowie, co-founder at Ignite Stack, says its research with Visible PR analysed 600 AI-generated answers to Christmas gifting questions. John Lewis appeared in around one in five responses, while Monica Vinader, LEGO and Hampers.com led their respective gifting categories.
“It’s no longer just about competing on price, advertising or search rankings,” Bowie notes. “Brands also need to make sure they’re appearing in the AI recommendations that increasingly influence what shoppers consider buying.”
Those findings describe visibility within the answers studied, not a share of Christmas sales. But they illustrate why retailers are paying attention to the point at which consumers assemble their shortlist.
Cathy Farmer, head of GEO at Third City, argues that retailers need to answer specific needs rather than rely on broad promotional language.
“Someone asking for a gift for a particular person, budget and interest needs a useful recommendation, not a page of generic claims,” she says. “I’d focus on clear product information, up-to-date availability and credible independent coverage that helps explain who a product is right for.”
This does not make other marketing channels irrelevant. Adobe also forecasts that revenue share from social networks will rise 24 per cent, with influencer partnerships up seven per cent. Jack Rigby, founder of PR Barn, argues that media coverage, social referrals, reviews and an easy-to-search website all contribute to AI visibility.
Farmer cautions: “A place in an AI answer is worth checking, but it isn’t a sale. Retailers need to look at what happens next: visits, purchases and whether those customers come back.”
The sales impact may be harder to track
Measuring those outcomes presents another challenge. Daisy Wolfenden, managing director at Wolfenden, reports strong growth in revenue coming directly from AI platforms across its retail clients, while stressing that it remains a small proportion of overall sales.
“AI is influencing which retailers consumers discover, which products they consider and ultimately where they spend, but much of that influence won’t be reflected in direct referral revenue,” she says. “A customer might discover a brand through ChatGPT and then purchase through Google or directly with the retailer.”
That distinction matters when assessing AI’s contribution this Christmas. Referral traffic can show one route to a purchase, but Wolfenden’s point is that discovery and checkout may happen in different channels. Looking only at sales attributed directly to an AI platform could miss some of its influence.
Conversational tools may also help explain why shoppers do not buy. James says an assistant can capture where a conversation stopped and which questions went unanswered, exposing barriers such as delivery charges.
“Web analytics only ever showed clicks,” he says. “This starts to show you people’s motivations and barriers.”
Discovery is ahead of delegation
Growing use of AI for inspiration should not be confused with a willingness to let it spend. Research from Signicat highlights how trust changes with the task: 42 per cent of consumers would trust AI to create recipes and 38 per cent to draft emails, but only eight per cent would be happy for it to make high-value purchases on their behalf. For smaller purchases, the figure is 19 per cent.
The research also finds discomfort with AI making purchases on a consumer’s behalf at 69 per cent, close to the 71 per cent recorded for opening financial products. That points to a boundary between seeking advice and allowing a tool to make financial decisions.
Mark Howell, director of EMEA retailers at Rithum, puts the distinction plainly: “The biggest impact of AI right now isn’t autonomous purchasing, its discovery. People are increasingly using AI tools as search engines.”
This switch therefore makes a stronger case for improving discovery and decision-making than for assuming shoppers will delegate the entire transaction.
The promise has to survive checkout
Even a well-targeted recommendation can fall short if the retailer cannot fulfil it. Product data, availability and the checkout experience connect AI-led discovery to actual revenue.
Joe Squire, marketing director at Epos Now, describes a shopper asking an assistant to find a gift under £40 that can be collected that day. In that scenario, he argues, accurate, connected stock information becomes crucial.
“That makes a retailer’s stock data its new shop window,” he notes. “An independent shop with a website and a till that don’t talk to each other risks being invisible at exactly the moment a shopper is ready to buy.”
The next hurdle is completing the order. Nikhita Hyett, EMEA general manager at Signifyd, says: “If AI helps someone find the right product at the right price, only for their order to be declined at checkout, the entire experience falls apart.”
Her warning is that fraud checks must distinguish genuine purchases from risky ones as shopping journeys change. Behind the transaction, staffing also matters: Kristján Freyr Kristjánsson, co-founder and CEO of 50skills, argues that automating contracts and onboarding can help retailers get seasonal workers ready sooner, allowing fulfilment to keep pace with customer expectations.
AI’s impact on UK ecommerce this Christmas is therefore unlikely to be captured by one traffic-growth figure. The forecasts suggest a fast-growing route into retail websites; the consumer research shows demand for help with prices, products and presents, alongside continuing reluctance to surrender control of purchases.
The opportunity is not simply to appear in more AI answers. It is to be recommended for the right reasons, offer the product the shopper actually needs and make the purchase work. A place on the Christmas shortlist is valuable — but the sale still has to be earned.

items.title: Poundland ‘frontrunner’ Xyra Group asks retailer’s founder to join bid
items.summary: The little-known investment firm emerging as a “frontrunner” to buy Poundland has called on Steve Smith, the retailer’s founder, to bolster its bid for the struggling firm.  Xyra Group Holdings, founded by 23-year-old Manvedeep Singh, has asked Smith to lend support to their £12.5m bid to keep Poundland afloat as the discount retailer veers towards [...]
items.body:
Poundland ‘frontrunner’ Xyra Group asks retailer’s founder to join bid
The little-known investment firm emerging as a “frontrunner” to buy Poundland has called on Steve Smith, the retailer’s founder, to bolster its bid for the struggling firm.
Xyra Group Holdings, founded by 23-year-old Manvedeep Singh, has asked Smith to lend support to their £12.5m bid to keep Poundland afloat as the discount retailer veers towards collapse, City AM has learned.
Smith has had conversations with Xyra Group in recent days but does not plan to take part in any takeover efforts until a deal has been completed, it is understood.
The Poundland founder, who set up the retailer with his father, Kevin Smith, in 1990, had been weighing investing in the company himself or backing a rival offer tabled by Martin Property Group but has ruled out both options.
Gordon Brothers, the US investment firm which owns Poundland, is racing to find a solvent buyer for the retailer before a moratorium blocking creditors from calling in their debt lapses on Thursday.
The firm’s filing of a notice to appoint administrators had sparked fears Poundland was edging towards collapse but it is now holding talks with multiple bidders over a sale of the company as a going concern.
Gordon Brothers’ earlier attempts to find a solvent buyer for Poundland had been derailed over its demand to be paid £22.5m for a loan it inherited from PepCo, the retailer’s previous owner, when it bought the firm for £1 last year.
PepCo owns £7.5m of this loan, which is worth £30m in total, but has offered to defer its repayment.
Jobs at risk from collapse
Xyra Group is offering to pay Gordon Brothers £12.5m up front, leaving a £10m shortfall on the investment firm’s share of this loan. Martin Property Group has offered to pay £5m initially, leaving a shortfall of £17.5m, it is understood.
This makes Xyra Group the “frontrunner” to acquire Poundland, sources told City AM. While there had been questions over the source of the investment firm’s funding, it has made “significant progress” in providing proof of “credible backing,” they said.
Xyra Group has not completed a single acquisition since it was founded in November 2024 and little is known about its senior leadership. Viktor Bronzovic, who serves as its chief executive, is a 27-year-old tech entrepreneur and former DJ.
Gordon Brothers has faced significant political pressure in recent weeks, prompted by fears that the retailer’s collapse would put its 12,000 staff and 600 stores at risk.
On Wednesday, the US investment firm will appear in front of parliament’s business select committee, where it will be grilled on its efforts to find a credible buyer for Poundland.
Xyra Group was contacted for comment. Gordon Brothers declined to comment.

items.title: Why retail colleague safety must remain a priority all year round | Viewpoint: Beth Worrall
items.summary: Nobody should have to worry about their safety when they arrive at work, but for too many retail colleagues, the prospect of violence and abuse has become very real. Now, the National Week of Action to Protect Retail Workers is shining a very important spotlight… This story continues at Why retail colleague safety must remain a priority all year round | Viewpoint: Beth Worrall Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Figures from the BRC at the beginning of the year revealed that as many as 1,600 incidents happen daily. While this is an improvement on the previous year, the scale of the problem remains deeply concerning.
VoCoVo research reveals the impact this is having on teams and retailers, with almost nine in ten (88%) seeing colleagues leave their roles because of physical or verbal abuse from a customer. It’s a significant human impact – people going to work are fearing intimidation and can experience wellbeing issues long after an incident has happened.
Retailers are very much aware of the issue and are taking action to help solve it, with collaboration across the sector playing a valuable role in driving progress. The National Week of Action provides an important opportunity to recognise this, bringing the industry together to share experiences, learn from one another and continue listening to colleagues about where they feel most vulnerable.
The industry state of play
Retail colleagues are often on the receiving end of wider frustrations and pressures in society, despite having little control over the issues that customers may be angry about. But there have been some genuine steps forward to turn the tide. The Crime and Policing Bill covers a standalone offence for assaulting a retail worker, which sends a very clear message that retail teams shouldn’t be expected to deal with the current situation.
There are also some very encouraging developments in the role of collaborative technology. London-based retailers have integrated new reporting tools to submit CCTV footage within minutes to police forces. This led to an increase from 7.3% to 29.4% in reported shoplifting cases resulting in a caution.
The ability for retailers to share information with emergency services and other stakeholders is valuable in tackling organised groups and repeat offenders. Shared intelligence can give teams the power to identify patterns and respond effectively to persistent offenders. For smaller retailers, such as convenience stores with fewer resources, this data can be especially valuable.
In other cases, retailers should be sharing intelligence with each other so they can refine their strategies for future incidents. Collaboration also matters just as much within the stores themselves. When communication is easy, colleagues have the tools and confidence to reach out whenever they need support.
Helping colleagues feel supported
Clear lines of communication among teams are crucial to dealing with an unfolding incident. Whether it’s another colleague, store manager or an external security team, colleagues need a way of discreetly alerting others when they feel threatened. Communication tools, such as headsets, can help facilitate this, giving teams instant access to support. This is vital for colleagues working in isolation, such as in convenience stores late at night, giving them reassurance that help is readily available.
A combination of technologies can provide an additional layer of protection, helping colleagues feel safer. Measures such as CCTV and real-time alerts allow colleagues to keep a close eye on suspicious activity and react quickly, while AI-powered tools are analysing live footage and automatically identifying potentially suspicious behaviour. Depending on the potential danger posed by the situation, colleagues can either take steps to prevent it from escalating or alert emergency services.
Pairing this technology with clear incident response procedures and structured training can ensure a more coordinated, connected approach and instil greater confidence in teams at the same time.
Momentum needs to be sustained
The National Week of Action to Protect Retail Workers is an important opportunity to build momentum, but meaningful progress will depend on the retail industry maintaining its focus on colleague safety throughout the year. Stronger legislation is a great starting point, but more intelligence sharing and advances in technology all have a role to play in helping to protect people on the shop floor.
The success of these efforts should be measured by how safe and supported colleagues feel when they come to work. By taking a more connected and proactive approach, retailers can give their teams the confidence that help is always available and that they will never be expected to face abuse alone.
Beth Worrall, is CEO of VoCoVo

items.body:
Tackling operational refund delays with instant gift card options
When a customer shops online and needs to return an item, for example to exchange it for a different size, refunds to a bank card can typically take 3-5 working days to process. This delay can interrupt what is often a non-linear shopping journey, where customers want to re-purchase quickly.
To give customers more control, New Look introduced an optional refund to giftcard. Customers can actively choose this at the point of return with 12 months to spend the balance, or continue with a traditional refund to their original payment method.
For those who select the gift card option, funds are issued digitally as soon as the returned item reaches the distribution centre, allowing customers to re-shop sooner and manage their money more easily.
Beyond the immediate use case, the solution plays a strategic role in customer retention by keeping value within the New Look ecosystem. Rather than driving a single transaction, it encourages repeat engagement and supports an ongoing relationship between the customer and the brand.
Challenge
New Look identified an opportunity to improve the customer experience at a key moment in the shopping journey: returns and refunds. While online shopping volumes continued to grow, traditional refund processes were not always aligned with customer expectations for speed, flexibility, and digital-first experiences.
In particular, customers returning items in order to exchange for a different size or style were often required to wait several days for a refund to be processed to their original payment method before placing a new order. At the same time, New Look wanted to move away from paper-based credit notes and create a more consistent experience across in-store and online channels.
Alongside these customer experience goals, the business looked at how its existing gift card program could play a bigger role, making gift cards a core part of the business rather than a brand awareness tool.
Solution
Working with Edenred Payment Solutions, alongside existing partners ZigZag and Voucher Express, New Look launched a new refund to gift card proposition.
The solution is offered as an optional alternative during the returns process, allowing customers to actively select a gift card refund if they want faster access to their money, or to continue with a standard refund to their original payment method.
For customers who choose the gift card option, an eGift card is issued digitally as soon as the returned item arrives at New Look’s distribution centre.
Funds are available to spend immediately online or in-store, either on a replacement item or a future purchase.
Edenred Payment Solutions provides the underlying payments capabilities powering the programme, including closed-loop gift card issuance, processing, balance enquiries, top-ups, and redemption, across virtual gift cards.
The result is a more flexible, digitally enabled refund experience for customers, while supporting New Look’s wider goals around retention and brand engagement as a natural by-product of improved customer choice.
“Edenred Payment Solutions are more than a supplier. They are a partner that allows us to continually innovate and improve the customer experience. Their gift card expertise gives us the confidence to test new ideas and deliver more flexible journeys for our customers,” said Jessica Hartnett, B2C partnerships mMarketing manager, New Look.
Results
Since launching in October 2024:
- Over £2M retained within the business
- 4% uplift in customers choosing the refund to gift card option
- £270k retained within the business in one month, as refunds were re-spent rather than paid out
- 42% of customers redeemed their gift card on a subsequent purchase
- 48% uplift in basket value when customers redeemed a gift card compared to standard purchases
Conclusion
New Look’s refund to gift card programme demonstrates how optional, digitally enabled refunds can better support modern shopping behaviour, where returns and re-purchases often happen close together.
By giving customers faster access to their money and greater choice at the point of return, New Look has improved flexibility at a key moment in the customer journey.
At the same time, the programme has helped strengthen loyalty and repeat purchase, showing how customer-first design can also deliver meaningful commercial outcomes when supported by the right payments infrastructure.

items.title: Comet brand returns as an electricals marketplace
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. Fourteen years after disappearing from Britain’s high streets, one of the country’s most recognisable electricals brands has officially returned, complete with its famous black and orange identity and a new ambition to become the UK’s go-to destination for tech and electricals. First founded in 1933, Comet was part of British life for generations, the place […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
Fourteen years after disappearing from Britain’s high streets, one of the country’s most recognisable electricals brands has officially returned, complete with its famous black and orange identity and a new ambition to become the UK’s go-to destination for tech and electricals.
First founded in 1933, Comet was part of British life for generations, the place millions of families went for a new television, washing machine, games console or their latest bit of tech.
Now, more than 90 years after the name first appeared, Comet has been rebuilt for the way Britain shops today.
The new Comet launches online with more than one million products spanning TVs, mobile phones, computing, gaming, cameras, kitchen appliances and household electricals.
While the familiar name and colours are back, the old retail model isn’t. Rather than holding its own stock, Comet has returned as a dedicated electricals marketplace, bringing products from 2,500 sellers together in one specialist destination.
Cas Paton, CEO of Comet, said: “Ask almost anyone in Britain about Comet and they’ll have a memory attached to it. It might be the first TV they bought when they moved out, the family computer, a games console at Christmas or the washing machine they suddenly couldn’t live without.
“Comet is a brand that still has such a positive impression on so many people. That connection hasn’t gone away, and now we have the opportunity to bring it back for a whole new generation.
“But this isn’t about trying to recreate the Comet of the past. We want to take that nostalgia, history and trust and build something for the way people shop today. Our ambition is simple: when you need something that plugs in, we want Comet to be the first place you think of.”
The relaunch is backed by a £10 million investment as Comet looks to re-establish itself as a major force in UK electricals.
For Paton, the ambition is to ultimately build Comet into a £1 billion business. With the backing of a famous British brand and a marketplace model built for modern shoppers, the focus is on reaching that milestone as quickly as possible.
Comet’s return also creates a significant new sales opportunity for businesses operating across the electricals market.
Unlike a traditional retailer, Comet does not compete with sellers by offering its own inventory. Instead, every sale made through Comet is a sale for one of the retailers or brands on the marketplace, giving them a new route to UK shoppers under one of the most recognised names in British electricals.
Paton added: “Every sale that’s made on Comet is a sale for another retailer. We’re a friend of the retailers. We’re here to attract customers, build trust and give customers choice.”
“We want to bring some competition back to the market, but in a way that creates opportunity for retailers and brands too. Comet already means something to British shoppers. Our job now is to turn that recognition into customers and sales for the businesses selling through us.”
Comet is now welcoming new sellers ahead of its first peak trading period, as it continues to expand the range available through the marketplace.
Retailers and brands interested in selling through Comet can find more information here.

items.title: Richardson family refit ‘garage with the nice view’ Spar Low Row

The Spar store, located between Brampton and Haltwhistle on the major A69 trunk road, has undergone a complete refurbishment and an expansion of floorspace. Around 400sq ft has been added to […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Spar North of England retailer M&L Richardson & Sons Ltd are reaping the benefits from a refit at their Low Row store and forecourt.
The Spar store, located between Brampton and Haltwhistle on the major A69 trunk road, has undergone a complete refurbishment and an expansion of floorspace.
Around 400sq ft has been added to its size to accommodate a new kitchen area which has been incorporated as part of the development work, taking the space to 1,500sq ft in total.
Driving this change is the introduction of an enhanced Food To Go offering which includes a hot Clayton Park Bakery food unit. Two new Cheeky Coffee machines have also been installed too, both dispensing iced coffees, to support demand for on-the-go customers.
The comprehensive changes have also seen new energy efficient refrigeration installed throughout, modern space saving shelving has been installed, bright LED lighting fitted, and a new customer counter introduced.
Externally, the Shell forecourt is enjoying a spruce up with the latest graphics and branding, and new lighting has been fitted around the canopy.
Low Row is where things began for the Richardson family business in 1968. Nestled on the picturesque border of Cumbria and Northumberland, and a stone’s throw from Hadrian’s Wall, it became part of Spar in 2003 when the Richardsons partnered with James Hall & Co. Ltd.
Martyn Richardson is one of four brothers who are directors of M&L Richardson & Sons Ltd alongside David, Kevin, and Paul. His niece, and David’s daughter Ellie, is the first of the next generation of Richardson family members to join the business.
Martynsaid: “We are very pleased with the look and feel of the Low Row store and a huge thank you to our team and to the various departments at James Hall for their work in bringing the transformation to life.
“The development has been positive and sales have improved. We made the changes really to take greater advantage of Food To Go, especially putting in the Cheeky Coffee brand and the Clayton Park Bakery unit has meant we can improve margin and introduce link deals.”
The Richardsons have continued to grow and invest in their business over the years, currently sitting at 11 sites across Cumbria, Northumberland, and County Durham.
A standalone Spar store on English Street in central Carlisle was opened in October 2024 within the same month that the family acquired a forecourt site at Edens Lawn in Haltwhistle.
Planning has also been approved to redevelop the family’s forecourt and Spar store at Crossways in Gretna, and Spar Frizington in West Cumbria has been given the green light by planning too for an expanded, much-improved community store and brand-new forecourt.
Martyn added: “We must keep progressing. Now we have Ellie working with us as the next generation of the family, learning the business, delivering the same level of service our customers expect, and bringing in new ideas to help drive it forward.”
Ellie said: “We are known as the garage with the nice view on the A69, and when you hear that from customers who regularly stop here, I think that is quite heartwarming.
“I started in the business as I wanted to be working after the pandemic where I lost a little motivation for academic study. I switched to do a Level 2 Retail Apprenticeship instead and I immediately loved it.
“It is a crazy, demanding and fast paced industry with plenty of variety – you see new faces and deal with regular customers daily. I can say for definite that no day is the same. I have washed cars, covered shifts on the tills, and I have helped manage the car workshop at Low Row.
“I am training up to be an Area Manager, but my focus currently is the Spar store at Low Row, particularly after the recent store refit and expansion to include the kitchen. Food hygiene and safety is vital with food service and that is a growing part of the business.”
James Hall & Co. Ltd is a fifth-generation family business which serves a network of independent SPAR retailers and company-owned Spar stores across Northern England six days a week from its base at Bowland View in Preston.

items.body:
Bridal retailer wed2b is continuing its investment in large-format physical retail with the opening of its second London Megastore on Friday 6th November, following record-breaking initial sales at its Royal Victoria Dock flagship.
The new Holborn Megastore, located at 1 Thavies Inn, Holborn Circus, offers more than 10,000 sq ft of retail space and over 1,500 wedding dresses, available to browse, try on and take home the same day. Together with Royal Victoria Dock, which opened on 18 September, wed2b’s two London Megastores will offer more than 20,000 sq ft of retail space and over 3,000 wedding dresses across the capital.
The expansion follows a remarkable opening period at Royal Victoria Dock, providing encouraging early evidence of customer demand for wed2b’s investment in larger, technology-enabled bridal shopping environments. During its first six complete trading weeks, Royal Victoria Dock generated 6.6 times the average sales of stores across the rest of wed2b’s European network, while attracting 7.2 times the average store footfall.
The new flagship also significantly outperformed the retailer’s highest-performing established stores. Over the same six-week period, Royal Victoria Dock generated 144% more sales than Milton Keynes, the next highest-performing store in the network. Compared with wed2b’s former Baker Street location, Royal Victoria Dock achieved 232% higher sales during its first 44 days of trading than Baker Street recorded during the equivalent period in 2025.
The flagship’s opening period has established new company records for single-day and weekly sales, an encouraging result during a traditionally quieter period for bridal retail.
While these early results reflect a substantially larger store format and the activity surrounding its launch, they demonstrate strong initial customer interest in wed2b’s evolving retail proposition.
The opening of Holborn marks the next stage in wed2b’s development of its Megastore concept, which combines the retailer’s established no-appointment, take-home-today model with greater choice, dedicated customer spaces and technology designed to enhance the bridal shopping experience. The investment comes at a time when retailers across the UK are under increasing pressure to demonstrate the commercial value of their physical stores.
For wed2b, the strategy is about building on the strengths of its existing European network while exploring how larger, technology-enabled environments can create new opportunities for growth.
Todd Cassidy, Co-Founder and Managing Director of wed2b, said: “When we opened Royal Victoria Dock in September, we believed there was an exciting opportunity to take our retail model to another level. The response has been exceptional, with the store setting new company sales records during its opening weeks. But this isn’t simply about opening bigger shops. We’ve built wed2b around making wedding dress shopping easier, more transparent and more enjoyable, without losing any of the emotion that makes finding your dress so special. Our Megastores build on that same model, combining greater choice and immediate availability with personal service and technology that helps brides explore different styles and find what suits them Holborn represents another significant investment in physical retail, and we’re excited to continue developing the concept alongside our established stores across Europe.”
The Holborn Megastore combines the expertise of wed2b’s Bridal Experts with new digital experiences designed to make discovering the perfect dress more intuitive, engaging and enjoyable. Central to this is the installation of two AI-powered virtual try-on screens, replicating the technology introduced at Royal Victoria Dock in September. The screens have proved exceptionally popular at the first Megastore, where they are in near-constant use by brides exploring different styles and silhouettes. More than simply an entertaining experience, the technology provides a practical way for brides to preview wedding dresses from the store’s live stock selection, experiment with silhouettes they might not otherwise have considered and identify styles they would like to try on. The popularity of the experience at Royal Victoria Dock has reinforced wed2b’s belief that digital innovation can complement, rather than replace, the traditional fitting-room experience.
Brides visiting Holborn will be able to use the same technology alongside expert advice from wed2b’s Bridal Experts, before trying on their preferred dresses in person.
The store offers more than 1,500 gowns in sizes UK 6–30, with wedding dresses priced from £599 to £1,199. No appointment is required, and brides can take their chosen dress home on the day.
The importance of the physical shopping experience is also reflected in wed2b’s 2026 Bridal Report, which surveyed 11,437 brides across five European countries. The research found that 53% of brides purchased their wedding dress after visiting just one bridal boutique, highlighting the importance of the in-store experience in helping brides make confident purchasing decisions. The Megastore concept seeks to combine this personal connection with greater choice and technology that supports, rather than replaces, expert bridal advice.
The latest opening follows wed2b’s recent recognition at the Retail Week Awards 2027, where its Royal Victoria Dock Megastore has been shortlisted as a finalist in the Best New Large Store of the Year category. The shortlist places wed2b alongside some of the UK’s most established retail brands, including Matalan, Sports Direct, Superdrug and Waitrose.
The award recognises innovation and excellence in physical retail, providing further recognition of wed2b’s investment in developing its next generation of stores.
wed2b Holborn opened Friday 6th November 2026.
Address: 1 Thavies Inn, Holborn Circus, London, EC4A 1AN.

items.body:
Following continued momentum for the Reese’s brand in the UK, Reese’s is unveiling its 2026 Christmas range, bringing together a broad selection of festive formats designed to meet shopper demand across gifting, stocking fillers, sharing and snacking occasions.
The 2026 range gives retailers a broad selection of Reese’s formats and price points, from £0.75 Peanut Butter Trees through to £7.25 Minis Tins, catering to a variety of festive shopping occasions, from stocking fillers and on-the-go treats to gifting and sharing.
The Reese’s Christmas range will also feature an on-pack competition, giving customers the opportunity to win a trip or family getaway to Ibiza. The promotion adds a little extra magic to the festive season and provides retailers with an engaging shopper proposition during the key festive trading period.
REESE’S 2026 CHRISTMAS RANGE INCLUDES:
- Reese’s 4pc Selection Box (157g) – RRP £3.70: A gift-ready selection of Reese’s favourites in a compact seasonal format, suited to gifting and stocking fillers.
- Reese’s Peanut Butter Filled Santa’s (55g) – RRP £2.00: A festive Santa-shaped format filled with Reese’s signature peanut butter, ideal for seasonal gifting and impulse occasions.
- Reese’s Advent Calendar (245g) – RRP £6.80: A 24-day Christmas countdown featuring individually portioned Reese’s treats, offering a strong seasonal gifting opportunity.
- Reese’s Peanut Butter Tree (34g) – RRP £0.75: A seasonal Reese’s favourite at a convenient, accessible price point, making it well suited to stocking fillers and on-the-go purchases.
- Reese’s 10 Cups Giant Bar (154g) – RRP £4.00: Ten Reese’s Peanut Butter Cups brought together in one standout format, designed for sharing or gifting.
- Reese’s King Size Peanut Butter Tree (68g) – RRP £1.30: A larger festive tree format offering an elevated option for seasonal treating and gifting.
- Reese’s Minis Tin (309g) – RRP £7.25: A generous format designed for sharing and gifting, providing a premium-looking seasonal option for Reese’s fans.
- Reese’s 5pc Selection Box (284g) – RRP £6.30: A larger selection box bringing together a variety of Reese’s favourites, ideal for gifting and premium seasonal snacking.
With a broad range of formats and pricing, the 2026 Christmas collection is designed to help retailers maximise opportunities throughout the festive shopping period, from early Christmas purchases and stocking fillers to gifting and at-home sharing.
The range also provides strong opportunities for visibility across seasonal confectionery fixtures and gifting displays, helping Reese’s stand out during one of the key trading periods of the year.
The Reese’s 2026 Christmas range will be available across UK retail outlets, including Tesco, Sainsbury’s, ASDA, Morrison’s and other major supermarkets, convenience and wholesale, availability subject to retailer.

items.body:
The Pets Foundation, Pets at Home’s corporate foundation, is committing £1.2 million over three years to help fund Dogs Trust’s Behaviour Support Line, giving more dog owners access to free, expert advice when they are struggling with their dog’s behaviour.
Demand for behavioural support is growing, with Dogs Trust’s Behaviour Support Line having helped more than 35,000 dog owners since launching as a pilot in 2022. In the last year alone, 19,000 owners were supported, with over 40,000 calls completed. The team forecasts demand will continue to grow, with more than 20,000 dogs expected to be supported this year.
The £1.2 million investment reflects The Pets Foundation’s commitment to tackling the underlying causes that can lead to pets being given up. With behaviour-related issues accounting for over a third of dogs handed over to Dogs Trust, the funding will focus on early intervention, helping owners access trusted support before challenges escalate to the point where they feel unable to cope. Pets at Home stores, petcare advisors, and Vets for Pets practices will also help signpost owners to the Behaviour Support Line, making support easier to find.
The investment marks the next chapter in a 14-year relationship between Pets at Home and Dogs Trust, which has generated more than £6 million in value for the charity and supported over 100,000 dogs and their owners. Over the years, Pets at Home Group has supported Dogs Trust in a variety of ways, from providing food and essentials for dogs in its care to supporting veterinary care and local rehoming centres. The new funding builds on this relationship with a shared focus on helping more dogs stay in loving homes.
Behavioural challenges can place significant pressure on owners and their relationships with their dogs, making access to early, trusted support an important part of helping prevent problems from escalating.
Dogs Trust’s Behaviour Support Line provides free, expert advice to all dog owners, offering a supportive and non-judgemental place to turn when they need help. As demand has increased, the service has expanded its opening hours and grown from a pilot team of three to a specialist team of over 20, with nearly two thirds of all callers getting the support they need over the phone.
Amy Angus, Head of Charity Partnership and Communities at Pets at Home, said:
“We know just how much pets mean to the people who love them, but behavioural challenges can sometimes leave owners feeling overwhelmed.
“The Behaviour Support Line gives owners somewhere to turn when they’re struggling, before those challenges reach a point of crisis. We want people to know that asking for help is okay, that they won’t be judged, and that giving up a much-loved pet isn’t their only option.
“That’s why we’re investing significantly in the helpline. By making trusted, expert advice easier for owners to access, we hope to tackle one of the key reasons dogs are given up and help more pets stay where they belong, in loving homes.”
Maria Murray, Dogs Trust Behaviour and Community Services Director said:
“We’re incredibly grateful to The Pets Foundation for this significant investment and proud to be continuing a relationship with Pets at Home that has lasted more than a decade. What has always united us is a shared ambition to make life better for dogs and the people who love them.
“The real value of this funding will be felt long beyond an individual phone call. Giving an owner the right advice at the right time can change the course of a dog’s life, building understanding and confidence and, in some cases, helping a family stay together. With The Pets Foundation’s support, we’ll be able to make that difference for many more dogs and their owners.”
The Behaviour Support Line in action – Barney’s Story
The difference the right behavioural support can make can be seen in Barney’s story. Barney settled in well after moving into foster care, but his carers became concerned that he was resource guarding. This is a behaviour where a dog becomes protective of something they consider valuable, such as food, toys or other possessions. Barney could become protective around his food bowl, a favourite toy or even a shoe, particularly when the other dog in the home came close.
His foster carers managed the situation by feeding the dogs separately, toys were supervised, and situations that might cause conflict were avoided, but another incident occurred and they contacted Dogs Trust’s Behaviour Support Line for additional support.
After talking through Barney’s routine and behaviour, the team helped his carers understand the anxiety behind his resource guarding and suggested some simple changes. These included feeding Barney before his morning walk to reduce the anticipation around mealtimes, preventing him from entering the kitchen while food was being prepared, and giving him plenty of uninterrupted space while eating. They were also given practical guidance on managing resource guarding and relationships within a multi-dog household.
“Once we understood why Barney was behaving the way he was, it all started to make much more sense. We had a plan to follow and felt much more confident moving forward,” said his foster carer, James.
With the new routine and management in place, there were no further incidents, and Barney became calmer and more settled.
“The difference was huge,” said James, “We could all relax a bit more, and Barney seemed much happier too.”
After six weeks in foster care, he found a loving new home and was adopted in July 2026, where he has continued to thrive.
His story shows how understanding the reasons behind a dog’s behaviour, and getting support when you need it, can make all the difference. With a little patience, the right advice and plenty of love, Barney was able to put his best paw forward and start the next chapter of his life.

items.body:
Herne Bay Co-op re-opens its doors and welcomes the community back in-store following a near four-week investment programme to enhance the store.
The store – located in Reculver Road in the Herne Bay community of Beltinge – opens between 7am-10pm daily and conveniently offers Co-op’s extensive range and choice of fresh and healthy products, meal ideas, food to go, Fairtrade products; an extended in-store bakery, and award-winning chilled beers and wines.
There is also a focus on seasonal food and drink, including Co-op’s Christmas sandwich range packed with festive flavours.
The online home delivery of groceries is available through Just Eat, Uber Eats and Deliveroo – with orders picked fresh in the store and delivered quickly and conveniently in the community.
New refrigeration has been installed throughout which is not only more energy efficient and supports Co-op’s carbon reduction journey, but also extends the range and choice of fresh and frozen goods.
Added services include Lottery; payment services via PayPoint and an ATM providing access to cash in the community.
Soft plastic recycling is also available so shoppers can return and recycle materials that are often not universally accepted via household kerbside recycling, such as crisp packets and bread bags, lids from ready meals, biscuit wrappers and, pet food pouches.
Karen Butler, Co-op’s store manager, said: “We are delighted to re-open, and the whole team is really enjoying welcoming our members and customers back into the store – we have had a great response. We work to ensure the store is a hub contributing to local life and meeting the needs of our community. With a focus on offering quality products, value and choice that can be enjoyed by everyone, we have deals and promotions throughout the store, and a range of added services to make everyday life easier. We’re proud to have the opportunity to serve Herne Bay, the team is here to contribute to local life and conveniently serve and support the community.”
Committed to backing British agriculture, all of Co-op’s own meat, poultry and dairy is 100% British – including in its pies, ready meals and sandwiches.
Fairtrade products are available across the store supporting farmers, workers and their communities around the world who grow and produce products and ingredients for Co-op.
With its history dating back more than 180 years, Co-op is one of the world’s largest consumer-owned co-operatives. Co-op exists to create value for its membership and communities, its more than 7.6 million members own the business and play an intrinsic part in the governance of the organisation.
More information about the benefits of Co-op Membership is available by visiting coop.co.uk/membership

Cafédirect is expanding its whole bean organic coffee range with the launch of its award-winning Mayan Gold in a new 750g format, available in Tesco from 9 November 2026, as well as through the Cafédirect website and selected online retailers. The launch comes as Britain’s love of café-quality coffee at home continues to grow, with […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
Cafédirect is expanding its whole bean organic coffee range with the launch of its award-winning Mayan Gold in a new 750g format, available in Tesco from 9 November 2026, as well as through the Cafédirect website and selected online retailers.
The launch comes as Britain’s love of café-quality coffee at home continues to grow, with UK bean-to-cup coffee machine sales reportedly rising by 33.5% and whole bean coffee sales increasing by 20.3% in volume over the past year¹.
And with Christmas approaching, coffee-making equipment is firmly on shoppers’ wish lists. New research from Lakeland reveals that 28% of Brits would welcome a coffee machine or coffee-making accessories as a Christmas gift², making Mayan Gold 750g a timely addition for coffee lovers looking to get the most from their home brewing experience.
Designed for engaged whole bean drinkers using bean-to-cup machines or grinding their own beans, the new 750g pack offers a convenient, better-value way to enjoy great coffee at home. Building on the success of Cafédirect’s existing Machu Picchu 750g format, the launch provides a natural trade-up opportunity for loyal Mayan Gold 200g shoppers, while giving Machu Picchu fans an exciting new single origin flavour to explore.
Sourced from the highlands of Mexico, including Chiapas, Mayan Gold is a single origin Arabica coffee that captures the rich character of its origins.
Grown among misty cloud forests and lush tropical jungle, where shade and mist help coffee cherries ripen slowly, Mayan Gold is celebrated for its smooth, rounded character and natural sweetness.
Warm, smooth and naturally sweet, the coffee offers soft caramel notes that develop into rich brown sugar and light molasses. Its dark roast delivers a velvety body, gentle acidity and a beautifully balanced, warm and lingering finish.
Versatile enough to suit a variety of brewing methods, Mayan Gold is ideal for bean-to-cup and espresso machines, as well as moka pots, AeroPress, pour-over, filter coffee and cafetières. Whether coffee lovers prefer a rich morning espresso or a leisurely cafetière, Mayan Gold makes it easy to enjoy great-tasting coffee at home.
For shoppers who care about more than just what’s in their cup, Cafédirect combines exceptional coffee with a commitment to putting growers first.
Founded in 1991, Cafédirect has spent more than 30 years championing a fairer way of doing business and building long-term relationships with coffee-growing communities.
As a pioneer of Fairtrade coffee in the UK, a social enterprise and a certified B Corp, Cafédirect is committed to making great coffee that benefits the people who grow it. Mayan Gold is both Organic and Fairtrade certified, offering consumers the reassurance that their everyday coffee choice supports more responsible farming and fairer trading practices.
And Cafédirect’s commitment goes beyond certification. The brand works closely with farmer cooperatives, giving growers a voice in the business and investing in initiatives designed to improve livelihoods and support more resilient coffee-growing communities.
Central to this approach is Cafédirect’s living income commitment, making it the first UK company to commit to paying Living Income Reference Prices by 2030, helping coffee farmers earn enough to support their families, invest in their farms and build a more secure future.
For coffee lovers seeking great taste, better value and a brand that shares their values, Mayan Gold 750g brings all three together.
Paige Langran, senior brand manager, Cafédirect, comments: “There’s something special about making a really great cup of coffee at home, and we’re seeing more people embrace that experience. Whether they’ve invested in a bean-to-cup machine or love grinding their own beans, coffee drinkers are becoming more adventurous about the flavours and origins they choose.
“Following the success of our Machu Picchu 750g coffee, we’re delighted to introduce Mayan Gold in the same larger format. With its beautifully smooth character, natural caramel sweetness and rich brown sugar notes, it’s a fantastic choice for coffee lovers looking to explore new flavours, while giving existing Mayan Gold fans more of the coffee they love. Sales are up over 20% year on year on our 750g packs, showing our customers not only want ethical coffee, but to stock up on more of their favourite coffee.
“And for us, great coffee isn’t just about how it tastes. From our Fairtrade and Organic credentials to our commitment to supporting living incomes for coffee farmers, we’re working to make coffee better for the people who grow it, too.
“We believe you shouldn’t have to choose between great taste and doing the right thing. With Cafédirect, you can have both of these. That’s what we mean by coffee done right.”
Cafédirect Mayan Gold 750g Whole Bean Coffee launches on 9 November 2026 in Tesco, on the Cafédirect website and through selected online retailers. RRP £17.25.

Virgin Atlantic Holidays is expanding its partnership with Marks & Spencer, bringing its expert holiday planning service to M&S customers with a new concession at the M&S store in Westfield White City.
Opening in December 2026, the new concession will give customers the opportunity to discover, plan and book their next Virgin Atlantic Holiday while visiting one of London’s leading shopping destinations.
Dedicated Virgin Atlantic Holidays travel experts will be on hand to offer personalised advice and help customers create long-haul holidays tailored to them – whether they’re looking for a luxury escape, multi-centre adventure, family getaway or a once-in-a-lifetime experience.
The new concession marks the next chapter in Virgin Atlantic’s growing relationship with M&S, following the loyalty partnership launched earlier this year linking M&S Sparks with Virgin Red. That partnership gives members more ways to earn, spend and be rewarded across both programmes. The introduction of Virgin Atlantic Holidays concession brings travel inspiration and holiday planning into the relationship too, creating another way for customers to engage with the two brands.
The expansion supports Virgin Atlantic Holidays’ ambition to grow its presence in London and reach more of the capital’s premium leisure travellers. It follows the recent announcement of a new Virgin Atlantic Holidays flagship store at Battersea Power Station, with the growing London retail network giving customers more ways to access the brand’s expert, personalised holiday planning service.
Dave Geer, Chief Commercial Officer, Virgin Atlantic, commented: “We’re really excited to build on our partnership with Marks & Spencer bringing Virgin Atlantic Holidays to even more customers in London.
“M&S is a brand people know and love, and this new concession gives customers another convenient way to start thinking about, planning and booking their next holiday. Our travel experts can help customers go beyond simply choosing a destination – sharing their knowledge and recommendations to create a holiday that really makes the most of every moment, whether that’s a Maldives escape, a multi-centre adventure across Seoul and Japan or a road trip across the US.
“Together with our new flagship store at Battersea Power Station, this opening is an important part of our investment in London and our ambition to make Virgin Atlantic Holidays more visible and accessible across the capital.”

The expansion will create thousands of opportunities for people to build their careers, with new baristas joining more than 18,000 employees already bringing the Starbucks Experience to life […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
Starbucks is set to welcome 7,500 new baristas across the UK over the next five years, alongside its plan to open 500 new coffeehouses across the country.
The expansion will create thousands of opportunities for people to build their careers, with new baristas joining more than 18,000 employees already bringing the Starbucks Experience to life for customers every day.
People in the Midlands, North of England, Wales and Scotland will see the most Starbucks jobs coming to their communities, with approximately 80 per cent of new coffeehouses targeted in areas north of the M25.
Darren King, vice president and managing director, Starbucks UK, said: ‘We’re proud to be creating thousands of new jobs across the UK over the next five years, bringing new opportunities to communities across the country as we continue to invest and grow here.
At the heart of our Back to Starbucks strategy is our ambition to create a place where people can build skills, grow their careers and feel part of a team. We’re deeply focused on how we can help more young people into these positions, starting by making entry level roles as accessible as possible. You don’t need previous industry experience and we’ll give you the training and support you need from day one’.
Starbucks is a major employer of young people in the UK with more than half (53 per cent) of partners in Starbucks company-operated stores under the age of 24.
Helen Dickinson, chief executive of the BRC, said: “At a time when too many young people are struggling to get a foot on the career ladder, this investment is hugely welcome. Retail and hospitality are vital routes into the workplace, helping young people build skills, confidence and experience while offering genuine opportunities to progress. Starbucks commitment to thousands of new jobs shows the important role the industry can play in opening doors for the next generation.”
To better understand young people’s perceptions of customer-facing roles in retail and hospitality, Starbucks commissioned research with Ipsos involving approximately 3,400 young people. The findings revealed that of the 18-35-year-olds surveyed who are currently, or have previously worked in a customer-facing job in the retail or hospitality industry (n=2392), 83% think the experience has helped them develop skills that will be useful in their working life including customer service skills, communication and teamwork.
Despite this, many young people do not see retail and hospitality as a long-term career path. Just 10% of those currently working in customer-facing roles in these sectors expect to remain in their role for more than 10 years. More generally, 68% of 18–35-year-olds surveyed agree that retail and hospitality roles are perceived as temporary or ‘stopgap’ work.
To help challenge this perception, Starbucks is creating more opportunities for baristas to grow their careers as the business grows, with clear pathways from a first job to a lasting career.
With more than 6,000 leaders already working in coffeehouses across the country, Starbucks is investing further in its leadership pipeline by creating an additional 140 deputy store manager roles. This builds on existing initiatives, including its Accelerated Leadership Programme, designed to give baristas an accelerated route into leadership and help them build the skills to become store manager-ready in approximately 13 months, compared with a journey that would typically take around three years.
Starbucks is also expanding the routes available for employees to learn, develop and build long-term careers with the business. It has committed to a further 200 apprenticeship places over the next year, building on the more than 2,000 employees who have already taken part in its fee-free apprenticeship programme. Opportunities span from Level 2 entry-level barista apprenticeships through to advanced professional qualifications for senior leaders, giving employees the chance to continue developing at every stage of their career.
The findings also come as routes into work are changing for young people. The research found that 68%* of those surveyed agree that AI is reducing traditional entry-level jobs available to young people aged 18-25. At the same time, almost one million 16–24-year-olds in the UK are currently not in education, employment or training.
King added: “These findings show that we need to rethink how we value hospitality careers. Working face-to-face with customers, colleagues and managers helps build vital interpersonal skills that can provide the foundation for any career, with 83% of young people with experience in these roles recognising the valuable skills they gain. But beyond developing transferable skills, we want more young people to see the opportunities to build a rewarding career in hospitality.
“That’s why we’re creating more ways for people to grow and progress at Starbucks. For those with a passion for coffee, programmes like Coffee Masters recognise our most skilled baristas and offer advanced coffee education. And for those who want to explore a different path, there are opportunities across our wider business, from beverage development to finance, marketing and much more.”

items.title: ShopKind Week and National Week of Action puts retail crime and abuse in the spotlight
items.summary: A joint national week of action to tackle retail abuse and crime, backed by policing minister Sarah Jones, is bringing together the retail sector, policing and partners and uniting four national campaigns for the first time from today, Monday 9 November. The Association of Convenience… This story continues at ShopKind Week and National Week of Action puts retail crime and abuse in the spotlight Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
The Association of Convenience Stores (ACS), Usdaw, the Retail Trust and the National Business Crime Centre (NBCC) are joining forces for a coordinated response to the scale of the issue, combining activity in shops and workplaces with public campaigning.
Running from 9 -15 November 2026, the partnership will unite ACS’s ShopKind, Usdaw’s Respect for Shopworkers Week, the Retail Trust’s Let’s Respect Retail and NBCC’s Safer Business Action Week.
Together, they will encourage respect for retail workers, call on shoppers to change their behaviour and support practical action against crime affecting businesses and their communities.
Preparations span workplace events, public advertising and support for retailers to take part in stores, alongside a coordinated policing response.
Partner activity planned for the week includes:
- ACS – ShopKind: With 173 supporting organisations, ShopKind will be promoted through national and trade media, with updated materials for stores and social media. Supporters are being encouraged to publicly endorse the campaign and nominate ShopKind Champions to share its messages.
- Usdaw – Respect for Shopworkers Week: Representative-led campaigning is planned in around 1,000 retail workplaces, backed by major retailers. Messages will ask shoppers to “Keep Your Cool” and workers to “Report It – Sort It”. Usdaw will also release interim findings from its 2026 Freedom From Fear survey of retail workers’ experiences.
- Retail Trust – Let’s Respect Retail: A new report by the charity will show the scale of shop staff abuse and its impact on workers, alongside calls for shoppers to treat shop workers respectfully appearing in thousands of stores, shop windows, shopping centres, cinemas and transport hubs. Employees at some of the country’s biggest retailers and shopping centres are also being given more support by the Retail Trust to help them respond to and deal with abusive incidents.
- NBCC – Safer Business Action Week: The NBCC is coordinating the policing response, with 20 forces already confirming participation. Forces are encouraged to work with businesses, Business Crime Reduction Partnerships and Business Improvement Districts on local activity covering prevention, intelligence, enforcement and engagement. This could include targeting prolific offenders, sharing intelligence on crime hotspots and improving incident reporting.
Crime and policing minister Sarah Jones said: “Retail workers are the backbone of our high streets, and no one should face abuse, threats or violence simply for doing their job.
“I am proud to support this national week of action, which brings together retailers, police and local partners to tackle the abuse, theft and antisocial behaviour that affects communities across the country.
“Shop theft is finally falling and there are thousands more neighbourhood police on our streets. But we won’t stop there. We are clear that retail crime is not minor and those responsible will be held accountable.”
Superintendent Lisa Maslen, National Business Crime Centre lead, said: “The strength of this week is the partnership behind it. Bringing all four campaigns together for the first time means we can reach more businesses, hear directly from shopworkers and turn that shared commitment into local action.
“With 20 police forces already signed up, preparations are gathering pace. Alongside our partners’ work in stores and communities, policing will focus on preventing crime, sharing intelligence and targeting the offenders causing the greatest harm.”
Association of Convenience Stores chief executive Ed Woodall said: “We are delighted at the support for the ShopKind campaign shown in thousands of shops across the UK and believe that bringing ShopKind Week together with leading awareness campaigns from shopworkers union USDAW, the Retail Trust and the National Business Crime Centre, sends a clear united message that colleagues shouldn’t have to face abuse, that the businesses they work for will report incidents, and that the police will respond effectively.
“Together with the backing of tougher legislation, we can make a real positive difference to hundreds of thousands of people working in our nation’s local shops.”
The four partners have been encouraging businesses to use campaign materials, involve staff and link up with their local police and business partnerships to plan activity during the week.

items.summary: Virgin Atlantic Holidays has expanded its partnership with M&S with plans to open a concession at the retailer’s Westfield White City store. Due to open in December 2026, the concession will offer shoppers personalised advice and booking services for long-haul holidays, including family trips, multi-centre breaks and luxury escapes. items.body:
Virgin Atlantic Holidays has expanded its partnership with M&S with plans to open a concession at the retailer’s Westfield White City store.
Due to open in December 2026, the concession will offer shoppers personalised advice and booking services for long-haul holidays, including family trips, multi-centre breaks and luxury escapes.
The latest announcement forms part of the travel company’s wider investment in London, following its recently announced flagship at Battersea Power Station.
It also builds on the loyalty partnership launched earlier this year between M&S Sparks and Virgin Red, which gives members more ways to earn and spend rewards across the two programmes.
The concession will extend that relationship into in-store holiday planning as Virgin Atlantic Holidays looks to reach more of the capital’s premium leisure travellers.
Virgin Atlantic chief commercial officer Dave Geer said: “M&S is a brand people know and love, and this new concession gives customers another convenient way to start thinking about, planning and booking their next holiday.”
He added: “Together with our new flagship store at Battersea Power Station, this opening is an important part of our investment in London and our ambition to make Virgin Atlantic Holidays more visible and accessible across the capital.”

items.title: Peak season 2026: What’s changed, and how do you win?
items.summary: Retailers are, of course, now entering into another golden quarter. However, this year looks slightly different. Whilst the core challenge of the season remains, supply chain disruption, changing shopper habits and a good portion of uncertainty mean that many leaders are struggling to see what peak this year is going to look like. To get...
items.body:
Retailers are, of course, now entering into another golden quarter. However, this year looks slightly different. Whilst the core challenge of the season remains, supply chain disruption, changing shopper habits and a good portion of uncertainty mean that many leaders are struggling to see what peak this year is going to look like.
To get to the heart of peak preparedness, Retail Gazette’s Unpacked podcast catches up with Charlotte Jamieson, VP advertiser and agency partnerships at Cardlytics to delve into the company’s recent research, and find out why some unexpected strategic tweaks could ensure that 2026’s golden quarter is a success.
“The whole landscape of retail has changed, and the golden quarter will be no exception to that,” says Jamieson. “What the data shows us is that shoppers are managing their budgets hard, even at Christmas. They’re shopping around, they’re trading down, they’re breaking old brand loyalties. We do see that they’re still spending, but only when something prompts them.”
“For retailers, it’s not whether the demand exists, but if you’re shopping up for shoppers at the right time, with the right relevance, and with the right value,” Jamieson adds.
Listen now to find out more, and check out the Retail Gazette Golden Guide ’26 for more insight into how to win this season.

items.title: Greggs and Too Good To Go save over 7m bags of surplus food
items.summary: Greggs and Too Good To Go have reportedly saved more than seven million bags of surplus food from going to waste since launching their partnership in 2021. The bakery chain…
items.body:
Greggs and Too Good To Go save over 7m bags of surplus food
Greggs and Too Good To Go have reportedly saved more than seven million bags of surplus food from going to waste since launching their partnership in 2021.
The bakery chain has worked with the food waste reduction platform for five years, offering customers discounted surplus products through its app.
The partnership allows shoppers to purchase Surprise Bags containing unsold food from Greggs stores at the end of the day and in the early morning, alongside Grab Bags featuring surplus hot food at various points throughout the day.
Greggs Grab Bags are now available in more than 2,000 shops across the UK, with prices starting at £2.99.
Customers can reserve and pay for the bags through the free Too Good To Go app before collecting them from their chosen store, with contents depending on what is available.
Too Good To Go UK and Ireland managing director Chelsea Kerr said: “Autumn is a great reminder of why partnerships like ours with Greggs matter. Routines get busier, budgets get tighter, and people want food that’s convenient and good value.
“Greggs has been partnered with us for five years, and together we’ve shown how a much-loved high street brand can make preventing food waste part of everyday life.”
The initiative forms part of Greggs’ efforts to reduce food waste across its store estate while offering customers lower-cost food options.
Greggs retail operations director Gillian Long said: “Our partnership with Too Good To Go plays an important role in redistributing unsold food.
“Whether it’s a bake, sandwich or sweet treat that’s being saved, it gives our customers a simple way to pick up something they love while helping us make sure good food doesn’t go to waste.”

items.summary: Marks & Spencer has appointed former Waitrose executive Alan Hoe as its new head of customer experience and operations, bringing more than two decades of grocery retail experience to the…
items.body:
M&S appoints former Waitrose executive Alan Hoe as customer experience boss
Marks & Spencer has appointed former Waitrose executive Alan Hoe as its new head of customer experience and operations, bringing more than two decades of grocery retail experience to the business.
Hoe joins the retailer after spending 21 years at Waitrose, where he held several positions, including retail proposition lead for front end and services.
Most recently, he worked as a consultant at customer experience consultancy CLX, advising on customer experience.
His appointment comes as M&S continues to invest in improving its stores, customer experience and operational efficiency as part of its wider transformation strategy.
The retailer recently reported a strong performance across its food business, with sales rising 13.9 per cent to £5.16bn in the 26 weeks to 26 September.
Like-for-like food sales increased 11.7 per cent, while adjusted operating profit climbed to £288.6m as the supermarket continued to attract shoppers through investment in value, quality and innovation.
M&S has also been accelerating investment in its store estate, completing 18 new, extended or renewed stores during the first half as it looks to improve the shopping experience and drive further growth.
