items.title: Morrisons unveils Goldilocks-inspired Christmas advert starring the Three Bears
items.summary: Morrisons has unveiled its 2026 Christmas advert, putting a modern twist on Goldilocks and the Three Bears to celebrate the personal touches that make the festive season special. The supermarket’s…
items.body:
Morrisons unveils Goldilocks-inspired Christmas advert starring the Three Bears
Morrisons has unveiled its 2026 Christmas advert, putting a modern twist on Goldilocks and the Three Bears to celebrate the personal touches that make the festive season special.
The supermarket’s 90-second campaign, titled ‘Christmas Made Just Right’, will debut on ITV, Channel 4, Five and Sky TV today at 9.15pm.
The advert follows Mummy and Daddy Bear as they prepare to welcome their grown-up son and his new girlfriend home for Christmas.
Daddy Bear visits Morrisons Market Street, where the supermarket’s skilled bakers, butchers, fishmongers and deli colleagues help him prepare the family’s festive feast, including an enormous salmon.
Meanwhile, Mummy Bear attempts to get the family home ready, with a few mishaps along the way.
When Baby Bear finally arrives, his girlfriend is revealed to be Goldilocks, who discovers a warm and welcoming Christmas celebration complete with a wonky tree, mismatched decorations and a carefully prepared festive spread.
The campaign aims to showcase Morrisons’ ‘fresh food expertise and its ability to cater to different tastes and family traditions’.
Morrisons marketing and advertising director Beverley Lumb said: “Everyone has their own idea of what makes Christmas ‘just right’ alongside their own family traditions that make the day feel truly magical.
“As Christmas comes in all shapes and sizes, we pride ourselves on delivering good, honest value, ensuring every piece of festive fare is crafted with the thought, care and quality for everyone gathered around your table.”
The advert was created by Leo UK and directed by Nick Ball, whose previous work includes campaigns for Tesco, Ikea and Uber Eats.
The Three Bears are brought to life using animatronics, with each character given their own distinct personality.
Alongside the TV campaign, Morrisons is launching a series of social media activations, including a Baby Bear takeover, teaser content across Instagram and TikTok, and a special Gogglebox partnership featuring the show’s stars reacting to the advert.
The supermarket is also releasing an exclusive cuddly bear toy, with 50p from every sale donated to Marie Curie.
Leo UK chief creative officer Andrew Long said: “Goldilocks and the Three Bears is a story generations know, but people experience stories very differently today.
“So we’ve built the campaign to work in different ways too: our Christmas TV spot tells the parents’ story, while our social takeover gives Baby Bear his own voice.”

items.title: More than half of shop workers face weekly abuse as attacks surge ahead of Christmas
items.summary: More than half of UK shop workers are now facing abuse every week, with rising violence, intimidation and unwanted filming prompting calls for shoppers to show greater respect ahead of the Christmas trading period. New research from the Retail Trust found that 54 per cent of retail workers experience abuse weekly, up from 43 per...
items.body:
More than half of UK shop workers are now facing abuse every week, with rising violence, intimidation and unwanted filming prompting calls for shoppers to show greater respect ahead of the Christmas trading period.
New research from the Retail Trust found that 54 per cent of retail workers experience abuse weekly, up from 43 per cent last year and 33 per cent in 2024.
The charity’s annual survey of 1,138 shop workers revealed that 79 per cent had experienced abuse or violence from members of the public over the past year, compared with 77 per cent in 2025.
Almost a quarter reported experiencing abuse involving a physical attack, while 38 per cent said they or a colleague had been filmed without consent, up from 30 per cent last year.
The findings highlight the growing impact of retail crime and aggressive customer behaviour on staff wellbeing, with 70 per cent of those affected by abuse reporting stress or anxiety about going to work.
More than a third said they felt unsafe at work, while 48 per cent admitted that worsening abuse had made them consider quitting their job or leaving retail altogether, up from 43 per cent in 2025.
Meanwhile, 84 per cent had witnessed shoplifting over the past year, with 35 per cent witnessing it daily.
The Retail Trust is launching its nationwide ‘Let’s Respect Retail‘ campaign today, urging shoppers to show greater kindness towards store workers during the busy festive period.
The initiative, backed by retailers including Sainsbury’s, Next, Currys, EE and Holland & Barrett, will see messages encouraging customers to ‘start with hello’ displayed across thousands of stores, shopping centres, cinemas and railway stations.
Retail Trust chief executive Chris Brook-Carter said: “Our country’s shop workers have had enough of being shouted at, threatened, and treated with contempt.
“We’re hearing from people who are frightened to come into work because they don’t know what they’ll face that day, and from others who have been pushed to breaking point by repeated abuse.”
He added that aggressive customer behaviour was increasingly being viewed as part of the job, damaging staff morale and driving experienced workers out of the sector.
British Retail Consortium chief executive Helen Dickinson said: “No one should go to work fearing for their safety, yet the Retail Trust’s findings are a stark reminder that violence and abuse against retail workers remain endemic.”
Sainsbury’s chief retail, logistics and supply chain officer Tracey Clements said the supermarket was investing heavily in measures to identify offenders, prevent them from returning to stores and work with police to hold them accountable.
“No retailer can tackle this alone and we’re standing with the Retail Trust to ask everyone to treat the colleagues helping them with the kindness and respect they deserve,” she said.
The campaign also has the backing of retail entrepreneur Theo Paphitis, who said kindness was essential to creating a positive working environment for store teams.
Despite the findings, the Retail Trust’s research revealed that 83% of employees said just one positive customer interaction during their shift could help them recover from a negative experience.
The campaign is being delivered alongside the Association of Convenience Stores, shopworkers’ union Usdaw and the National Business Crime Centre as part of a dedicated week of action tackling violence and abuse against retail workers.

items.body:
Morrisons Christmas advert will make its national TV debut on Monday 9th November at 9.15pm on multiple major networks including ITV, Channel 4, Five and Sky TV with a modern retelling of the Goldilocks story in which everyone likes things a little differently. For the early birds, highlight clips will also be dropping across Instagram and TikTok from 6:00am.
The new 90-second ad brings Goldilocks and the Three Bears together for Christmas, playing on the familiar idea that everyone likes things a little differently. At its heart are Morrisons skilled bakers, butchers, fishmongers and deli colleagues, who make and prepare food in store and help customers find the right cuts, portions and food for their own Christmas tables.
The advert tells the familiar story of a Mum and Dad preparing for their grown-up child to bring a partner home for Christmas for the first time. It just so happens that these parents are Mummy & Daddy Bear.
Daddy Bear heads to Morrisons Market Street, where its skilled fresh food makers help him prepare the family’s festive spread including an enormous salmon, with expert cooking instructions provided by a Morrisons Fishmonger to ensure it’s ‘just right’ for the big day. At home Mummy Bear sets about making the house just right, with a few bear-shaped mishaps along the way. When Baby Bear finally arrives, his new girlfriend is revealed as Goldilocks.
As ‘Goldie’ steps inside, she finds a Christmas that is warm and welcoming rather than fairy-tale flawless. The tree is wonky, the decorations and place settings do not match and her chair is showing signs of disrepair. Her face lights up at the beautiful, homely Christmas and mouthwatering spread with a perfectly sized place setting for each of them. As she sits down to dinner, it is clear that everything has been chosen and prepared with love and care, especially for her.
The advert ends with the campaign line: “Christmas Made Just Right”.
Beverley Lumb, Marketing and Advertising Director at Morrisons, said: “Everyone has their own idea of what makes Christmas ‘just right’ alongside their own family traditions that make the day feel truly magical. As Christmas comes in all shapes and sizes, we pride ourselves on delivering good, honest value, ensuring every piece of festive fare is crafted with the thought, care and quality for everyone gathered around your table.”
“From award-winning smoked salmon and perfectly sliced glazed Christmas ham, to golden mince pies, freshly baked in store or British-grown fresh veg, our skilled bakers, fishmongers, butchers, and deli teams craft fresh food daily and help customers find exactly what they need, from the right cut to the perfect portion.”
The ad was directed by award-winning film maker Nick Ball, whose credits include campaigns for Uber Eats, Tesco and IKEA and work with Mariah Carey, Chris Hemsworth, Tina Fey and Christopher Walken. The Three Bears are brought to life as animatronic characters, with each given their own personality and performance.
Andrew Long, Chief Creative Officer at Leo UK, said: “There’s a huge amount of craft in bringing a family everyone knows to life and giving each bear their own personality. For us at Leo, this is also a great example of Populist Creativity that gets people talking. Goldilocks and the Three Bears is a story generations know, but people experience stories very differently today. So we’ve built the campaign to work in different ways too: our Christmas TV spot tells the parents’ story, while our social takeover gives Baby Bear his own voice. Each generation gets its own way into the story, just as Morrisons helps people make Christmas ‘just right’ for all the different tastes around their table. ”
For little ones who are eager to bring the magic to life, Morrisons is launching an exclusive cuddly bear plush toy, with 50p from the sale of every bear being donated to Marie Curie.

Morrisons marketing and advertising director Beverley Lumb said: “Everyone has their own idea of what makes Christmas ‘just right’ alongside their own family traditions that make the day feel truly magical.
“As Christmas comes in all shapes and sizes, we pride ourselves on delivering good, honest value, ensuring every piece of festive fare is crafted with the thought, care and quality for everyone gathered around your table.”
The advert was created by Leo UK and directed by Nick Ball, whose previous work includes campaigns for Tesco, Ikea and Uber Eats.
The Three Bears are brought to life using animatronics, with each character given their own distinct personality.
Alongside the TV campaign, Morrisons is launching a series of social media activations, including a Baby Bear takeover, teaser content across Instagram and TikTok, and a special Gogglebox partnership featuring the show’s stars reacting to the advert.
The supermarket is also releasing an exclusive cuddly bear toy, with 50p from every sale donated to Marie Curie.
Leo UK chief creative officer Andrew Long said: “Goldilocks and the Three Bears is a story generations know, but people experience stories very differently today.
“So we’ve built the campaign to work in different ways too: our Christmas TV spot tells the parents’ story, while our social takeover gives Baby Bear his own voice.”

items.title: Poundland blocked from buying new stock despite £86m turnaround
items.summary: Poundland has reportedly been blocked from ordering new stock ahead of the crucial Christmas trading period, despite an £86m improvement in its financial performance over the past year. The embattled company has been unable to pay suppliers for new products since 27 October after owner Gordon Brothers restricted its access to credit facilities and cash...
items.body:
Poundland has reportedly been blocked from ordering new stock ahead of the crucial Christmas trading period, despite an £86m improvement in its financial performance over the past year.
The embattled company has been unable to pay suppliers for new products since 27 October after owner Gordon Brothers restricted its access to credit facilities and cash generated through trading, according to ITV News.
The restrictions mean Poundland is continuing to sell its existing inventory, but cannot replenish its shelves, raising fresh concerns over its ability to continue trading.
As of 3 November, Poundland reportedly had around £25m in cash that management was unable to access, despite the balance continuing to grow through store sales.
Poundland boss Barry Williams revealed a dramatic improvement in the retailer’s financial performance in a message to staff on Friday.
According to the internal memo, seen by ITV News, Poundland swung from an EBITDA loss of £68.1m in the financial year to September 2025 to a profit of £18.1m in the year to September 2026.
The £86.2m turnaround comes as like-for-like sales continue to improve, with sales rising seven per cent in the first period of the new financial year.
Trading strengthened further during Halloween week, when like-for-like sales jumped 11.4 per cent year on year and exceeded budget by £1.5m.
Williams acknowledged that total sales remained below last year’s levels but attributed the decline to the closure of 115 stores as part of the retailer’s restructuring programme.
The figures have yet to be audited.
However, Gordon Brothers, which acquired Poundland from Pepco Group for £1 in June 2025, has maintained that the business remains financially vulnerable despite its improving performance.
In a letter to the government last week, Gordon Brothers’ UK operations boss Mark Newton-Jones warned that rising inflation, higher employment costs and shoplifting continued to put pressure on the company.
He said Poundland was still not generating cash at a sustainable level, despite its turnaround efforts.
Martin Property Group and Xyra Group Holdings are among the parties to have submitted proposals to acquire Poundland as a going concern.
Meanwhile, Tesco, B&M, Iceland, Poundstretcher, The Range and Lidl have all expressed interest in acquiring parts of the retailer’s store estate.
Martin Property Group has reportedly urged Gordon Brothers to release funding to allow Poundland to replenish stock and keep trading while rescue negotiations continue.
Poundland’s management has also held talks with the government, with Williams and chief financial officer Shaun Wills meeting business minister Kate Dearden last week.
Gordon Brothers is set to face scrutiny from MPs over its handling of the retailer’s financial difficulties, with the Business and Trade Committee due to hear evidence from company executives in private on Wednesday.
Poundland’s notice of intention to appoint administrators is due to expire on Thursday 12 November, leaving just days to secure a deal that could safeguard more than 10,000 jobs.

items.title: Police warn online bargain hunters are fuelling organised retail crime
items.summary: Police have warned that shoppers hunting for cut-price deals on resale platforms such as Vinted, eBay and Facebook Marketplace are inadvertently fuelling organised shoplifting gangs. Criminal networks are now regularly turning to online marketplaces to sell goods stolen from high street retailers. As such, shoppers have been urged to question heavily discounted products advertised as...
items.body:
Police have warned that shoppers hunting for cut-price deals on resale platforms such as Vinted, eBay and Facebook Marketplace are inadvertently fuelling organised shoplifting gangs.
Criminal networks are now regularly turning to online marketplaces to sell goods stolen from high street retailers. As such, shoppers have been urged to question heavily discounted products advertised as brand new.
National Business Crime Centre lead Superintendent Lisa Maslen told The Telegraph that organised gangs were ‘exploiting women and children’ to steal products from stores, before selling them through legitimate-looking online listings.
She warned that clothing advertised as ‘brand new with tags’ could be a particular red flag, especially when offered at prices significantly below their retail value.
“If it seems too good to be true and too good a price, then you know there’s something wrong. Trust your instincts,” Maslen said.
The police chief urged consumers to consider the wider consequences of buying potentially stolen goods, warning that demand was helping sustain criminal activity on Britain’s high streets.
Maslen is set to host a summit in January alongside Home Office officials and representatives from Vinted, Facebook Marketplace and Gumtree to tackle the growing use of online resale platforms by organised crime groups.
Research commissioned by the NBCC and backed by the Home Office, found that shoplifting remained profitable because criminals could quickly convert stolen stock into cash through online marketplaces, rogue businesses and other resale channels.
The report called for greater collaboration between police, retailers and online platforms to disrupt the networks handling stolen goods.
The British Independent Retailers Association has also urged marketplaces to take greater responsibility for preventing stolen products from being sold through their platforms.
Bira chief executive Andrew Goodacre previously warned that disrupting the markets making theft profitable was just as important as catching offenders.
Currently, more than 500,000 shoplifting offences are recorded annually across England and Wales.
Usdaw general secretary Joanne Thomas said shop theft had doubled since the pandemic, with offenders becoming increasingly brazen and organised.
Meanwhile, eBay insisted it prohibits the sale of stolen goods and uses technology to identify suspicious activity, alongside working with police to support investigations.

items.title: Swedish grocery retailers come together on food climate data as FoodFacts footprints 120,000+ products
items.summary: FoodFacts reports that it now delivers comparable carbon footprints for more than 120,000 food products every week to retailers ICA Sweden, Coop Sweden and Axfood, which together represent around 90% of the Swedish grocery market. The initiative addresses two key challenges: agreeing how food emissi
items.body:
FoodFacts reports that it now delivers comparable carbon footprints for more than 120,000 food products every week to retailers ICA Sweden, Coop Sweden and Axfood, which together represent around 90% of the Swedish grocery market.
The initiative addresses two key challenges: agreeing how food emissions should be calculated and having the technology to apply those calculations consistently at scale.
To establish a common approach, the Swedish Food Retailers’ Federation and the Swedish Food Federation commissioned the Swedish research institute RISE to develop an industry methodology for calculating food related carbon footprints, first published in 2023. In 2025, FoodFacts was selected to operationalise the methodology across the grocery assortment.
“For the first time, Swedish grocery retail has access to comparable carbon footprints across the food assortment, calculated according to a common methodology. This gives the industry a shared starting point to understand climate impact, prioritise action and strengthen climate reporting," says Jenny Hagberg, Head of Sustainability, Swedish Food Retailers’ Federation.
FoodFacts automates the calculation process by combining product information, including ingredients, packaging and geographical origin, with scientifically based life cycle data. This enables more than 120,000 product level footprints to be calculated and continuously updated, rather than relying on broad category averages. Two products in the same category can therefore have different footprints reflecting their individual composition and characteristics.
The current calculations primarily use secondary and representative life cycle data, enabling consistent coverage at scale. As more specific producer data becomes available, it can be incorporated within the same calculation, creating a pathway towards increasingly precise product footprints.
“Agreeing a common methodology is a major step, but applying it across more than 100,000 constantly changing products requires technology. FoodFacts turns that methodology into actionable climate data at scale, with the potential to incorporate increasingly specific producer data over time," says Alexandra Ferreira, CEO at FoodFacts.

items.body:
Veesion, which taps AI to help retailers detect gestures commonly linked to shoplifting, has appointed Wouter Ubbels as Vice President, Indirect and Mid-Market.
He will lead the company’s mid-market business and channel partnerships, supporting Veesion’s expansion in the US and internationally. Ubbels joins from Nedap Retail, where he spent nearly 14 years and most recently served as Vice President of Global Sales. His previous positions at Nedap included Director of Channel Sales Americas, with responsibility for partner relationships across North and Latin America.
“Retailers want partners they can trust, and Wouter has spent his career earning that trust on both sides of the Atlantic. We are thrilled to have him lead this next chapter of our growth with mid-market retailers and our partners,” says Veesion Co-founder and CEO Thibault David.
“Mid-market retailers and our partners are two of the biggest opportunities for Veesion. I’m here to make sure both get the attention, support and clarity they need to grow with us,” says Ubbels.
Veesion’s AI analyses video from the cameras a store already has. When it spots gestures commonly linked to shoplifting, it sends a short video alert to store teams. They then review the alerts and decide how to respond.

Alan Hoe is starting a new position as Head of Customer Experience & Operations at Marks and Spencer.
His CV includes a 21 year stint at Waitrose & Partners where he held a number of roles during that time, including Retail Proposition Lead - Front End and Services.
Most recently he has been working as a consultant for customer experience consultancy CLX.
It's Christmas!!!
M&S is bringing fashion, home, beauty and food together in one Christmas campaign for the first time since 2017.
The retailer's Home of Christmas offering launches on its Instagram page and YouTube channel at 7am today and stars James Norton as an undercover Santa, alongside Lucy Punch as Mrs. Claus, with a special appearance and exclusive soundtrack by Katherine Jenkins.
Beyond the film, an integrated campaign will run across TV, video on demand, cinema, outdoor, social media, radio, digital display and print, alongside M&S’s owned channels, influencer activity and PR.
Across social and digital channels, the Friends of M&S will share their festive selections through M&S Love That Lists, featuring gifts, food, fashion, beauty and homeware. Customers will also be able to access festive recipes through a hub and check ingredient and product availability through a digital catalogue, supporting meal planning and shopping list preparation.
Sharry Cramond, Fashion, Home & Beauty Marketing Director at M&S, says: "Customers don't think about Christmas as one meal, one gift or one outfit. They think about all the moments that make the season special. As the only retailer with a truly cross-category offer spanning Food, Fashion, Beauty, Gifting and Home, M&S plays a unique role in helping customers create Christmas from start to finish. Bringing those categories together allows us to tell one connected Christmas story and celebrate all the ways our customers make the season their own. That's why we're proud that customers call M&S The Home of Christmas."
Andrew Hicks, Food Marketing Director at M&S, says: "Christmas is made up of countless moments, traditions and rituals that mean something different to every family. For generations, M&S has been privileged to play a part in those celebrations, helping customers create a Christmas that feels uniquely their own."
"From the food shared around the table to the thoughtful finishing touches that make the season memorable, we're proud to be part of some of the moments that matter most. This year's campaign brings that to life in a way that is warm, unexpected and full of charm, celebrating the special place M&S holds in our customers' festive traditions and reinforcing why we're proud to be The Home of Christmas."

items.body:
Katherine Jenkins popped up at London's St. Pancras International on Friday to give people a live performance.

There's something so wonderful about surprising people and bringing a piece of Christmas magic to their day, and it certainly felt like a fitting time and place to do that.”

We’re thrilled Katherine has brought her extraordinary voice to the station for this special surprise performance, hot on the heels of the M&S Christmas advert, and we hope her performance under our tree has brought festive cheer to many."

items.title: M&S makes sure it's connected with Vusion partnership: last week’s biggest retail technology plays
items.summary: RTIH rounds up the stand out retail technology deals, launches, deployments and pilots from the past seven days. Including Just Eat, JD Sports, Moon Boot, Batteries Plus, Morrisons, Seed to Table, Coolshop, The Estée Lauder Companies, Ahold Delhaize USA, and Euronics International.Hyungji EliteHyung
items.body:
RTIH rounds up the stand out retail technology deals, launches, deployments and pilots from the past seven days. Including Just Eat, JD Sports, Moon Boot, Batteries Plus, Morrisons, Seed to Table, Coolshop, The Estée Lauder Companies, Ahold Delhaize USA, and Euronics International.
Hyungji Elite
Hyungji Elite, a South Korean apparel company and affiliate of Fashion Group Hyungji specialising in school uniforms, corporate workwear, and licensed sports merchandise, has introduced Beontag's RFID tags across its product management lifecycle.
The first step is 2027 season merchandise. Until now, inbound and outbound inspections and inventory audits relied on manual methods, where products are checked one by one. This takes time, and it inevitably leads to discrepancies between the physical stock on the shelf and the stock recorded in the system. Those gaps cost money, either as lost sales when products are not available or as excess inventory that ties up resources.
With RFID, tags attached to the products are read wirelessly, and many items can be identified at the same time, without scanning barcodes individually. For the teams at Hyungji Elite, this means inbound and outbound checks and inventory audits can be automated, with shorter inspection times and higher accuracy.
The 2027 season will launch RFID implementation with its first brand, covering four million pieces utilising Tricto M830 and ECO Hook M M830 tags. By identifying each item individually, Hyungji Elite says it will build product level data that tracks goods across production, logistics, and sales, laying the foundation for enhanced demand forecasting as well as precise production and inventory planning.
Just Eat
Just Eat has announced the launch of JETads, a new platform for European advertisers, with reach across 59 million active consumers, 592 million orders per year and more than 342,000 partners in 14 markets. It is live across all of them from today.
JETads builds on JET's personalisation technology, which analyses billions of interactions between consumers and partners across the platform. By understanding what each customer needs at a given moment, the system helps advertisers reach the right audience at the right time.
"We built JETads from scratch, for the AI era. The timing gave us the chance to ask what advertising should look like if you design it properly today, instead of copying what already works. The goals haven’t changed: helping advertisers reach the right audience with as little friction as possible, and bringing a more relevant offering to our customers. With the scale of JET and the AI of Prosus behind us, we can make partner investment genuinely efficient," says David Vismans, Chief Growth Officer at Just Eat.
Euronics International
Wayvia has announced a partnership with Euronics International focused on building a more connected digital shopping ecosystem for brands, Euronics’ retailers and the consumers they serve.
The partnership, powered by Wayvia’s Where to Buy technology, will enable brands to directly connect shoppers who discover products on their websites to more than 6,500 stores and online retailers across the Euronics network, which spans 36 markets in Europe and Asia.
“Euronics is one of the most trusted names in consumer electronics retail, and millions of customers rely on its members for the technology that's now central to all our lives,” says Anthony Ferry, Co-founder and CEO at Wayvia. “Through this partnership, we are helping to build the digital ecosystem that brands and Euronics retailers need to grow in an increasingly complex environment where consumer journeys are becoming ever more personalised.”
“The consumer electronics market is more competitive than ever, and today’s consumers expect and deserve a seamless journey from product discovery to purchase,” says John Olsen, CEO at Euronics International.
“Our partnership with Wayvia creates a stronger connection between brands, our members and consumers. Our retailers are a key part of brands’ go-to-market strategies, combining omnichannel capabilities with trusted advice, local expertise and a compelling in-store experience."
"By connecting brand websites with this retail network, we can make the consumer journey more seamless while supporting both our members and our suppliers. We have always believed that suppliers, retailers and technology partners achieve the most when they work together.”
JD Sports
Zebra Technologies says that it has helped JD Sports to achieve 98% on-shelf availability and 20% faster replenishment, so high demand sizes move from the storeroom to the shelf when and where customers want them.
JD Sports has nearly 5,000 stores across 46 countries. As the retailer scaled, inventory visibility in stores remained a challenge. To reliably offer one-hour Click & Collect or 30-minute delivery, the stock count needed to be accurate. It sought a real-time inventory visibility solution that could support omnichannel retail, was easy for retail assistants to use and fast to roll-out across stores.
A pilot across five stores highlighted the capabilities of Zebra’s TC2 Series mobile computers paired with RFD40 UHF RFID sleds to read tags faster and at greater range. JD Sports also selected Zebra OneCare which allows its store associates to address everyday wear and tear and accidental damage by simply swapping devices at no cost if something breaks.
Alongside Zebra, JD Sports worked with Renovotec, a Zebra partner who led the device deployment, and Checkpoint Systems, a Zebra eegistered ISV who integrated its ItemOptix software, giving a single view of inventory data across the retailer.
"What Zebra gives us is the ability to scale with trust,” says Daniel McGrath, Head of Customer Operations, JD Sports. “Things just land and work. Colleagues open a box, turn it on, and they are up and running. That lets our teams spend their time where it matters: with the customer.”
Moon Boot
ESW has announced a partnership with Tecnica Group to support the global e-commerce expansion of Moon Boot, its winter footwear and lifestyle brand.
ESW is providing Moon Boot with an end-to-end e-commerce solution spanning fulfilment, shipping and returns, merchant of record (MOR) services, localisation and B2B2C.
The partnership forms part of a wider transformation of Moon Boot’s e-commerce operations, including its migration from Salesforce Commerce to Shopify. Arsenalia is acting as systems integrator and leading the Shopify replatforming, working alongside Tecnica Group and ESW to integrate the new platform.
The model supports Moon Boot in key markets including the United States, combining international fulfilment and logistics with the cross-border infrastructure needed to serve customers in-market.
Andrea Antonioli, eCommerce Strategy & Operations Manager at Moon Boot says: “As we expand our international ecommerce operations, we need a model that can support the complexity of serving customers across different markets. ESW brings together the fulfilment, logistics and cross-border capabilities we need within one solution, while giving us the flexibility we need as the business grows. We are excited to get the partnership underway.”
OTAA
OTAA, a Melbourne-based menswear brand, is expanding its US fulfilment operation at Cart.com’s facility in Longview, Texas, which now ships most of its American orders.
OTAA began shipping from Longview in February, giving the company a domestic base in its largest market, which accounts for roughly half its business.
“The end of de minimis changes the economics of serving American customers and makes the decision about where to hold inventory much more consequential,” says Omair Tariq, Founder and CEO at Cart.com.
“Brands need a US operation sized to proven demand, with room to expand as the business grows. OTAA is doing that by bringing its bestsellers into our Longview facility and adding to the range in stages. We provide the facilities, software and operators to make that transition, so brands can invest in US inventory without having to build a fulfilment operation themselves.”
M&S
Vusion reports that Marks & Spencer will deploy its Connected Store platform to a number of new stores, with further roll-out potential in the future.
The deployment will support the retailer's focus on modernising store operations and improving the in-store experience for customers and colleagues.
Built on Bluetooth enabled infrastructure, Vusion's EdgeSense platform is designed to help connect store systems, product information and colleague activity more effectively across the shopfloor.
The initial deployment will focus on practical operational improvements, including managing product information more effectively, supporting colleagues in locating products more efficiently through location aware capabilities such as flashing labels, helping simplify in-store inventory processes and shopfloor execution, and creating a digital foundation that may support further store innovation over time.
Roy Horgan, CEO UK & Ireland at Vusion, says: “We are pleased to be working with M&S as it continues to invest in its store estate and colleague experience. Our Connected Store platform is designed to help retailers improve operational execution while providing the infrastructure to support future innovation.”
easyShop
easyShop.com, a new online marketplace from the company behind easyJet, has partnered with buy now, pay later provider, Clearpay.
The tie up comes as the number of UK shoppers planning to use BNPL for their Christmas shopping has risen over the last two years.
According to the IPA’s 2026 Christmas Consumer Report, 14% of consumers intend to use it this year, up from 9% in 2024. Among Millennials, the figure is 22%.
Cas Paton, Founder and CEO at OnCommerce, the platform powering easyShop, says: “Now that we're into November, Christmas shopping is in full swing. Between now and the big day, people will be picking up gifts here and there, taking advantage of good deals when they see them and gradually work through their lists."
"Clearpay lets them pay the same way, splitting the cost into smaller, interest-free payments. That’s what makes our partnership so strong; it’s a straightforward payment option that fits how people shop.”
Batteries Plus
Profitmind has announced the general availability of its AI powered Awase product matching solution. This identifies the same product across competing online catalogues without relying on a shared barcode or other product code.
The model has been running in production with Profitmind customers since April. “We have used Profitmind’s competitive matching since 2024. With Awase, about 11,000 of our products are now matched to roughly 75,000 competitor listings, up from about 2,000 matches before, giving us visibility into products that account for more than 95% of our consumer revenue,” says Peter Evans, CFO at Batteries Plus. “We use this information to inform when to adjust prices and by how much.”
Morrisons
Morrisons has partnered with Duvo.ai as it looks to identify opportunities to make greater use of AI across its existing systems.
Duvo was co-founded by Tomáš Čupr, who founded Rohlik Group, the European online grocer. It identifies and automates repetitive business tasks, freeing up team members to focus on decision-making, creativity, customer service and partner relationships.
The project will start by capturing how processes actually work across the UK grocery retailer's people, teams and systems. Duvo will then help it identify opportunities to simplify and redesign those processes, focusing where AI can create the most value, and highlighting a pathway for their swift adoption into everyday operations.
"Our business processes have evolved over decades and Duvo gives us a way to understand them in detail, and quickly," says Gordon MacPherson, Group Productivity Director at Morrisons.
"It means decisions about which repetitive everyday tasks to simplify, redesign and automate can be based on evidence rather than assumptions. That will give us a much clearer path from identifying AI opportunities to putting them into operation, freeing up our people to concentrate on high value work for the benefit of colleagues and customers."
Seed to Table
Seed to Table, a grocery retailer in Naples, Florida, has created Goldie, a conversational AI avatar who shoppers can talk to via a full size Proto Hologram screen.
“Seed To Table is a cutting-edge grocery store/entertainment Mecca like no other and adding Goldie to it just brings us to another level that no other supermarket has,” says Dan St. Martin, General Manager. "We are the Disney World of supermarkets.”
At the entrance, a seven-foot Proto Hologram presents information, advertising and Goldie, which has a face, voice and whimsical personality. Shoppers can ask Goldie questions, get recommendations and discover ideas. She can also remember preferences and previous interactions.
Throughout the store, participating brands use QR enabled shelf displays. Shoppers can scan to discover a brand story, learn about a product, receive an offer or recommendation, and explore content created specifically around what they’re seeing.
“Seed to Table deserves tremendous credit for having the vision to be first,” says James Beckmann, CEO at Live Buzz Intelligence. “They’re showing what is possible when a retailer modernises engagement at exactly the right moment. We’re excited to bring something genuinely new to shoppers.”
Ahold Delhaize USA
Ahold Delhaize USA is expanding its work with NCR Voyix as it looks to modernise key in-store capabilities across Point of Sale, self-checkout, pharmacy and fuel operations.
The multi-year roll-out is now underway, with new PoS technology now available in 100 stores and additional deployment planned over the next several years.
“As we advance our technology strategy, we’re focused on making it easier for customers to shop with our brands and easier for our brands’ associates to serve their customers,” says Ann Dozier, Chief Information Officer at Ahold Delhaize USA.
“Our goal is to create a more consistent technology foundation and a more connected experience, while maintaining the flexibility that allows each of our local brands to meet its customers’ needs in the short-term and positions us for the future. The roll-out is underway with new PoS technology now available in 100 stores, with the roll-out continuing over the next several years.”
The selection of the Voyix Commerce Platform builds on Ahold Delhaize USA’s relationship with NCR Voyix, whose technology has supported the company’s operations for a number of years.
Coolshop
Coolshop.com is expanding its warehouse automation strategy with Geek+ SkyCube, in a move that is pitched as Europe’s first project of its kind, delivered by the latter's partner STL.
A spokesperson for Geek+ says: "From shelf-to-person in 2023 to Geek+ SkyCube today, Coolshop shows what scalability looks like: automation that grows with the business, without starting over."
"Another milestone with STL, our exclusive Nordic partner, whose local expertise have been key from day one."
Further details on the project are set to be announced in the near future.
MishiPay and The Barcode Warehouse
MishiPay has announced a partnership with The Barcode Warehouse.
The tie up combines MishiPay’s suite of checkout solutions including self-checkout kiosks, hybrid kiosks, mobile PoS, scan and go and RFID enabled checkout with TBW’s expertise in end-to-end retail technology deployment, hardware, and support.
A MishiPay spokesperson says: "Because our platform integrates with retailers’ existing systems and infrastructure, it can go live in days rather than the 12–24 months a legacy PoS overhaul typically takes helping retailers modernise checkout without costly rip-and-replace projects."
MishiPay is deployed in more than 2,000 stores globally across grocery, convenience, fashion, travel retail and specialty retail, including Flying Tiger Copenhagen, MUJI in Europe, and Avolta, Carter’s, Event Network and MLSE in North America.
“This new partnership supports MishiPay’s strategy of working with trusted channel partners to bring frictionless checkout to more retailers, faster. Our cloud-based platform helps retailers manage rising customer expectations for convenience, store efficiency and digital transformation," says Mustafa Khanwala, Founder and CEO at MishiPay.
Retailers will be able to see the company's solutions in action at TBW’s Innovation & Customer Experience Centre (ICE) in the UK.
Lindt & Sprungli UK
Just Eat has announced a new partnership with Lindt & Sprungli UK to bring its chocolate range straight to customers’ doors in as little as 30 minutes. This makes it the brand's first delivery aggregator partner.
Customers can now order various Lindt's products from 26 locations across the UK. The brand's Pick & Mix offering is available with over 25 flavours available, including exclusives only sold from Lindt stores & Lindor flavours such as Shortbread, Pistachio, and Cherry Blossom Sakura.
From early next year, customers in eight locations will also gain exclusive delivery access to the Lindt Chocolate Bar through the Just Eat app, offering ‘Crema Gelata’ ice cream, hot chocolates and coffees.
A Just Eat spokesperson said: "The partnership marks another step in
expanding our gifting offer ahead of the festive season, so as we approach Christmas there’s no need to worry about securing those last minute presents."
The Estée Lauder Companies
The Estée Lauder Companies has announced a new partnership with Microsoft involving its cloud and data foundation and supporting the adoption of AI enabled capabilities across the business.
The tie up is a major part of The Estée Lauder Companies’ One Operating Ecosystem, which brings together shared platforms, connected data, and partners with the aim of enabling consistent, scalable, and effective execution across the enterprise.
A key initiative is harnessing the Microsoft platform to advance the company’s unified data platform. This foundation is the core enabler for AI and agility, connecting the company's data across brands, regions, channels, and functions to reduce duplication, enable reusable data products, and create more consistent access to data driven insights.
“As we continue to execute on Beauty Reimagined, we are building the future of consumer centricity, in our products, experiences, commerce, and more,” says Brian Franz, Chief Technology and Transformation Officer, The Estée Lauder Companies.
"Our partnership with Microsoft, in addition to the other strategic partners in our One Operating Ecosystem, is powering our teams with the capabilities to ultimately deliver more relevant, personalised experiences that meet consumers’ evolving needs. These enhanced capabilities will help us drive sustainable growth, improve productivity, and support margin expansion, creating capacity to reinvest into our enterprise to serve our consumers.”

items.body:
Check out our most clicked retail technology articles from last week, including Retention.com, M&S, Vusion, Duvo, Gophr, Screwfix, Focal Systems, PMC, Poq, VoCoVo, Deliverect, Enactor, SOLUM, Pricer, TCS, Toshiba Global Commerce Solutions, Vusion, Quorso, Datitude, and Sitoo.
Retention.com CEO and Co-founder Adam Robinson, wife, and children among victims in Florida plane crash
A Learjet 60 was bound for the Bahamas from Austin when it nosedived into a multi-lane highway on 1st November. The National Transportation Safety Board is investigating whether ice and turbulence contributed to the crash, and whether human error played a role.
E-commerce technology startup Retention.com CEO and Co-founder, Adam Robinson, his wife Helen Sharp and their two children, Emma, 4, and Charlie, 2, were all killed in the crash.
A company spokesperson said: "We are heartbroken by the loss of Adam, his wife Helen and their two young children. Adam was much more than our CEO. He was a friend, a mentor and a bold, outspoken leader who lived life to the fullest. He cared deeply about the people around him and brought energy and conviction to everything he built. His loss is deeply felt across our team and the tech community, as we collectively mourn this significant loss."
They continued: "Our hearts are with Adam and Helen’s family and loved ones, and with everyone affected by the crash. We ask that their privacy be respected during this difficult time. Our immediate focus at Retention.com is supporting our employees and Adam and Helen’s family. We are grateful for the kindness and support extended to them and our team."
Morrisons, Waitrose, and Dunelm take top honours at 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony in London
Focal Systems, PMC, Poq, VoCoVo, Deliverect, Enactor, SOLUM, Pricer, TCS, Toshiba Global Commerce Solutions, Vusion, Quorso, Datitude, and Sitoo were among the winners last week at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony.
We received a record number of entries this year, showcasing truly impressive innovation across both traditional and digital retail spaces.
To quote a member of our star studded judging panel: "Reviewing such inventive, high impact solutions has been a truly rewarding experience. The depth of engineering, scalable architecture, and strategic vision displayed throughout the submissions underscores the rapid transformation happening across modern retail technology."
Our 2026 hall of fame entrants were revealed during a sold out event which took place at The HAC in Central London and consisted of a drinks reception, three course meal, awards ceremony presided over by actor, comedian and writer Aurie Styla, and after party until 1am.
Congratulations to our 2026 winners, and a big thank you to our sponsors, judging panel, the legend that is Aurie Styla, and all those who attended our gathering.
Marks and Spencer taps Vusion EdgeSense platform amid retailer's store modernisation push
Vusion reports that Marks & Spencer will deploy its Connected Store platform to a number of new stores, with further roll-out potential in the future.
The deployment will support the retailer's focus on modernising store operations and improving the in-store experience for customers and colleagues.
Built on Bluetooth enabled infrastructure, Vusion's EdgeSense platform is designed to help connect store systems, product information and colleague activity more effectively across the shopfloor.
The initial deployment will focus on practical operational improvements, including managing product information more effectively, supporting colleagues in locating products more efficiently through location aware capabilities such as flashing labels, helping simplify in-store inventory processes and shopfloor execution, and creating a digital foundation that may support further store innovation over time.
Roy Horgan, CEO UK & Ireland at Vusion, says: “We are pleased to be working with M&S as it continues to invest in its store estate and colleague experience. Our Connected Store platform is designed to help retailers improve operational execution while providing the infrastructure to support future innovation.”
Morrisons partners with Duvo as UK grocery giant eyes opportunities for AI adoption
Morrisons has partnered with Duvo.ai as it looks to identify opportunities to make greater use of AI across its existing systems.
Duvo was co-founded by Tomáš Čupr, who founded Rohlik Group, the European online grocer. It identifies and automates repetitive business tasks, freeing up team members to focus on decision-making, creativity, customer service and partner relationships.
The project will start by capturing how processes actually work across the UK grocery retailer's people, teams and systems. Duvo will then help it identify opportunities to simplify and redesign those processes, focusing where AI can create the most value, and highlighting a pathway for their swift adoption into everyday operations.
"Our business processes have evolved over decades and Duvo gives us a way to understand them in detail, and quickly," says Gordon MacPherson, Group Productivity Director at Morrisons.
"It means decisions about which repetitive everyday tasks to simplify, redesign and automate can be based on evidence rather than assumptions. That will give us a much clearer path from identifying AI opportunities to putting them into operation, freeing up our people to concentrate on high value work for the benefit of colleagues and customers."
Gophr powered Screwfix Sprint on demand delivery service now available in 600 stores
Screwfix Convenience is designed to drive usage of Screwfix Sprint delivery, Click & Collect and check-In services among tradespeople and DIY customers.
And the Sprint service, which promises delivery within 60 minutes, is now live at 600 stores and counting.
In a LinkedIn post, Max Britten, Managing Director UK & Ireland at Screwfix, said: "We know how important convenience is for our busy trade customers. They want to stay on the job, avoid unnecessary downtime and get what they need, when they need it. Sprint helps them do exactly that, with tens of thousands of customers using it so far this year."
He added: "So making Sprint accessible to more customers is a real priority for Screwfix. With the additional stores, it now reaches more than 62% of the UK population. A huge thank you to all our colleagues and our delivery partner Gophr who have helped us reach this important milestone, and of course to our customers for continuing to use Sprint."
VoCoVo hires former Waterstones exec Emma Hillyard as CFO and former CBRE technology chief Paul Birkin as CTO
Retail communications specialist, VoCoVo, has announced the appointments of Emma Hillyard as Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and Paul Birkin as Chief Technology Officer (CTO).
Hillyard has worked across both the private and not for profit sectors, including retail, with previous CFO roles at Waterstones, Blackwells and Alzheimer’s Society.
She says: “VoCoVo has achieved strong growth already, and my role is to help make sure we navigate this next period and build on the growth already seen. For me, that means giving teams the insight and support they need to make informed decisions and creating the right environment for people to do their best work."
"I’ve always been very people centric and believe culture is critical to making meaningful change stick. That was a big part of what attracted me to VoCoVo. Its people and culture are a real superpower, and I’m excited to build on that.”
Birkin has held C-suite positions at CBRE, Experian, Capita, Logica and Cisco.
He says, “I’ve spent much of my career leading large scale transformations where technology can make a visible difference. That’s what makes VoCoVo so exciting - there’s already a strong technology foundation and a true ambition to keep innovating. As retail becomes increasingly intelligent, AI has the potential to create huge business value. My focus is on turning that potential into tangible value for our customers and pushing what the connected store can deliver.”
Vinted, eBay and Depop set to be hit by under-16s ban as grooming concerns grow
The UK government is set to ban under-16s from Vinted and eBay amid fears that the online platforms' messaging functions allow strangers to groom children.
Culture Secretary, Lisa Nandy, is gearing up to discuss expanding the social media ban announced earlier in the year to cover online marketplaces. Depop and Facebook Marketplace are also expected to be included.
The Children’s Society claims that some young users are being “asked for indecent photos in exchange for money” or gifts on these sites.
A government source told The Times: “There is an increasing body of evidence that says under-16s are accessing these services a lot and are potentially accessing risk. We need to take a comprehensive approach to protecting children from harm online."
Vinted, eBay, Depop, and Facebook Marketplace did not respond to our request for comment.
Drone delivery specialist Zipline bags $1.5 billion in funding at eye watering $21.5 billion valuation
Zipline has announced a $1.5 billion raise at a $21.5 billion post-money valuation, led by Paradigm, WCM Investment Management, and Layer Global with participation from Valor Equity Partners, Fidelity Management & Research Company, Uber, Tiger Global, J.P. Morgan, ARK Invest, and Salesforce Ventures.
It will use the capital to expand its US manufacturing facilities and ramp up hiring as it builds a drone delivery network across the country.
Walmart and Zipline are working together to launch 300 additional sites as part of a new national multi-year agreement with potential to grow further. Uber is targeting one million deliveries a day with Zipline by 2029.
“Zipline is now one of the largest autonomous robotics companies in the world - operating with scale, safety, and a magical user experience for consumers and merchants,” says Matt Huang, Co-Founder and Managing Partner at Paradigm. “It's no wonder that some of the largest merchants in the world are partnering with Zipline to use their delivery network.”
"Zipline has built a team and culture that has been developing cutting-edge drone delivery capabilities for over 10 years, and the market is now recognizing how transformational its technology is. Within e-commerce and food delivery, Zipline represents a generational improvement in user experience and delight,” says Alan Tu, Portfolio Manager at WCM Investment Management.
UK creators assemble! Amazon says it is coming to YouTube's Shopping affiliate programme
Amazon is joining YouTube's Shopping affiliate programme. Eligible UK creators will now be able to tag its products in their Shorts, long-form videos and livestreams.
A spokesperson for YouTube says: "Video has changed how we shop. In the past, we browsed store windows. Today we browse videos - from product reviews and unboxings to shopping hauls. Viewers spend an average of over 110 million hours daily watching shopping videos on YouTube. With YouTube Shopping, we’ve built the future of e-commerce directly into the video player."
YouTube creators can tag the products they are talking about in their videos, Shorts and livestreams, earning a commission anytime viewers buy something.
The spokesperson comments: "Viewers love the convenience. They don't have to search the description box of a video for a URL. When they click on a Shopping tag, they're taken to a verified site (like M&S, Currys, Boots and now Amazon) to buy the product. Creators love the affiliate Shopping programme because it allows them to maintain their authenticity while earning money off their content. And authenticity matters - according to a survey conducted by Kantar, surveyed viewers in the United States rank YouTube as the number one platform for helping them make more confident shopping decisions."
They add: "Shopping is a significant area of investment for YouTube, and we’ve seen incredible momentum. We’ve expanded the affiliate programme to more countries around the world, and recently expanded to the UK, Mexico and Argentina. There are now more than one million creators signed up for YouTube Shopping. YouTube Shopping GMV has grown 13X from Q1 2024 to Q1 2026. We’re also seeing tremendous momentum boosted by our investments in Gemini powered auto-tagging."
"In March 2026, we expanded access to the YouTube Shopping affiliate programme to all creators in the YouTube Partner Programme with at least 500 subscribers and who meet eligibility guidelines. By lowering this threshold, we’re unlocking earning potential earlier than ever."
Fake news: UK and US consumers are avoiding purchases over misleading online reviews fears
Research published by the Coalition for Trusted Reviews (CfTR), an alliance bringing together Amazon, Booking.com, Expedia Group, G2, Holidaycheck, Tripadvisor and Trustpilot, has revealed growing concerns around fake reviews and how they affect purchasing decisions.
The research is based on a survey of 6,000 people across the UK, Italy, and the US. While eight in ten consumers in the UK (85%), US (82%), and Italy (80%) use online reviews at least sometimes when considering a purchase, 74% of UK consumers, 73% of Americans and 61% of Italians have decided not to purchase a product or service due to concerns about fake or misleading reviews.
Although many online platforms invest heavily in fighting misuse, review fraud is becoming increasingly sophisticated. Bad actors - those who attempt to breach platform guidelines and mislead consumers and businesses via fake reviews - operate across platforms and jurisdictions, reusing identities, tactics and networks. This makes it challenging for any single platform or regulator to disrupt fraudulent activity.
Review and user verification is one of several methods online platforms may use to combat fake content. However, the research also highlights a tension between consumers' desire for authentic reviews and their willingness to accept additional verification measures. In the UK, 56% of consumers say that being required to provide ID would make them less likely to leave a review, alongside 46% in the US and 43% in Italy.
Becky Foley, Executive Committee member of Coalition for Trusted Reviews and VP, Head of Trust & Safety at TripAdvisor, says: “When reviews are fake or manipulated, the consequences go far beyond one misleading rating. Consumers risk making decisions based on information that isn’t genuine, while businesses that play by the rules face an uneven playing field. Over time, this undermines trust across the online marketplace.”

items.title: Oxford Street pedestrianisation brings ‘staggering’ shopping boost
items.summary: The pedestrianisation of Oxford Street has delivered a “staggering’ boost in footfall, data compiled by the London mayor’s office has shown, as Christmas shopping could usher in a larger surge in the number of shoppers.  Datasets gathered by City Hall suggest that spending and footfall soared in the first week of a traffic-free Oxford Street, [...]
items.body:
Oxford Street pedestrianisation brings ‘staggering’ shopping boost
The pedestrianisation of Oxford Street has delivered a “staggering’ boost in footfall, data compiled by the London mayor’s office has shown, as Christmas shopping could usher in a larger surge in the number of shoppers.
Datasets gathered by City Hall suggest that spending and footfall soared in the first week of a traffic-free Oxford Street, even as the mayor’s decision to close it to buses and cyclists divided Londoners.
According to City Hall, footfall between Orchard Street and Great Portland Street rose by 16 per cent compared to the October 2025 half-term while international visitor numbers were up by about 42 per cent.
Visits after 6pm also rose, with researchers arguing that data has far surpassed expectations. Data by the payments company Adyen also suggested that spending at stores down the traffic-free area of Oxford Street grew from £2.9m to £3.7m year-on-year, it was revealed last week.
Sir Sadiq Khan, the mayor of London, said the results were a “real boost for the nation’s high street”.
“These are staggering early results that show the transformational impact that the pedestrianisation of Oxford Street will have,” Khan said.
“With Christmas around the corner, I’d encourage Londoners and visitors to come and see what a traffic-free Oxford Street has to offer, whether you’re here to shop, meet friends or make an evening of it. The new Oxford Street is going to be one of the world’s most exciting public spaces, so come and be a part of this truly momentous project.”
Oxford Street change divides London
The decision to shut off Oxford Street has split Londoners, with cyclists and residents protesting against the mayor’s intervention.
The Marylebone Association, which is made up of locals living around the area, used public information to argue that bus journeys are taking up to 11 minutes longer following the pedestrianisation.
Hundreds of cyclists also staged a protest near Oxford Circus over a week ago.
Khan had pushed for a boost in shopping levels across Oxford Street for years, even as critics have complained about candy shops and other Harry Potter-style gift stores opening over the years. The mayor has argued that the pedestrianisation of the street would encourage “quality shops” to move in, adding that “decline is not inevitable”.

items.summary: The UK government is set to ban under-16s from Vinted and eBay amid fears that the online platforms' messaging functions allow strangers to groom children.Culture Secretary, Lisa Nandy, is gearing up to discuss expanding the social media ban announced earlier in the year to cover online marketplaces
items.body:
The UK government is set to ban under-16s from Vinted and eBay amid fears that the online platforms' messaging functions allow strangers to groom children.
Culture Secretary, Lisa Nandy, is gearing up to discuss expanding the social media ban announced earlier in the year to cover online marketplaces. Depop and Facebook Marketplace are also expected to be included.
The Children’s Society claims that some young users are being “asked for indecent photos in exchange for money” or gifts on these sites.
A government source told The Times: “There is an increasing body of evidence that says under-16s are accessing these services a lot and are potentially accessing risk. We need to take a comprehensive approach to protecting children from harm online."
Vinted, eBay, Depop, and Facebook Marketplace did not respond to our request for comment.
Public demand
The UK government ran a national consultation on a social media ban for under-16s from March to May 2026. It claims that the results showed overwhelming public demand for action, with nine in ten parents backing a ban, and two-thirds of young people agreeing under-16s should not be allowed to use at least some social media platforms.
The plan is to use the same model that is live in Australia. That country's model includes platforms like Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, Snapchat, Facebook and X. Messaging services like WhatsApp and Signal are not set to be included.
High risk features including livestreaming and strangers being able to contact children will also be restricted for under‑16s on other online services like gaming. This will be backed up by stronger requirements for age checks on platforms.
The first set of regulations will be laid out before the end of the year, and the changes should be implemented in spring 2027.

Pierce Brosnan channels his licence to thrill in Burberry's Christmas advert
Burberry’s newly-released Christmas ad stars actor Pierce Brosnan boogying with model Cara Delevigne - to the music of Sylvester’s 1982 hit Do Wanna Funk?
The scene is a boisterous family festive party in the panelled ballroom of a stately home.
Filmed at Longleat House, the home of the Marquess of Bath, it features an array of Burberry merch for adults, children - and dogs.
Clobber includes a £1,895 Kensington trench coat, a £1,925 Cotswolds handbag, a £1,395 Ambleside puffer jacket, assorted scarves in the ‘house check’ and the new blackwatch tartan design for £395.
Investors will be hoping to hear that these and other gift items from the iconic British brand are flying off the shelves when Burberry chief executive Joshua Schulman announces results on Thursday.
Sales at the FTSE 100 company are expected to have risen by 3 per cent to just over £1.1billion in the half-year to September while operating profits jumped to £44million from £19million.
Since taking on the top job in July 2024, Schulman has embarked on a turnaround of the beleaguered business which had been hit by the consumer slowdown in China, its most important market where it has 65 stores.
The company has also been wooing back younger aspirational shoppers who had been put off by exorbitant price tags for bags, beanie hats and other accessories - essential entry-level products for securing long-term loyalty to a luxury label.
An emphasis on ‘Britishness’ has been a key tactic in Schulman’s approach in what is a tough luxury goods sector.
Some observers believe that spending will never return to its buoyant post-pandemic levels when shoppers indulged in ‘revenge buying’ after lockdowns.
Watching the latest update with intent will be Mike Ashley.
The maverick entrepreneur now has a 6 per cent stake in the 170-year old company through his Frasers empire which also encompasses Sports Direct, a holding in British bag maker Mulberry, the Harvey Nichols stores - and his Flannels shops, a Burberry stockist.
Schulman will doubtless be quizzed on any conversations with Ashley – and on the price of Burberry shares. When he joined the company, they traded at £7.40p, compared to £11.22.
But that’s still way below their post-pandemic peak.
The question is: does Ashley aspire to add Burberry to the ‘luxury eco-system’ which he is building?
Or is he happy to be merely a bystander, having recently reduced his slice of the company?

items.title: Trump may have lost but don’t bet Democrats can fix the economy
items.summary: There’s not much they can do over the next couple of years to alleviate angry voters’ stress over prices It was the economy, again. Although Donald Trump largely ignored it, voters’ acute concerns over the rising cost of living fuelled a political upheaval for the ages that is likely to deliver the biggest swing toward Democrats since Watergate, granting them the largest House majority in nearly four decades alongside their biggest edge in the Senate since 2008. Still, having come to power promising to restore affordability, the new crop of Democrats are soon to discover that there is not much they can do over the next couple of years to alleviate angry voters’ stress over pricey gas and groceries, exorbitant mortgages and unaffordable healthcare. Eduardo Porter is a journalist focused on economics and politics. He writes the newsletter Being There on Substack Continue reading...
items.body:
It was the economy, again. Although Donald Trump largely ignored it, voters’ acute concerns over the rising cost of living fuelled a political upheaval for the ages that is likely to deliver the biggest swing toward Democrats since Watergate, granting them the largest House majority in nearly four decades alongside their biggest edge in the Senate since 2008.
Still, having come to power promising to restore affordability, the new crop of Democrats are soon to discover that there is not much they can do over the next couple of years to alleviate angry voters’ stress over pricey gas and groceries, exorbitant mortgages and unaffordable healthcare.
Democrats would do well to recall that the affordability strains that helped deliver them to power are not dissimilar to those that delivered the presidency to Trump two years ago. And they could again quickly become their enemy.
“First, Americans want Washington to bring down the cost of living,” said Chuck Schumer, Senate majority leader-in-waiting. Likely House speaker Hakeem Jeffries added that “we’ve promised to fight for an affordable America, and that’s exactly what we will do”. They will soon discover the limits to their power to undo Trump’s economic blunders and steer an economy that is largely driven by forces outside their control.
Take gas prices, the single most powerful motivation for voters’ rebellion against the Republicans enabling Trump’s policy choices. Reining them in will require reaching an understanding with Iran that reopens the strait of Hormuz. Schumer thinks Democrats can achieve that. “We are going to end the war,” he said.
Trump may disagree, however. And while it is true that Congress is legally entitled to end wars – it is the only branch of government entitled to start one – it is unclear what such legal niceties might mean in practice. Republicans have controlled Congress since Trump went to war. Still, he has pursued it without asking for their approval. Democrats could now try to cut war funding, but they do not have the requisite 60 Senate votes to prevent a filibuster.
Trump’s trade war has similar characteristics. When the supreme court struck down Trump’s “national security” tariffs because they exceeded presidential authority, the administration reimposed many of them under a different statute, deploying a new, also spurious rationale. There is also little that Democrats can do to stop Trump’s war on immigration. It is fully funded and can carry on unimpeded, further disrupting construction and other immigrant-reliant industries.
Even the low-hanging fruit hangs rather high. While it may seem easy to reinstate federal subsidies for health insurance programs under the Affordable Care Act, or undo or postpone cuts to Medicaid and food stamps in Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act, Democrats will be hard-pressed to find the money, given a budget deficit that is already running at a whopping 6% of the nation’s gross domestic product.
Just preventing further damage will be an uphill battle. A lame duck Trump who no longer feels the need to please voters is likely to give free rein to his most destructive urges. While Democrats will be able to block Trump’s new legislative proposals, they don’t have the votes to overcome presidential vetoes.
Optimists may believe that after Tuesday’s shellacking, sufficient Republicans in Congress could be convinced to buck their president’s wishes. But most of those who survived the bloodbath come from the most faithful Maga districts and states and are the least likely to abandon their leader.
The economy itself – driven almost exclusively by a frenzied artificial intelligence investment boom – is unlikely to help Democrats achieve their goal of easing voters’ economic strains.
Wall Street is already doubting that the massive investments to build data-processing centers to train powerful AI models will pay off in time to justify the money. The tech-heavy Nasdaq stock index has fallen by more than 10% in the last month.
Goldman Sachs estimates that the large AI hyperscalers have raised almost $200bn in bond markets so far this year, almost twice as much as in all of 2025. Altogether, the bank added, AI-related firms have raised nearly $500bn in debt so far in 2026.
Were this bubble to pop and the funding to stop, it would likely deliver an economic downfall to beat even the Great Recession sparked by the housing bubble in 2008. When the time comes, a government hamstrung by $40tn in debt and interest rates hovering near 20-year highs will have little fiscal space to soften the blow.
Can voters’ newfound love for Democrats survive the likely turbulence ahead? Justin Wolfers, an economist at the University of Michigan who runs Platypus Economics, observes that neither the unemployment rate nor inflation are bad enough to justify Americans’ extreme pessimism about the economy. So what’s driving the sour mood? A collapse in confidence in economic leadership.
Tuesday’s Republican bloodbath might, on its own, improve Americans’ spirits. Limited though their powers may be, Democrats will at least offer some resistance to Trump’s most destructive impulses. But the economy will likely pose a greater challenge for the new Democratic Congress than it has to the Republicans currently in charge. In two years’ time, Democrats might be facing anger over an economic scenario that has gotten palpably worse.
They might then come to embrace the limits of their power and hope voters blame the president – not Congress – for their economic unhappiness.
- Eduardo Porter is a journalist focused on economics and politics. He writes the newsletter Being There on Substack
